playbooks.name: Retail Chains
playbooks.one_liner: A multi-branch FMCG grocery/supermarket retail chain (3-30 stores) running on a centralised POS and warehouse, buying from distributors/wholesalers and selling everyday-essentials to walk-in households across Tier-1/2/3 India on thin margins and high stock velocity.

operating_model.summary: A retail chain is a volume game on borrowed shelf-space economics: buy assortment from FMCG distributors/super-stockists (or direct company billing at scale), move it through a central or cluster warehouse to multiple stores, and convert footfall into baskets via a POS. Profit comes not from per-item margin (which is wafer-thin on staples) but from inventory velocity, supplier trade-margin + schemes, private-label mix, and operating leverage across stores. Cash conversion is favourable (sell-for-cash, pay-supplier-on-credit) which funds expansion if discipline holds.
revenue_streams: Front-end retail sale of FMCG/staples/fresh at MRP-anchored shelf price (core, ~75-85% of revenue)
Supplier-funded income: trade margin, slotting/listing fees, volume & QPS schemes, visibility/end-cap charges, expiry/damage claims
Private-label / loyalty-brand SKUs at 2-3x category margin
General merchandise, home & kitchen, apparel basics (higher-margin non-food)
Ancillary: bill-payment/BBPS, recharge, ATM/aggregator commissions, in-store ad/brand activation, store-front rental of FMCG branded coolers
cost_structure: Cost of goods sold (~80-88% of revenue) — the dominant line
Rent & CAM (5-10% of sales in Tier-1 high-street; lower in Tier-2/3)
Store payroll + central staff (4-7% of sales)
Shrinkage/wastage/expiry (1-3%, higher with fresh/dairy)
Power, cold-chain, refrigeration, DG (1-2%)
Logistics/last-mile from warehouse to stores, packing, POS/software/MDR fees
value_drivers: Inventory turns and fill-rate (every extra turn directly lifts ROCE)
Same-store sales growth (SSSG) and basket size/cross-sell
Supplier terms — credit days, scheme realisation, and direct-vs-distributor sourcing margin
Private-label penetration and category mix toward higher-margin non-food
Store-cluster density (warehouse + brand leverage across nearby stores)

value_chain: Assortment & category planning (SKU range, planogram, private-label)
Sourcing & procurement (distributor/super-stockist/direct company billing + scheme negotiation)
Inbound logistics & central/cluster warehousing (GRN, putaway, batch/expiry)
Replenishment & store distribution (auto-indent, route planning, store receiving)
POS checkout, billing & payment (GST-compliant, loyalty capture)

core_processes.description: POS sell-through and min-max reorder levels per SKU per store trigger daily/weekly indents to the warehouse, which raises POs to suppliers; goal is high fill-rate with low days-of-stock and zero stockouts on A-class fast-movers.
Inbound goods checked against PO and invoice at warehouse/store: quantity, batch, MRP, expiry, and rate-vs-scheme; mismatches blocked before payment to plug margin leakage and protect ITC.
Barcode scan -> GST-rated invoice -> UPI/card/cash tender -> end-of-day cash drawer, MDR and UPI settlement reconciliation per store, with exception flags for voids/discounts/manual price overrides.
FEFO rotation, near-expiry markdown/return windows, cycle counts and CCTV-linked audits to keep wastage and pilferage inside 1-3% of sales.
Plan offers, encode at POS, then claim back supplier scheme/visibility money and reconcile actual realisation vs accrued to protect the real (post-scheme) gross margin.

department_structure.mandate: Run the floor: footfall conversion, planogram & availability, billing, cash, hygiene, staff rosters and customer experience across all branches.
Decide assortment, pricing, planogram and private-label; negotiate supplier terms, margins and schemes; manage the buying calendar.
Own inbound, warehousing, replenishment, route planning and store distribution; maintain fill-rate, batch/expiry and cold chain.
Cash & bank reconciliation across stores, supplier payables, scheme/claim accounting, GST/ITC, margin and shrinkage MIS, working-capital control.
Drive footfall and basket size via local catchment marketing, loyalty programme, promotions and (where present) omni-channel/quick-commerce.
Hire and roster high-churn store staff, payroll, Shops & Establishment / labour compliance, training and statutory benefits.

operational_bottlenecks.bottleneck: Stockouts on fast-movers alongside dead stock on slow-movers
operational_bottlenecks.symptom: A-class staples (atta, oil, milk) out of stock at peak hours while shelves and warehouse choke with slow SKUs nearing expiry
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Lost sales 5-10% + walk-outs to competitor/kirana; capital trapped in dead stock; expiry write-offs eat the thin margin
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Reorder levels set on gut feel not POS velocity, no SKU-level ABC/FEFO discipline, and indents not auto-driven by sell-through across branches

operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Physical stock < book stock at cycle count; near-expiry dump; unexplained cash short at EOD; frequent manual price overrides/voids at POS
operational_bottlenecks.impact: 1-3%+ of sales lost — often larger than net profit; ITC and supplier-claim disputes
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Weak FEFO rotation, no exception monitoring on POS discounts/voids/cash, multi-store cash handling with poor reconciliation, and pilferage at warehouse-to-store handoff

operational_bottlenecks.bottleneck: Margin erosion from un-realised supplier schemes and rate mismatches
operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Booked gross margin looks fine but actual post-scheme margin is lower; large unreconciled 'claims receivable' from distributors
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Real gross margin 1-3 points below plan; cash stuck in unclaimed schemes for months, straining working capital
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Scheme terms tracked on WhatsApp/Excel, no 3-way match of PO-invoice-scheme, and no systematic claim filing/follow-up with distributors

operational_bottlenecks.bottleneck: Inconsistent execution and high attrition across branches
operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Same chain, different store: stockouts, untidy planograms, billing errors, rude service; constant cashier/floor-staff churn
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Erratic SSSG, customer trust erosion, training cost spiral, owner firefighting per-store instead of scaling
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Tribal-knowledge operations with no enforced SOPs/checklists, low-paid high-churn staff, and weak per-store performance visibility for the owner

operational_bottlenecks.bottleneck: Working-capital and cash-cycle strain during expansion
operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Sales growing but bank balance not; supplier credit days squeezed; new store ramps slower than projected
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Over-leverage, delayed supplier payments (risking schemes & Sec 43B(h)), stalled expansion
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Each new store front-loads inventory + deposit + fit-out before it breaks even, and free supplier credit gets consumed by inventory pile-up rather than funding growth

ai_automation_opportunities.opportunity: AI demand-forecasting and auto-replenishment per SKU per store using POS velocity, seasonality and local festival calendar to set dynamic min-max and cut both stockouts and dead stock
Automated 3-way match (PO vs supplier invoice vs scheme) plus a scheme/claim tracker that flags rate mismatches and chases unrealised distributor claims to protect true gross margin
POS exception analytics: AI flags abnormal voids, discounts, manual price overrides, cash-short patterns and shrinkage hotspots per store/cashier for loss prevention
Auto GST reconciliation across multi-store invoices and e-invoicing, matching GSTR-2B for full ITC capture and on-time multi-GSTIN filing
Standardised, enforceable store SOPs and daily checklists (opening, FEFO, planogram, EOD cash) to drive consistent execution across branches
Loyalty/CRM basket-analysis and targeted offers: AI segments customers, recommends cross-sell and personalised promotions to lift basket size and SSSG
Multi-store cash-flow and working-capital cockpit projecting store-level break-even, supplier-credit utilisation and expansion affordability

consulting_frameworks.use: Map DIO + DSO - DPO; retail's edge is near-zero DSO (cash sales) and supplier credit, so the lever is squeezing days-of-inventory and protecting supplier credit days to self-fund stores.
Identify the binding constraint (usually warehouse replenishment throughput or shelf availability) and subordinate everything to keeping A-class SKUs in stock at peak footfall.
Classify SKUs by sales value (ABC) and demand variability (XYZ) to set differentiated reorder/safety-stock policy; enforce FEFO on perishables to cut expiry.
Build a per-store P&L (gross margin - rent - payroll - shrink - power) to know each branch's contribution and break-even month before approving the next store.
Separate growth from new-store-adds vs genuine maturation; the real health signal for a chain and the basis for footfall/basket diagnosis.
Clarify ownership across central buying vs store ops (e.g., who owns pricing, planogram, claims) to stop the owner being the single point of every decision as branches multiply.

risk_model.risk: Inventory shrinkage, pilferage and expiry write-offs exceeding net margin
risk_model.control: FEFO discipline, periodic cycle counts vs book stock, CCTV-linked loss prevention, POS exception monitoring on voids/discounts, and dual cash-handling controls per store

risk_model.risk: GST/ITC leakage and non-compliance across multiple store GSTINs (mis-rated SKUs, GSTR-2B mismatch, e-invoicing thresholds)
risk_model.control: Centralised POS with correct HSN/GST-rate master, monthly GSTR-2B reconciliation for full ITC, e-invoice where turnover crosses threshold, and on-time multi-GSTIN filing

risk_model.risk: Delayed payment to MSME suppliers triggering Sec 43B(h) disallowance and loss of trade schemes
risk_model.control: Track MSME-classified vendors, pay registered micro/small suppliers within 45 days, and reconcile schemes/claims before withholding payment

risk_model.risk: Working-capital crunch from over-expansion / inventory pile-up
risk_model.control: Per-store break-even gating before new launches, days-of-inventory caps, RBI MSME working-capital/CC limits sized to inventory cycle, and cash-flow forecasting

risk_model.risk: Food safety / FSSAI non-compliance on packaged & fresh food (labelling, storage, expiry, licence)
risk_model.control: Valid FSSAI licence per premises, cold-chain temperature logs, FEFO and expiry-removal SOPs, and supplier FSSAI verification

risk_model.risk: Labour / Shops & Establishment and statutory (PF/ESI/PT) non-compliance with high-churn store staff
risk_model.control: Shops & Establishment registration per store, EPF/ESI enrolment, professional tax, and payroll-system-driven statutory deduction & filing

kpi_structure.definition: COGS / average inventory at cost, annualised, chain-wide
Real margin after supplier schemes/claims and markdowns, % of net sales
Value of stock lost to pilferage, damage and expiry as % of sales
Like-for-like sales growth of stores open >12 months, YoY
% of indented SKUs available on shelf at peak, esp. A-class fast-movers
Net sales / number of bills, per store

unit_economics: A mid-size supermarket (~2,500 sq ft, Tier-2): monthly sales ₹40-70 lakh, gross margin ~18% = ₹7-12 lakh, less rent ₹1.5-3 lakh + payroll ₹2-3.5 lakh + shrink/power/other ~₹2 lakh, net ~₹1.5-3 lakh/month at maturity
Per-store fit-out + opening inventory + deposit: ₹40 lakh-₹1.2 crore depending on size/city; break-even typically month 8-18
Average basket ₹300-700; ~80-120 bills/day/store at ramp, 200-400 at maturity; sales/sq ft target ₹2,000-4,000/month
profitability_analysis.working_capital_notes: Structurally favourable: cash/UPI sales (near-zero DSO) + 15-45 days supplier credit can fund inventory if turns stay high. The trap is inventory pile-up and unclaimed supplier schemes consuming the credit float — keep days-of-inventory low and chase claims. Each new store front-loads ₹10-40 lakh of working capital before contribution turns positive.
levers: Lift inventory turns (faster replenishment, kill dead stock) to raise ROCE without margin change
Grow private-label & high-margin non-food mix from <5% toward 10-15% of sales
Fully realise supplier schemes/visibility income and tighten 3-way match to protect post-scheme margin
Cut shrinkage below 1.5% via FEFO + loss-prevention — drops almost entirely to net profit
Negotiate direct company billing at scale to capture distributor margin

pm_workflows.cadence: Per expansion; 60-90 day project with weekly steering review
milestones: Licences (Shops & Estab, FSSAI, trade) + GSTIN for premises
Fit-out, racking, cold-chain, POS & network install
Opening assortment & planogram + initial inventory load
Soft launch -> grand opening with catchment marketing

pm_workflows.cadence: One-time 3-4 month program, then quarterly optimisation
milestones: Central server + per-store POS + barcode/weighing integration
GST e-invoicing & GSTR-2B reconciliation wired in
Identify high-volume categories for private label
Track private-label penetration % and margin uplift vs target

stages.focus: Prove a repeatable, profitable store model and centralise buying for scale leverage
plays: Lock per-store unit economics and break-even before adding the next
Move from over-the-counter to a real POS + inventory system with clean SKU/GST master
Centralise buying across stores to win better distributor terms and schemes
Codify opening/FEFO/EOD-cash SOPs so a second store runs without the owner on-floor

stages.focus: Build the central warehouse + replenishment engine and professionalise category & finance
plays: Stand up a central/cluster warehouse with auto-indent replenishment and fill-rate targets
Hire category managers; negotiate direct company billing where volume permits
Launch loyalty/CRM to drive SSSG and basket size
Introduce private label in top categories; install loss-prevention and per-store MIS

stages.focus: Operating leverage, omni-channel reach and data-driven category management
plays: AI demand-forecasting and dynamic replenishment chain-wide
Add quick-commerce / WhatsApp ordering / home delivery from store dark-aisles
Deepen private-label and high-margin non-food to lift blended margin
Tighten working capital and explore RBI MSME / NBFC credit lines sized to inventory cycle for funded expansion

digital_maturity_model.name: Manual / paper counter
signals: Handwritten/khata billing or basic calculator
Stock 'in the owner's head', no SKU master
No GST-correct invoicing, schemes tracked on paper/WhatsApp
Per-store cash with no central reconciliation
digital_maturity_model.next_step: Install a barcode POS with a clean SKU/HSN/GST/MRP master and GST-compliant billing

digital_maturity_model.name: Basic POS, siloed stores
signals: POS billing live per store but data not consolidated
Inventory tracked in Excel, manual reorder
GST filed but ITC not reconciled to GSTR-2B
Owner pulls each store's numbers manually
digital_maturity_model.next_step: Centralise multi-store data and connect a warehouse/inventory module with reorder levels

digital_maturity_model.name: Integrated retail ERP
signals: Centralised POS + inventory + purchase across all stores
Reorder levels and GRN/3-way match in place
Consolidated MIS, batch/expiry tracking, scheme accrual
GSTR-2B reconciliation and e-invoicing where applicable
digital_maturity_model.next_step: Add loyalty/CRM, exception/loss-prevention analytics and demand-based replenishment

digital_maturity_model.name: Data-driven & omni-channel
signals: Loyalty/CRM with basket and customer analytics
POS exception dashboards for shrinkage/voids
Auto-replenishment from sell-through; private-label managed by data
Online/quick-commerce/WhatsApp ordering integrated to stock
digital_maturity_model.next_step: Layer AI forecasting and prescriptive decisioning across pricing, replenishment and loss prevention

digital_maturity_model.name: AI-native retail
signals: AI demand-forecasting per SKU/store with festival/weather signals driving dynamic min-max
Automated 3-way match + scheme/claim chasing and margin protection
AI loss-prevention flagging shrinkage hotspots in near-real-time
Personalised offers, dynamic pricing and predictive working-capital cockpit for the owner
digital_maturity_model.next_step: Continuously expand autonomous decisioning while keeping human oversight on pricing, vendor and expansion calls

playbooks.name: Wholesale Distribution
playbooks.one_liner: An Indian wholesale distribution MSME (distributor/stockist/C&F) that buys principal-company stock on credit/advance and redistributes it across a defined territory through field beats and secondary sales to retailers, earning a thin trade margin on high volume velocity.

operating_model.summary: Margin-on-volume intermediation. The firm appoints itself (or is appointed) as distributor/super-stockist/C&F for one or more principal companies (FMCG, pharma, electrical, agro, building material), invests working capital in inventory + retailer credit, and converts it through a salesforce running daily beats. Profit = trade margin + scheme/QPS incentives - financing cost - distribution opex. C&F differs: it is asset-light commission/logistics on principal-owned stock (no inventory ownership), while distributor/stockist owns inventory and carries the credit risk.
revenue_streams: Primary trade margin on principal MRP/PTR (typically 4-10% FMCG, 8-20% pharma/electrical, 2-4% commodity)
Secondary sales to retailers/sub-stockists across the beat (volume velocity is the real engine)
Quarterly/annual performance schemes, QPS, slabs, display & visibility incentives from principals
C&F / super-stockist commission (1.5-4% of throughput on principal-owned stock, asset-light)
Cash-discount and prompt-payment incentives captured on early principal payments
Logistics/last-mile and breakage/expiry claim recoveries
cost_structure: Cost of goods (90-96% of revenue — the dominant line)
Working-capital financing: CC/OD interest at 10-16% on inventory + retailer receivables
Field salesforce + DSE/PSR salaries, incentives, travel (beat cost)
Godown rent, racking, cold-chain (pharma/food), insurance, shrinkage/expiry/breakage
Delivery fleet/3PL, fuel, vehicle maintenance
GST compliance, ERP/DMS software, accounting, audit
value_drivers: Inventory turns (stock velocity) — the single biggest lever on ROCE
Beat productivity: lines per call, drop size, range selling, ECO/TLSD
Working-capital cycle: receivable days vs payable days vs stock days
Width & depth of distribution (numeric + weighted reach) and principal relationship strength
Claim hygiene — fast, complete recovery of scheme/expiry/damage claims from principals

value_chain: Demand forecasting & primary order placement (purchase from principal)
Inbound GRN, batch/expiry capture & godown stocking
Field secondary sales (order capture via DSE/SFA on the beat)
Returns/expiry/damage handling & claim filing to principal

core_processes.description: PSR captures retailer order on SFA app on the beat -> auto credit-limit/outstanding check -> pick-pack at godown -> GST-compliant invoice + e-way bill -> deliver -> collect cash/UPI/credit -> reconcile against retailer ledger and aging.

Forecast + norm-stock driven indent to principal -> PO -> inbound truck GRN with batch & expiry -> 3-way match (PO/GRN/invoice) -> capture landed cost -> pay principal within credit terms to bag cash discount.

Territory split into daily beats; permanent journey plan assigns outlets/day to each PSR; productivity tracked as outlets billed/total visited, lines per bill, value per bill; route optimised for coverage and frequency.

Track every principal scheme (QPS, display, damage, near-expiry, price-protection) -> file claim with proof -> follow up -> reconcile credit notes -> close. Leakage here directly erodes the thin net margin.
FEFO/FIFO picking, ABC-XYZ stock norms, near-expiry alerts, periodic cycle counts, returns segregation (saleable vs damaged), shrinkage reconciliation.

department_structure.mandate: Drive secondary sales: beat coverage, retailer reach, range selling, scheme execution and collection on the route.
Receive, store (FEFO/FIFO, cold-chain where needed), pick, pack and deliver accurately while controlling shrinkage, expiry and breakage.
Manage working capital, retailer credit & collections, principal payments, GST compliance and claim recovery.
Forecast demand, place primary orders, maintain norm stocks, negotiate schemes and own the principal relationship/ROI conversation.
In most Indian distributorships the proprietor personally runs strategy, banking, principal negotiation and people; admin handles HR, statutory, IT/DMS.

operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Cash perpetually tight; CC/OD limit maxed; can't fund new SKUs or principals despite growing topline.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: ROCE collapses; growth self-limited; forced to skip cash-discount and scheme buying.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Retailer receivable days (25-45) exceed principal payable days (7-21) while stock sits 20-40 days; the firm finances the entire chain on a thin margin.

operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Principal credit notes always short of filed claims; large unreconciled 'claims receivable' balance ages 90+ days.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Directly erodes the 1-3% net margin — often the difference between profit and loss on a principal.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Manual claim tracking on Excel, missing proof of execution, no SKU-level scheme master, weak follow-up discipline with principal.

operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Near-expiry stock found at cycle count; non-saleable returns pile up; slow-movers block godown space and cash.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Write-offs hit margin; partial/late principal reimbursement; cash locked in unsaleable inventory.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: No FEFO discipline, poor forecasting causing over-indent of slow SKUs, and delayed/incomplete expiry-claim filing.

operational_bottlenecks.symptom: High 'visited but not billed' (low ECO), low lines-per-bill, reps pushing only fast-movers and top schemes.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Under-utilised salesforce cost; weak weighted distribution; principal threatens territory split.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: No SFA-enforced PJP, no range-selling targets, incentive design rewards value not productivity/range, and no daily call analysis.

operational_bottlenecks.symptom: 60-80% of throughput from one principal who can cut territory, change ROI, or appoint a parallel distributor.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Existential — a single appointment letter change can wipe out the business overnight.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Over-concentration on one principal, no portfolio diversification, and a weak negotiating position on ROI/credit terms.

operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Order books, hand-written invoices, ledgers in registers; no real-time stock or outstanding visibility.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Billing errors, GST/e-way mismatches, stock-outs of fast-movers, and owner-dependent decision-making.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: No DMS/SFA adoption; perception that distribution software is costly and field staff resist app usage.

ai_automation_opportunities.opportunity: AI demand forecasting + auto-indent: predict SKU-level secondary offtake from beat history, seasonality and scheme calendar to set norm stocks and generate primary orders — cutting both stock-outs and over-indent of slow movers.
Automated claim & scheme reconciliation: parse principal scheme circulars, match filed claims to credit notes at SKU/scheme level, and flag the aging shortfall to recover leaked margin.
Working-capital and ROI cockpit: live distributor ROI, receivable/payable/stock days, cash-discount-vs-financing-cost trade-off and CC/OD utilisation alerts for the owner.
Smart beat optimisation & PSR coaching: optimise PJP routes, predict drop size, and nudge reps with next-best-SKU / range-selling suggestions to lift ECO and lines-per-bill.
e-Invoice + e-way bill auto-generation and GST reconciliation (GSTR-1/2B/3B) against the DMS to eliminate mismatch notices and ITC loss.
AI credit-risk scoring for retailers: score each outlet on payment history, set dynamic credit limits, and auto-block over-limit billing on the SFA app to cut bad debt.
FEFO/near-expiry alerting and dead-stock liquidation engine that recommends transfers, push-schemes or returns before write-off.
DMS/SFA selection & roll-out advisory tailored to distribution (Bizom/FieldAssist/SAP-B1/Tally-DMS) with data-migration and adoption playbook.

consulting_frameworks.use: Quantify DSO (retailer receivable days) + DIO (stock days) - DPO (principal payable days) to expose how many days of cash are locked, then attack each leg — the core financial diagnostic for any distributor.
Identify the binding constraint (almost always working capital or godown throughput) and subordinate decisions to it before adding SKUs/principals/headcount.
Compute principal-wise ROI = (margin + schemes - opex - finance cost) / capital employed; decide which principals to grow, renegotiate or exit. This is the language principals themselves use.
Classify SKUs by value (ABC) and demand variability (XYZ) to set differentiated norm stocks, service levels and FEFO priority — controlling expiry and dead stock.
Map primary->stocking->beat->secondary->collection->claims to locate margin leakage and non-value-added steps (e.g., manual claim filing, double handling).
Clarify accountability across owner, ASM, PSR, godown and accounts for credit approval, claim filing and expiry control — bottlenecks usually hide in unowned hand-offs.
Rank improvement initiatives (DMS roll-out, claim automation, beat redesign) by Reach x Impact x Confidence / Effort so a cash-constrained MSME sequences correctly.

risk_model.risk: Principal terminates or splits the territory / changes ROI structure
risk_model.control: Diversify across 3+ principals/categories, document service-level performance, and keep the distributorship agreement and termination/notice clauses reviewed.

risk_model.risk: Retailer bad debt and over-extended credit
risk_model.control: Credit-limit master with auto-block on the SFA app, aging-based collection discipline, and PDC/UPI-autopay for high-risk outlets.

risk_model.risk: GST mismatch / e-way bill non-compliance leading to ITC loss and notices
risk_model.control: Auto e-invoice + e-way generation from the DMS and monthly GSTR-1/2B reconciliation before filing.

risk_model.risk: Delayed payment to MSME suppliers triggering Sec 43B(h) disallowance / and own-side delayed principal payments losing cash discount
risk_model.control: Track MSME vendor status, pay within 45 days, and align payable calendar to capture cash discounts; reconcile under the working-capital cockpit.

risk_model.risk: Inventory expiry, breakage and shrinkage write-offs
risk_model.control: FEFO picking, ABC-XYZ norm stocks, near-expiry alerts, cycle counts and timely expiry-claim filing to the principal.

risk_model.risk: Drug/food licence lapse for pharma/FMCG-food distributors (wholesale drug licence / FSSAI)
risk_model.control: Maintain Form 20B/21B wholesale drug licence and FSSAI registration with renewal calendar; competent person and batch-record compliance for pharma.

risk_model.risk: GST registration / invoicing default and e-invoice threshold breach
risk_model.control: Monitor turnover against e-invoicing threshold, register and issue compliant invoices, and reconcile through the GST portal monthly.

kpi_structure.definition: (Annual margin + schemes - opex - finance cost) / average capital employed (inventory + receivables - payables).
Annual COGS / average inventory value.
Stock days + receivable days - payable days.
Outlets billed / outlets visited per beat (productive call %).
Average distinct SKUs billed per productive call.
Unreconciled principal claims (schemes/expiry/damage) and their age.
Retailer outstanding / daily secondary sales.

profitability_analysis.typical_net_margin: 1-3% on turnover (the business is ROCE-driven, not margin-driven)
unit_economics: A mid-size FMCG distributor on ₹8-15 crore annual turnover runs on ~6-8% gross margin = ₹50-100 lakh gross, netting ~1.5-2.5% (₹15-35 lakh) after beat, godown, finance and shrinkage costs.
Capital employed ~₹60-90 lakh (inventory ₹40-60 lakh + receivables ₹25-40 lakh - principal payables ₹15-25 lakh); on ₹25 lakh net that is ~28-35% ROCE when turns and claims are well managed.
Finance cost: CC/OD at 11-14% on ~₹70 lakh employed = ₹8-10 lakh/yr — a single biggest discretionary cost; every 5-day cut in CCC frees ~₹2-4 lakh of cash.
profitability_analysis.working_capital_notes: This IS the business. Distributors finance the channel: they pay principals fast (7-21 days, often advance for cash discount) but collect from retailers slow (20-45 days) with stock idle 20-40 days. The negative-to-tight working-capital gap is funded by CC/OD limits pledged against stock+book debt. Levers: faster turns, tighter retailer credit, capturing cash discounts, and zero-leak claim recovery. Sec 43B(h) now also forces timely payment to MSME-registered sub-vendors.
levers: Cut cash conversion cycle: tighten retailer credit (DSO down) and capture every principal cash discount
Lift inventory turns via ABC-XYZ norms and dead-stock liquidation — directly raises ROCE
Plug claim/scheme leakage (recover the 2-4% of throughput that silently vanishes)
Raise beat productivity (ECO + lines per bill) to grow secondary sales without adding capital
Renegotiate principal credit terms and margin slabs once service performance is documented

milestones: Master data clean-up: SKUs, outlets, beats, price/scheme masters
Field rep onboarding & app adoption (target >90% orders via app)
Baseline CCC, claims aging and CC/OD utilisation
Claims SOP with proof capture and weekly principal follow-up
Cash-discount capture calendar aligned to payables
Quarterly ROCE & CCC scorecard to owner

pm_workflows.cadence: Daily call analysis, monthly beat review
milestones: ECO and lines-per-bill baselines per PSR

key_activities: Negotiate distributorship/C&F agreement, ROI, margin slabs, credit terms
Obtain GST/Udyam and sector licences (drug/FSSAI where needed)
Define territory, beats and norm stocks; set up DMS masters
Forecast SKU-level offtake from beat history + scheme calendar
Place primary indent, manage norm/safety stock, capture cash discount
GRN with batch/expiry, 3-way match, landed-cost capture
Run daily beats via PJP and SFA order capture
Credit check, pick (FEFO), GST-compliant invoice + e-way bill, deliver
Execute schemes, merchandising and range selling
Reconcile principal & retailer ledgers, GST returns
Track ROI, CCC, turns, claims aging vs targets
Renegotiate principal terms / rationalise SKUs & principals

stages.focus: Stabilise core: digitise billing/GST, establish beats, control credit and expiry, prove ROI to the principal.
plays: Adopt Tally/entry DMS + e-invoice/e-way compliance
Define PJP and a basic credit-limit policy
Build a claims-filing discipline to stop early leakage
Lock norm stocks to avoid stock-outs of fast movers

stages.focus: Diversify principals to cut concentration risk; professionalise salesforce and working-capital management.
plays: Add 2-4 complementary principals/categories
Full DMS+SFA with ECO/lines-per-bill tracking and incentive redesign
ABC-XYZ norms + dead-stock liquidation; tighten CCC
Formal credit-control and collections function

stages.focus: Scale to super-stockist/C&F and multiple territories; build asset-light commission throughput and data-led operations.
plays: Take on super-stockist/C&F mandates (asset-light commission)
Sub-distributor network & redistribution model
Warehouse automation, 3PL, and AI forecasting/route optimisation
Investor/banking readiness for higher CC limits and expansion capex

digital_maturity_model.name: Manual / paper
signals: Hand-written order books and invoices
Ledgers in physical registers
No real-time stock or outstanding visibility
Owner-memory-driven decisions
digital_maturity_model.next_step: Adopt Tally/accounting + GST-compliant computerised billing and a basic stock register.

playbooks.name: Pharma Retail & Distribution
playbooks.one_liner: A licensed Indian retail chemist and/or pharma distribution (C&F/stockist) business that procures, stocks, and dispenses Schedule H/H1/X and OTC drugs against prescriptions under strict Drugs & Cosmetics Act controls, running on thin margins and high-velocity working capital across Tier-1/2/3 markets.

operating_model.summary: Buys medicines from manufacturers/super-stockists/distributors against credit, holds batch-and-expiry-tracked inventory under a Drug Licence (Form 20/21 retail, 20B/21B wholesale) supervised by a registered pharmacist, and resells to walk-in patients (retail) or sub-stockists/chemists/hospitals (distribution). Margin is regulated/thin; profit comes from volume, scheme/credit arbitrage, mix (generic vs branded vs surgical/FMCG/wellness), and disciplined working-capital and expiry management.
revenue_streams: Retail dispensing of Rx (Schedule H/H1/X) and OTC medicines at MRP
Distribution/wholesale margin to downstream chemists, sub-stockists, nursing homes and hospitals
High-margin adjacencies: generics/private-label, surgicals & consumables, nutraceuticals/wellness/FMCG, diagnostics tie-ups and home delivery
Manufacturer trade schemes, quantity/turnover incentives, and credit-period float
cost_structure: Cost of goods (medicine purchase) — 80-90% of revenue
Rent, electricity/refrigeration (cold-chain), and store/godown overheads
Salaries — registered pharmacist (mandatory), counter & delivery staff
Expiry/breakage/near-expiry write-offs and inventory carrying cost
Working-capital interest on distributor credit / OD, GST and licence/renewal fees, billing software (e.g. Marg/Vyapar) and POS
value_drivers: Inventory availability & fill-rate (in-stock fast-movers reduce lost scripts)
Expiry control via FEFO and tight return-to-supplier discipline
Credit terms negotiated upstream vs cash/credit given downstream (working-capital spread)
Footfall/location, doctor proximity & loyalty repeat-fill of chronic patients
Purchase-scheme capture and dead-stock minimisation

value_chain: Licensing & pharmacist onboarding (Drug Licence, GST, Udyam)
Goods inward, 3-way match, cold-chain check & FEFO shelving
Dispensing/sale against valid prescription (Schedule H1 register)
Billing, GST invoicing & collections (retail cash, distribution credit)

core_processes.description: Every batch tracked by expiry; First-Expiry-First-Out picking, near-expiry (60/90-day) flagging, and time-bound returns to distributor/manufacturer to recover value before write-off.
Schedule H/H1/X drugs sold only against a valid prescription; H1 drugs (and antibiotics) logged in the H1 register with patient/prescriber/quantity, retained 3 years for FDA inspection.
Purchase orders to distributors/super-stockists matched against goods receipt and invoice; trade schemes, free-goods and credit terms captured to protect margin.
Manage distributor credit (payables) against retail cash and downstream-chemist credit (receivables); reconcile bank, OD utilisation and supplier ageing weekly.

department_structure.mandate: Legal, accurate dispensing of Rx/OTC under a registered pharmacist; Schedule H1 register upkeep and patient counselling.
Maintain fill-rate and stock health, negotiate schemes/credit, run FEFO, manage expiry returns and recalls.
Service downstream chemists/hospitals via beat plans, order booking, delivery and credit collection.
GST/e-invoicing, payables/receivables, licence renewals, FDA/drug-inspector readiness, audit and statutory filings.

operational_bottlenecks.symptom: 1-3% of purchase value lost to expired stock; distributor refuses time-barred returns
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Direct erosion of already-thin net margin; cash locked in dead stock
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Weak FEFO discipline, over-ordering on schemes, no systematic near-expiry alerting or return-window tracking

operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Downstream chemists/hospitals pay in 60-120 days while distributors demand 30-45 days; OD maxed out
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Cash crunch, missed early-payment discounts, inability to capture schemes
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Generous credit given downstream vs tighter credit received upstream, plus no disciplined collections/ageing process

operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Patient walks to competitor when a molecule/brand is unavailable; substitution friction
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Lost sale + lost repeat chronic-patient lifetime value
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Manual reordering, no min/max or velocity-based reorder points, fragmented multi-distributor sourcing

operational_bottlenecks.bottleneck: Regulatory exposure on Schedule H1 / cold-chain
operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Incomplete H1 register, expired-drug-on-shelf, temperature excursions for vaccines/insulin
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Drug-inspector penalty, licence suspension/cancellation, stock seizure
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Paper registers, no temperature logging, low staff training, pharmacist not always present

operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Scheduled-drug ceiling prices and e-pharmacy 15-25% discounts undercut counter price
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Falling gross margin, footfall leakage to online players
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: DPCO price caps, manufacturer-driven MRPs, and aggressive online/chain competition with deeper buying power

ai_automation_opportunities.opportunity: Velocity- and expiry-aware auto-reorder: compute min/max and reorder points per SKU, flag near-expiry batches for return before the distributor window closes, and propose consolidated POs across distributors.
Working-capital & collections copilot: ageing of distributor payables vs downstream receivables, OD-cost vs scheme-discount trade-off, and early-payment/credit-term optimisation.
Schedule H1 / cold-chain compliance SOP automation: digital H1 register, expired-stock-on-shelf checks, FEFO picking SOP, temperature-log reminders and drug-inspector audit pack.
GST & e-invoicing automation for high-volume, multi-rate (5%/12%/18%) pharma billing with ITC reconciliation and HSN tagging.
Distribution beat-plan & order-booking optimisation: route/beat planning, downstream chemist coverage, and fill-rate/OTIF tracking for the wholesale arm.
Scheme & rate-contract negotiation intelligence: compare distributor schemes/credit terms per molecule and surface the best landed cost.

consulting_frameworks.use: Quantify days inventory (expiry-sensitive), receivables from downstream chemists, and payables to distributors; shrink the gap that funds the float.
Identify the binding constraint — usually working capital or expiry write-offs — and subordinate ordering/credit policy to relieve it.
Map margin leakage stage-by-stage from procurement scheme capture to dispensing to returns, and target the leakiest stage first.
Classify SKUs by value (ABC) and demand variability (XYZ); set service levels and reorder discipline, with FEFO overlay for expiry control.

consulting_frameworks.framework: Unit economics per prescription / per delivery
consulting_frameworks.use: Compute contribution per script/per chemist delivery net of carrying, expiry and credit cost to decide which segments and adjacencies to grow.

risk_model.risk: Drug Licence suspension/cancellation for Schedule H1 register lapses, expired stock on shelf, or pharmacist absence
risk_model.control: Digital H1 register, daily expired-stock sweep, ensure registered pharmacist on premises during sales, periodic mock drug-inspector audits

risk_model.risk: Cold-chain breach spoiling vaccines/insulin/biologicals
risk_model.control: Temperature-logged refrigeration with alarms, backup power, documented excursion protocol and FEFO

risk_model.risk: Working-capital insolvency from receivables drag and over-ordering on schemes
risk_model.control: Receivables ageing & credit limits downstream, OD-vs-discount discipline, velocity-based ordering, Sec 43B(h) MSME-payable awareness

risk_model.risk: GST mismatch / ITC denial on multi-rate pharma invoices and e-invoicing non-compliance
risk_model.control: Billing software with correct HSN/GST slabs, monthly GSTR-2B reconciliation, e-invoicing where turnover threshold applies

risk_model.risk: Expiry/dead-stock write-offs beyond returnable window
risk_model.control: Near-expiry (60/90-day) alerts, time-bound distributor return process, scheme-buy caps tied to velocity

risk_model.risk: Sale of spurious/sub-standard or banned/recalled drugs
risk_model.control: Buy only from licensed distributors, retain purchase invoices/batch records, act on recall notices immediately

kpi_structure.definition: (Sales − COGS) / Sales across retail + wholesale mix
COGS / average inventory at cost
Value of expired/unreturnable stock / purchase value
Average receivable days from downstream buyers
% of A-class/fast-moving SKUs in stock when demanded

unit_economics: Retail chemist: average ticket ₹250-450; ~120-250 bills/day; monthly revenue ₹15-40 lakh at a Tier-2 store; net ₹50k-1.5 lakh/month after rent, pharmacist salary and write-offs
Distribution: services 150-400 downstream chemists; monthly turnover ₹50 lakh-3 crore; net margin 1-3% means heavy reliance on scheme income and credit float
Expiry write-off of even 2% on ₹1 crore annual purchase (₹2 lakh) can wipe out a quarter of net profit
profitability_analysis.working_capital_notes: Working capital is THE bottleneck. Distributors give 21-45 days credit; retail is largely cash but chronic-patient and institutional/hospital sales run on credit. Distribution arm carries 30-90 day receivables against 30-45 day payables — a structural negative spread funded by OD/CC at 10-14%. Inventory of 30-45 days at cost plus expiry risk makes velocity-based ordering and tight collections the primary levers.
levers: Capture trade schemes/quantity discounts without over-ordering past velocity
Shift mix toward higher-margin generics, surgicals, nutraceuticals and private-label
Cut expiry write-offs to <1% via FEFO and time-bound returns
Tighten downstream credit and accelerate collections to shrink DSO
Negotiate longer distributor credit / better landed cost on A-class molecules

pm_workflows.initiative: FEFO + auto-reorder rollout in billing/inventory software (e.g. Marg)

pm_workflows.cadence: Monthly cycle with weekly ageing review
milestones: Build receivables ageing & set credit limits per chemist

key_activities: Obtain retail (Form 20/21) or wholesale (Form 20B/21B) Drug Licence
GST & Udyam registration, store fit-out with refrigeration
Define assortment: Rx, OTC, generics, surgicals, wellness
Loyalty for chronic patients, scheme/mix optimisation

stages.stage: Single retail store / single-area distributor (₹15-50 lakh/yr)
stages.focus: Survive on working capital and compliance; build local doctor & chronic-patient loyalty
plays: Get FEFO and digital H1 register right from day one
Capture chronic-patient repeat refills
Negotiate first solid distributor credit terms
Adopt billing software (Marg/Vyapar) with batch tracking

stages.focus: Margin mix and working-capital spread; expand beat or store cluster
plays: Add high-margin generics, surgicals, nutraceuticals & private-label
Tighten downstream credit & DSO
Centralise procurement to win bigger schemes
Launch WhatsApp/home-delivery and diagnostics tie-ups

stages.focus: Scale, technology and capital efficiency
plays: Central warehouse with WMS & cold-chain
ERP + e-pharmacy / aggregator integration
Institutional & hospital supply contracts
Data-driven assortment, demand forecasting and possible franchise expansion

digital_maturity_model.name: Manual / paper
signals: Handwritten bills and paper H1 register
No batch/expiry tracking
Reordering from memory; frequent stock-outs and expiry
digital_maturity_model.next_step: Adopt a basic pharmacy billing/inventory software with batch & expiry capture (e.g. Marg, Vyapar)

digital_maturity_model.name: Basic digital billing
signals: Software billing with GST invoices
Batch/expiry recorded but not actively used
Manual reordering, no analytics
digital_maturity_model.next_step: Turn on FEFO picking, near-expiry alerts and min/max reorder points; digitise the H1 register

digital_maturity_model.name: Integrated inventory & compliance
signals: FEFO and expiry-return discipline live
Digital H1 register & GST reconciliation
Receivables ageing tracked
digital_maturity_model.next_step: Add demand forecasting, supplier-scheme comparison and a working-capital dashboard

digital_maturity_model.name: Data-driven operations
signals: Velocity-based auto-reorder & forecasting
Cash-conversion-cycle and fill-rate dashboards
e-pharmacy/aggregator and delivery integration
digital_maturity_model.next_step: Layer AI copilots for reorder, collections and compliance audit packs; integrate ERP across stores/warehouse

digital_maturity_model.name: AI-native
signals: AI auto-reorder & expiry-return optimisation
Automated GST/H1/cold-chain audit packs
AI working-capital & scheme-negotiation copilots across the network
digital_maturity_model.next_step: Continuously tune AI models on demand, expiry and credit data; expand AI-driven assortment and pricing

playbooks.name: Manufacturing MSMEs
playbooks.one_liner: A small-to-mid Indian manufacturing unit (typically Udyam-registered, ₹1-50 cr turnover) that converts raw material into finished/intermediate goods via machining, fabrication or assembly — usually job-work/OEM-supply driven with a thin spread of own-brand sales.

operating_model.summary: Order-to-cash anchored on a BOM-driven shop floor: raw material is procured against confirmed orders (or forecast for fast-movers), converted through machining/fabrication/assembly work-centres into WIP and finished goods, then dispatched to OEM/B2B buyers on 45-90 day credit. Most Indian manufacturing MSMEs run as Tier-2/3 OEM job-shops or component suppliers with 1-3 anchor customers contributing 50-70% of revenue, supplemented by spot/replacement-market sales. Margin lives in machine utilisation, scrap control, and conversion-cost discipline, not in price.
revenue_streams: OEM/B2B supply contracts (rate-contract or PO-based) — the bulk of revenue
Job-work / contract machining (customer supplies material, unit charges conversion + labour)
Replacement/aftermarket and spares sales (higher margin, lumpy)
Own-brand / channel sales through distributors and dealers (for finished-goods makers)
Scrap and by-product sale (recovered MS/metal turnings, runners, offcuts)
cost_structure: Raw material & bought-out components — 55-70% of sales (steel, polymer, castings, fasteners, electronics)
Direct labour + contract/casual workforce — 8-15%
Power & fuel (DG backup, furnace/compressor load) — 3-8%, higher for energy-intensive processes
Consumables, tooling, dies & cutting inserts — 2-5%
Machine depreciation, maintenance & spares — 3-6%
Factory overheads (rent/lease, factory licence, safety, EPF/ESI, GST/logistics) — 6-10%
Interest on working-capital limits (CC/OD against receivables & stock) — 2-5%
value_drivers: Machine/asset utilisation (OEE) — fixed cost absorption
First-pass yield and scrap/rework rate — directly converts to margin
On-time-in-full (OTIF) delivery — retains anchor OEM customers and avoids penalties
Working-capital velocity (inventory turns + DSO) — determines cash strain
Customer concentration vs diversification — risk-adjusted enterprise value
Process capability (Cpk) and certifications (ISO/IATF/BIS) — unlocks premium tier-1 customers

value_chain: Enquiry & RFQ costing (BOM + routing + conversion cost estimate)
Order confirmation & production planning (PPC, capacity load)
Procurement & inward QC (raw material, bought-outs, 3-way match)
Machining / fabrication / assembly (work-order execution, WIP tracking)
In-process & final quality inspection (FPY, Cpk, rejection logging)

core_processes.description: Build a multi-level bill of materials with material rates, scrap allowance, machine-hour rate and conversion cost to quote accurately; the single biggest determinant of whether an order is profitable. Most MSMEs under-cost overheads and lose money on long-tail SKUs.

core_processes.process: Production planning & control (PPC) and work-order management
core_processes.description: Convert confirmed orders into work orders, sequence them across work-centres against capacity, release material, and track WIP movement so the shop floor isn't planned on a whiteboard and a shop diary.

core_processes.process: Procurement & inventory control (raw material to WIP to FG)
core_processes.description: Reorder-point/MOQ-driven buying with 3-way match (PO-GRN-invoice), batch/heat-number traceability, and FIFO stock rotation to avoid the twin failures of stock-outs halting machines and dead inventory eating cash.

Incoming, in-process and final inspection with rejection/rework logging, Cpk for critical dimensions, and material traceability — mandatory to keep IATF/ISO/BIS certification and tier-1 OEM contracts.
Scheduled preventive maintenance and spares planning for critical machines; unplanned breakdowns are a primary cause of OTIF misses and overtime cost.

department_structure.mandate: Execute work orders across work-centres, hit daily output and OTIF targets, control WIP and run preventive maintenance.
Incoming/in-process/final inspection, control plans, Cpk monitoring, rejection & customer-complaint resolution, certification audits.
Source raw material/bought-outs at right cost & lead time, manage stores with traceability, plan inward & outward logistics and e-way bills.
Win RFQs, manage anchor-customer relationships, negotiate rate contracts, handle order pipeline and aftermarket sales.
Working-capital & CC/OD management, GST/TDS compliance, costing & profitability, collections (DSO), payroll and statutory dues.
Workforce (permanent + contract) management, EPF/ESI/PT compliance, factory-licence & safety norms, training and industrial relations.

operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Orders won on price turn out loss-making after actuals; owner can't tell which SKUs/customers make money.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Eroded margins despite high turnover; chronic cash stress and 'busy but broke' syndrome.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: No proper multi-level BOM + machine-hour-rate costing; overheads, scrap and rework not loaded into quotes; costing done on gut feel in Excel.

operational_bottlenecks.bottleneck: Working-capital trap (high DSO + slow inventory + Sec 43B(h))
operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Receivables stuck at 75-120 days from large OEM buyers while suppliers and labour need paying weekly; CC limit always fully drawn.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Production throttled by cash, not capacity; growth orders refused for lack of working capital.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Power asymmetry with anchor OEM customers who dictate credit terms; slow inventory turns; weak collection discipline; supplier payments now squeezed by 45-day Sec 43B(h) deadline.

operational_bottlenecks.bottleneck: Customer concentration / dependence on 1-3 anchor OEMs
operational_bottlenecks.symptom: 50-70% of revenue from a handful of buyers who control price, payment terms and volume.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: A single customer loss or volume cut can wipe out a year's profit; valuation discount on exit/funding.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Tier-2/3 job-shops grow by deepening one relationship rather than diversifying; lack of own brand or aftermarket channel.

operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Machines idle waiting for material/tooling/operators; frequent breakdowns; overtime to meet dispatch.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Fixed costs under-absorbed, missed OTIF, penalties and lost repeat orders.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: No OEE measurement, reactive (breakdown-only) maintenance, poor PPC sequencing, material not staged ahead of the machine.

operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Customer line rejections, 8D reports, high in-house rework; scrap recovered below cost.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Direct margin loss, certification risk, and damaged OEM relationships.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Inadequate in-process control plans, untrained/contract-heavy workforce, no SPC/Cpk monitoring on critical characteristics, weak incoming QC.

operational_bottlenecks.bottleneck: Skilled-labour shortage and high contract-workforce churn
operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Difficulty hiring trained machinists/welders; absenteeism; over-reliance on contract labour.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Inconsistent quality, training cost re-incurred, compliance exposure on contract labour.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: ITI/skill-pipeline gaps in Tier-2/3 clusters, wage competition, no structured multi-skilling or retention plan.

ai_automation_opportunities.opportunity: Automated BOM-and-routing-based RFQ costing engine that loads material rates, scrap%, machine-hour rate and overheads to produce a defensible quote in minutes and flag below-margin orders.
Receivables/DSO copilot that ages invoices, auto-drafts collection reminders to OEM buyers, prioritises by amount-at-risk, and tracks against the CC limit and Sec 43B(h) supplier-payment clock.
Production planning & OEE assistant: sequences work orders against capacity, predicts OTIF risk, and surfaces machine idle/breakdown patterns for preventive maintenance scheduling.
Inventory/reorder agent driving ROP-MOQ reorder suggestions, dead-stock and excess alerts, and batch/heat-number traceability across RM-WIP-FG.
GST + e-invoice + e-way bill automation: auto-generate IRN and e-way bills on dispatch, reconcile GSTR-2B for ITC on inputs, and flag mismatches before filing.
Vendor-development and procurement agent: multi-vendor RFQ comparison, lead-time/OTIF scorecards, and 3-way-match exception flagging (PO-GRN-invoice).
Quality/8D copilot that logs rejections, runs Pareto on defect modes, drafts 8D/CAPA reports for customer complaints, and tracks Cpk on critical characteristics.

consulting_frameworks.use: Identify the bottleneck work-centre/machine that caps plant throughput, exploit and subordinate to it (stage material ahead, avoid starving/blocking), and elevate only when justified — the single highest-ROI lens for a job-shop.

Quantify DIO + DSO − DPO to expose the cash gap; target each lever (faster inventory turns, tighter collections from OEM buyers, negotiated supplier terms within Sec 43B(h)) to free trapped cash without new debt.

consulting_frameworks.framework: Unit economics / contribution margin per machine-hour
consulting_frameworks.use: Cost every SKU by BOM + machine-hour rate + conversion cost; rank products by contribution-per-bottleneck-hour to decide what to push, re-price or drop.
Map enquiry-to-cash to locate where margin is lost (under-costing, scrap, idle machines, collection delay) and where to invest for differentiation (quality, OTIF, certification).
Reduce the seven wastes on the shop floor, baseline and improve OEE (availability x performance x quality), and run structured Kaizen on scrap, changeover (SMED) and rework.
Clarify who is Responsible/Accountable for RFQ costing, work-order release, QC sign-off, dispatch and collections so handoffs between PPC, production, QA and dispatch don't drop.

Segment RM and spares by value (ABC) and criticality (VED) to set differentiated reorder, safety-stock and counting policies — tight control on the few high-value/critical items, light control on the many cheap ones.

risk_model.risk: Customer concentration — loss or volume cut from an anchor OEM (50-70% of revenue)
risk_model.control: Diversify to a target where no single customer exceeds 30-35% of revenue; build aftermarket/own-brand channel; secure annual rate contracts and rolling forecasts.

risk_model.risk: Working-capital squeeze — receivables stuck 75-120 days while Sec 43B(h) forces 45-day supplier payment
risk_model.control: Enforce credit policy and DSO targets, use TReDS/bill discounting for OEM receivables, time MSME-supplier payments within 45 days to keep the deduction and avoid disallowance.

risk_model.risk: Factory safety / Factories Act non-compliance (accidents, working-hours, hazardous process)
risk_model.control: Maintain valid factory licence, statutory registers, safety committee, machine guarding, and incident reporting; appoint a safety officer above thresholds.

risk_model.risk: Selling/dispatching BIS-notified products without mandatory certification (QCO)
risk_model.control: Check the QCO/BIS-notified list for your HSNs before production; obtain ISI/BIS licence; verify imported inputs are certified.

risk_model.risk: GST ITC loss & e-way-bill default — input credit denied on supplier non-filing; goods detained in transit
risk_model.control: Reconcile GSTR-2B monthly before claiming ITC, hold payment on non-compliant vendors, auto-generate e-invoice IRN and e-way bills on every dispatch.

risk_model.risk: EPF/ESI and contract-labour compliance failure (large casual/contract workforce)
risk_model.control: Register and remit EPF/ESI on time, audit contractor compliance, maintain muster/wage registers, transition to Labour-Code-aligned records.

risk_model.risk: Quality rejection / product-liability and certification suspension from chronic defects
risk_model.control: In-process control plans, SPC/Cpk on critical characteristics, structured 8D/CAPA, supplier-quality audits, calibration discipline.

kpi_structure.definition: Availability x Performance x Quality on bottleneck/critical machines.
% of customer orders delivered complete and on the committed date.
% of units passing QC without rework; or rejection PPM on critical characteristics.
COGS / average inventory per year.
Average days to collect receivables from customers.

kpi_structure.kpi: Scrap & rework cost as % of sales
kpi_structure.definition: Cost of scrapped material + rework labour / net sales.
Productive machine-hours / available machine-hours.

unit_economics: Machine-hour rate (mid-size CNC/VMC): ₹350-900/hr loaded (depreciation + power + operator + overhead); a job is profitable only if conversion price > machine-hour rate x cycle time + material + scrap allowance.
Indicative component: RM ₹120 + bought-outs ₹30 + conversion (0.5 hr @ ₹500) ₹250 + 3% scrap ₹12 = ₹412 cost; quoted at ₹520 → ~21% gross contribution before factory overhead.
Scrap recovery: MS turnings sold at ₹25-40/kg vs RM bought at ₹55-75/kg — every 1% scrap reduction on a ₹10 cr material spend adds ~₹6-8 lakh to the bottom line.
profitability_analysis.working_capital_notes: Working capital is the binding constraint: typical cash conversion cycle of 90-150 days (DIO 45-75 + DSO 60-100 − DPO 30-45). Most units run on CC/OD limits (12-16% interest) drawn against stock + book debts. OEM buyers dictate 60-90 day credit while Sec 43B(h) forces MSME-supplier payment within 45 days, squeezing the middle. Freeing 15 days of the cycle on ₹20 cr turnover releases roughly ₹80 lakh-₹1 cr of cash.
levers: Re-cost and re-price (or exit) loss-making long-tail SKUs using machine-hour costing
Lift OEE/utilisation to absorb fixed cost over more output — the fastest margin lever
Cut scrap/rework via in-process SPC and operator training
Compress DSO via disciplined collections, TReDS/bill discounting on OEM receivables
Shift mix toward higher-margin aftermarket/spares and certified premium work
Negotiate supplier terms and consolidate vendors to improve DPO and price

pm_workflows.initiative: ERP / shop-floor digitisation (BOM + work-orders + WIP + GST)
milestones: Master data clean-up (item master, BOM, routings, vendors)

pm_workflows.initiative: OEE & lean improvement program on the bottleneck line
pm_workflows.cadence: Daily shop-floor huddle + weekly Kaizen review (90-day cycle)
milestones: Identify top-3 loss buckets (breakdown, changeover, quality)
