playbooks.name: FMCG Distribution
playbooks.one_liner: An FMCG distributor is the local last-mile credit-and-logistics engine that buys branded fast-moving goods from a company/super-stockist and redistributes them on fixed beats to 200-2,000 kirana/retail outlets across a defined town or territory, earning a thin fixed margin on high-velocity turns.

operating_model.summary: A capital-and-logistics intermediary: the distributor invests working capital and a delivery fleet to convert company primary sales into outlet-level secondary sales across a fixed-territory beat plan. Margin is fixed by the principal (typically 4-8% on FMCG), so the entire game is volume, range/width of distribution, low stock-out, fast inventory turns and tight credit recovery. A super-stockist sits one rung up, breaking bulk for sub-distributors in deeper Tier-3/rural markets.
revenue_streams: Primary-to-secondary distribution margin on principal brands (fixed % per SKU/category, ~4-8%)
Volume/QPS slabs, scheme pass-back differentials and display/visibility incentives from the company
Logistics/breaking-bulk margin as super-stockist to downstream sub-distributors
Liquidation of near-expiry/damaged stock and modern-trade/e-com B2B supply where permitted
Float/credit-spread economics (buying on company credit, selling partly on credit) and cash discounts for early principal payment
cost_structure: Inventory purchase (90%+ of cash outflow; the dominant working-capital block)
Salesman/DSR salaries + incentives and delivery boy wages (the beat workforce)
Delivery fleet/vehicle running, fuel, third-party tempo hire
Godown rent, electricity, refrigeration for cold-chain SKUs, racking
Damages/expiry/leakage write-offs, claim-recovery lag, and ERP/DMS software + handheld/SFA app licences
value_drivers: Range selling and numeric + weighted distribution (how many outlets, how much of the basket each buys)
Inventory turns (8-15x/yr for grocery FMCG) and fill-rate/OTIF to retailers
Credit discipline / low DSO and low expiry-damage %
Beat productivity: lines-per-call, drop size, and bills-cut-per-DSR-per-day

value_chain: Principal/company tie-up and territory appointment (ROI agreement, scheme terms)
Primary order forecasting and indenting from company/super-stockist
Inward GRN, godown storage, batch/expiry binning and master-data setup
Beat planning and DSR route allocation (PJP - permanent journey plan)
Outlet order capture (SFA app / manual) and order consolidation
Invoicing (GST e-invoice), picking, loading and last-mile delivery on beat
Secondary sales realisation, credit collection and outstanding management
Scheme/claim filing with company, reconciliation and primary re-order
Returns, near-expiry liquidation and damage-claim settlement

core_processes.description: Fixed weekly journey plan where each DSR covers a set of outlets per day; productivity tracked via SFA app on calls, productive calls, lines and value per call.
Buy on company credit (7-21 days), sell on retailer credit (3-15 days for grocery, longer for cosmetics); manage the gap, cash discounts and overdue recovery to protect ROI.
Track every consumer/trade scheme, QPS slab and damage claim, file with the company and reconcile receivable claims against credit notes - the single biggest source of locked-up money.
First-Expiry-First-Out batch rotation, near-expiry alerts, ageing buckets and damage segregation to keep expiry/damage under 0.5-1% of throughput.

department_structure.mandate: Maximise secondary sales, numeric/weighted distribution and beat productivity across the territory.
Accurate inward/GRN, FEFO storage, error-free picking and on-time last-mile delivery.
Manage ROI, working capital, credit/collections, GST/e-invoice filing and claim recovery.
Forecast primary indents, avoid stock-outs and overstock, control expiry and damages.
Principal relationship management, territory expansion, cash and overall ROI governance.

operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Lakhs of rupees in unsettled scheme/damage claims sitting as receivable for 60-120+ days, eroding ROI.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Working capital starved; distributor effectively finances the brand's promotions interest-free.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Manual scheme tracking, frequent scheme changes, mismatch between claimed vs company-approved amounts, and slow company settlement processes.

operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Rising DSO, cheque bounces and ageing outstandings from kirana outlets; DSR doubling as recovery agent.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Cash gets stuck on the street, distributor borrows to fund the next primary order, ROI falls below cost of capital.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Informal credit culture in trade, no credit-limit enforcement at billing, weak follow-up discipline and over-reliance on relationship-based selling.

operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Write-offs and returns on perishable/short-shelf-life SKUs; godown full of slow-movers.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Direct margin loss (often wiping out 1-2% of a 5% margin) plus blocked space and capital.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: No FEFO discipline, over-indenting against schemes, poor SKU-level demand sensing and weak near-expiry liquidation process.

operational_bottlenecks.bottleneck: Low beat productivity and unproductive calls
operational_bottlenecks.symptom: DSRs visiting outlets but not booking orders; low lines-per-call and drop size; high beat skips.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Fixed salesforce cost not covered by secondary sales; distribution width stagnates.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Unscientific PJP/beat design, no SFA enforcement, salesman selling only top 10 SKUs, and lack of range-selling incentives.

operational_bottlenecks.bottleneck: Stock-outs of A-class SKUs vs overstock of C-class
operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Best-sellers unavailable while warehouse is clogged with slow movers; lost secondary sales.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Retailer buys competing brand, distribution width and loyalty erode, fill-rate drops.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Indenting driven by company push/schemes rather than secondary off-take data; no ABC-XYZ classification or reorder logic.

operational_bottlenecks.symptom: No single view of secondary sales, outstanding, stock and claims; owner runs business by gut.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Slow decisions, reconciliation errors, GST/e-invoice mismatches and fraud/leakage risk.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Underinvestment in DMS/SFA, poor data hygiene, and resistance to digital adoption among staff.

ai_automation_opportunities.opportunity: AI demand-sensing and auto-indent: predict primary order quantities per SKU from secondary off-take, seasonality and scheme calendar to cut stock-outs and expiry.
Automated claim/scheme reconciliation bot that matches filed claims to company credit notes, flags shortfalls and ages receivables.
AI beat optimiser + DSR productivity coach: redesign PJP routes, predict best next-SKU to pitch per outlet, and nudge range-selling.
Credit-risk scoring of retailers and automated overdue collection workflows (limit enforcement at billing, reminder cadence).
GST e-invoice + e-way bill auto-generation and ITC reconciliation against principal invoices.
DMS/ERP rollout advisory and SFA app onboarding to digitise secondary sales capture end-to-end.
FEFO expiry-alert SOPs and near-expiry liquidation playbook generation.

consulting_frameworks.framework: Working-capital cycle (cash conversion: DIO + DSO - DPO)
consulting_frameworks.use: Diagnose where cash is trapped - inventory days vs retailer credit days vs company payment terms - and re-engineer to protect distributor ROI, the sector's core metric.
The industry-standard P&L lens: (annual margin + schemes - expenses) / average investment; companies and distributors both target 18-30%+ ROI, so every lever maps to it.
Identify the binding constraint in the flow - usually working capital or beat-coverage capacity - and exploit/elevate it before optimising elsewhere.
Classify SKUs by value (ABC) and demand variability (XYZ) to set differentiated indent/reorder and expiry rules, killing overstock of slow C-movers.
Measure not just how many outlets are billed (numeric) but the basket each buys (weighted) to drive width and depth, the two growth axes for a distributor.
Clarify ownership across DSR, billing, godown and collections for high-friction processes like claims and overdue recovery to remove the 'everyone/no-one' gaps.
Model cost-to-serve a beat (DSR cost + delivery + working-capital interest) vs secondary margin generated to decide beat splits and salesforce sizing.

risk_model.risk: Receivables/credit blow-up: retailer overdues turn into bad debt and cheque bounces
risk_model.control: Hard credit limits enforced at billing, ageing reports, DSR-linked collection incentives, and stop-supply rules; track against benchmark DSO.

risk_model.risk: GST / e-invoice / e-way bill non-compliance and ITC mismatch
risk_model.control: Auto e-invoice above threshold, e-way bill for inter-city movement, monthly GSTR-2B reconciliation against principal invoices.

risk_model.risk: Inventory expiry, damage and shrinkage losses
risk_model.control: FEFO batch rotation, near-expiry alerts at 60/90 days, segregated damage stock and disciplined company claim filing.

risk_model.risk: Delayed payments to / from chain choke working capital (MSME Sec 43B(h) exposure on payables)
risk_model.control: Pay registered-MSME suppliers within 45 days to avoid disallowance; align primary payment terms with secondary realisation.

risk_model.risk: FSSAI licensing lapse for handling/storing food & beverage FMCG
risk_model.control: Maintain valid FSSAI distributor/storage licence, hygienic godown, batch traceability and timely renewal.

risk_model.risk: Principal de-appointment / territory loss or margin cut
risk_model.control: Diversify across multiple non-competing principals, exceed coverage/ROI norms, and formalise the distributor agreement terms.

risk_model.risk: Cash-handling fraud, fictitious billing and scheme leakage by staff
risk_model.control: SFA-app order capture, segregation of duties, daily cash reconciliation and surprise stock audits.

kpi_structure.definition: (Annual net margin incl. schemes - operating expenses) / average capital invested.
Annual cost of goods sold / average inventory at cost.
Average days to collect secondary-sales receivables from retailers.
Value of expired/damaged stock as % of throughput.
% of mapped outlets in territory billed at least once per month.
Average distinct SKUs billed per outlet that ordered.
% of ordered lines delivered in full and on time.

profitability_analysis.typical_gross_margin: 4-8% (fixed by principal; cosmetics/impulse higher, staples lower)
profitability_analysis.typical_net_margin: 1-2.5% net of all expenses (the business is a thin-margin, high-turn, ROI-on-capital game)
unit_economics: A mid-size FMCG distributor doing ₹6-12 crore annual turnover on a ~5% blended margin earns ₹30-60 lakh gross; after DSR/delivery salaries, godown rent, fuel, interest and damages (~3-3.5% of sales), net is ₹6-18 lakh.
Per DSR/beat: covers ~30-50 outlets/day, ~₹2-4 lakh secondary sales/month at ₹15-25k loaded cost - must generate >₹10-15k margin/month to be ROI-positive.
Working-capital block: ₹50 lakh-₹1.5 crore tied in inventory + receivables; at 12-14% borrowing cost, every extra 10 DSO days can erase 0.3-0.5% of net margin.
profitability_analysis.working_capital_notes: This is fundamentally a working-capital business. Cash conversion = inventory days (25-45) + receivable days (5-20) - company credit days (7-21). The winning levers are faster turns, near-zero overdues, prompt claim recovery, and negotiating cash discounts vs credit from the principal. Channel-finance / RBI MSME credit lines and supply-chain finance materially lift ROI when overdues are controlled.
levers: Increase inventory turns via ABC-XYZ indenting and FEFO to release trapped capital
Cut DSO with credit limits, stop-supply discipline and collection-linked DSR incentives
Accelerate claim/scheme recovery to unlock 30-90 day receivables from principals
Lift weighted distribution / range-selling to grow margin on the same fixed cost base
Negotiate cash-discount terms with principals and use supply-chain finance to fund primary

pm_workflows.initiative: DMS + SFA digitisation rollout (secondary sales capture)
milestones: Vendor/DMS selection and master-data cleanup (SKU, outlet, beat)
DSR handheld app onboarding and parallel run with manual billing
Adoption KPIs hit: >90% orders via app, daily auto-secondary dashboard
Age all retailer outstandings and pending company claims
Set and enforce credit limits at billing
File and reconcile backlog claims with principals
Bring DSO under 12 days and claim-receivable under 30 days
Outlet census and white-space mapping in target town
Numeric distribution >80% in new beat within one quarter
Master-data and beat mapping for new range
First-quarter coverage and sell-through targets met

key_activities: Negotiate territory, margin and ROI agreement
Set up godown, capital and fleet
Master-data and beat mapping for the new range
Indent based on secondary off-take and scheme calendar
Beat/PJP execution and outlet order capture
ROI and coverage review with principal

stages.focus: Stabilise core operations, ROI and credit discipline
plays: Digitise billing and secondary sales (DMS/SFA)
Enforce credit limits and FEFO to protect margin
Hit >80% numeric distribution in the core town

stages.focus: Diversify brands and densify coverage
plays: Add non-competing principals to spread fixed costs
Expand beats into Tier-3 / rural via sub-stockists
Build claims-recovery and working-capital muscle; tap channel finance

stages.focus: Scale, formalise and add new channels
plays: Operate as super-stockist supplying sub-distributors in deeper geographies
Add modern-trade and B2B e-commerce supply where allowed
AI-driven demand sensing, beat optimisation and centralised finance/ERP across territories

digital_maturity_model.name: Manual / paper
signals: Handwritten bills and order books
Stock and outstanding tracked in registers
Owner runs business on memory and relationships
digital_maturity_model.next_step: Move accounting and invoicing onto Tally with GST e-invoicing.

digital_maturity_model.name: Basic digital accounting
signals: Tally/Busy for billing and GST
Excel for stock and outstanding
No outlet-level secondary visibility
digital_maturity_model.next_step: Adopt a Distribution Management System (DMS) to capture stock, schemes and secondary sales.

digital_maturity_model.name: DMS / SFA enabled
signals: DMS for inventory, schemes and claims
DSRs on a Sales Force Automation app for order capture
Secondary sales and coverage dashboards exist
digital_maturity_model.next_step: Integrate DMS with the principal's system and add analytics on beat productivity and ageing.

digital_maturity_model.name: Integrated & analytics-driven
signals: Company-distributor data integration and auto-claim flow
ABC-XYZ indenting and credit-limit enforcement
KPI dashboards (ROI, DSO, fill-rate) used for decisions
digital_maturity_model.next_step: Layer AI for demand forecasting, beat optimisation and predictive credit/expiry alerts.

digital_maturity_model.name: AI-native distribution
signals: AI demand-sensing auto-generates primary indents
AI beat optimiser and next-best-SKU recommendations to DSRs
Automated claim reconciliation and predictive credit-risk scoring
digital_maturity_model.next_step: Extend AI orchestration across multiple territories/principals with autonomous replenishment and finance copilots.

playbooks.name: Agro Trading
playbooks.one_liner: An Indian MSME agro-commodity trading house that aggregates spices, rice, grain and pulses from mandis/FPOs, value-adds (cleaning, grading, drying, packing) and sells into domestic wholesale buyers, processors and APEDA-registered export channels.

operating_model.summary: A working-capital-intensive arbitrage and aggregation business: buy physical agri-commodities at the farm gate/mandi at the right grade and price, hold/transform briefly, and resell at a spread to domestic processors, large wholesalers or overseas buyers. Margin is thin and per-quintal; profit is made on turns, freight/quality arbitrage and disciplined price-risk management, not on a fat markup.
revenue_streams: Spot trading spread on commodity sales (domestic wholesale/mandi-to-mandi arbitrage), typically 2-6% gross per cycle
Export sales to APEDA buyers in INR/USD (spices, basmati/non-basmati rice, pulses) at higher 8-15% gross but longer cycles
Value-add fees: cleaning, sortex grading, fumigation, drying, private-label packing for processors/brands
Commission/del-credere as a buying agent for large mills or exporters
Storage/warehouse rent and pledge-finance facilitation (WDRA e-NWR collateral)
cost_structure: COGS = farm-gate/mandi purchase price (85-92% of revenue) — the dominant line
Mandi charges, APMC cess/commission (1-2.5%), market fee and arhatiya commission
Logistics: primary freight from mandi, secondary freight to buyer/port, loading/unloading, handling
Processing & quality: cleaning/sortex, drying, fumigation, gunny/jute/PP bags and packing
Storage & shrinkage: warehouse rent, moisture/weight loss, pilferage, quality deterioration (1-4%)
Finance cost: interest on CC/OD limits and pledge loans (10-14% p.a.) — material given 60-120 day cycles
Compliance/export: APEDA, phytosanitary, fumigation, lab testing (pesticide residue/aflatoxin), CHA, documentation
value_drivers: Inventory turns and cash-conversion speed (turns matter far more than per-unit margin)
Quality grading & moisture control accuracy (rejections destroy a season's profit)
Price-risk discipline — buying against confirmed orders vs speculative open positions
Trusted farmer/FPO/arhatiya sourcing network and buyer relationships
Access to cheap working capital (CC limit, e-NWR pledge finance, channel credit)

value_chain: Sourcing & price discovery (mandi/FPO/farm-gate, eNAM, daily price scan)
Procurement & quality inspection (grading, moisture, foreign-matter check at lifting)
Order matching & price-risk cover (domestic buyer or export contract)
Export documentation/customs OR domestic invoicing & e-way bill

core_processes.description: Lift stock from mandi/FPO only against a confirmed buyer order or firm price view; capture grade, moisture, weight slip and arhatiya bill; release farmer payment within agreed days; avoid open speculative positions beyond a set risk limit.

Sample-test every inbound lot for moisture, foreign matter, broken %, and (for export) pesticide residue/aflatoxin; assign lot numbers; segregate by grade so the right quality maps to the right buyer/export spec and rejections are pre-empted.

Match purchased lots to sales contracts, raise GST invoice + e-way bill (domestic) or export docs (invoice, packing list, phytosanitary, BL, APEDA RCMC), dispatch, then track collection/LC realisation and book the net spread per trade.
Run CC/OD utilisation, e-NWR pledge loans against stored stock, supplier and buyer credit days so that the cash-conversion cycle stays funded without breaching drawing power or interest budget.

department_structure.mandate: Own price discovery, sourcing relationships and buy/sell decisions within a defined risk/position limit; the P&L engine of the firm.
Grade, test, clean, dry, fumigate and certify lots to domestic and export specs; minimise rejections and shrinkage.
Manage godown intake, stacking, inventory accuracy, dispatch and freight to buyer/port at lowest landed cost.
Fund the cycle (CC/pledge), control credit, run GST/e-way/TDS, book trade-wise P&L and manage banking/LC.
Handle APEDA/DGFT/customs documentation, CHA coordination, lab certs and buyer compliance for export consignments.

operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Stock bought at high mandi price suddenly worth less when commodity prices crash before a buyer is locked; a single bad position wipes out months of thin spreads.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: A 5-8% adverse price move on an unhedged lot can erase the entire 2-6% trading margin and turn a season profitable-on-paper into a loss.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Speculative buying ahead of confirmed orders, no position/stop-loss limits, and absence of any hedging (NCDEX futures) or back-to-back contracting discipline.

operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Cash stuck in inventory and receivables for 60-120 days; CC limit maxed out at peak season; farmer payments due immediately while buyers pay late.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Missed buying opportunities at season-low prices and high interest cost (10-14% p.a.) compressing already-thin net margin.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Asymmetric credit terms (pay farmers fast, collect from buyers slow), under-utilised e-NWR pledge financing, and inventory held longer than needed without turns discipline.

operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Consignments rejected by exporters/processors for high moisture, broken %, foreign matter, pesticide residue or aflatoxin; weight loss in storage.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Rejection means freight back, distress resale at a discount, and for export a failed contract plus reputational hit; 1-4% shrinkage silently eats margin.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Inadequate inbound QC/lab testing, poor drying/moisture control, godown pest/moisture issues, and no lot-level traceability to isolate bad batches.

operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Buyers rely on phone calls to arhatiyas for daily prices; arbitrage opportunities across mandis missed; over-dependence on a few commission agents.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Buying above the best available price and weak negotiating leverage; margin left on the table on every lot.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: No systematic capture of eNAM/mandi price feeds, weak FPO/farm-gate direct sourcing, and informal, relationship-only price intelligence.

operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Shipments held at port over missing phytosanitary/fumigation certs, APEDA RCMC issues, residue test failures or e-BRC/LC mismatches.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Demurrage and detention charges, delayed realisation, buyer penalties and lost repeat orders.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Manual, last-minute documentation, no pre-shipment compliance checklist, and poor coordination between QC, CHA and the export desk.

operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Significant cash dealing at mandi, incomplete purchase records, mismatch between physical stock and books.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: GST/ITC leakage, inability to raise adequate bank limits, exposure on tax assessment, and unreliable trade-wise profitability.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Legacy mandi cash culture, lack of digitised purchase capture, and treating accounting as a year-end compliance chore rather than a daily control.

ai_automation_opportunities.opportunity: Daily multi-mandi/eNAM price-scan and arbitrage alert engine that flags the best buy/sell spread per commodity and warns on open-position price risk.
Working-capital and cash-conversion-cycle dashboard linking inventory days, receivable days and CC/pledge utilisation with alerts before drawing-power breach.
Lot-level inventory + shrinkage and aging tracker with grade/moisture tagging so slow/at-risk stock is matched to buyers before quality degrades.
Automated export documentation and pre-shipment compliance checklist (APEDA RCMC, phytosanitary, fumigation, residue/aflatoxin lab certs, e-way/e-BRC) to kill port delays.
GST invoice + e-way bill auto-generation and ITC reconciliation against mandi/supplier purchases to plug input-credit leakage.
Procure-to-pay assistant that ties every lifting to a confirmed order or risk limit and schedules farmer/FPO payments within agreed days.
Price-risk and quality-rejection risk register that scores open positions, counterparty credit and consignment specs against buyer requirements.

consulting_frameworks.use: Quantify inventory days + receivable days - payable days; this is the single most important lever in agro trading where margins are thin and cash velocity, not markup, drives ROCE.
Identify the binding constraint each season — usually working-capital limit or QC/sortex throughput — and subordinate buying/selling decisions to relieve it rather than over-buying.

Map farm-gate-to-buyer/port to find where value is added (grading, drying, packing, export) and where margin leaks (shrinkage, demurrage, commission), then push the firm toward higher-margin value-add and direct sourcing.
Build a per-quintal landed-cost-to-realisation model including mandi charges, freight, shrinkage, finance cost and rejection allowance to know true net spread before committing to a buy.
Set maximum open (unhedged) inventory value and per-commodity stop-loss; decide back-to-back vs NCDEX hedge for each position to cap the price-crash downside that destroys agro traders.
Clarify who decides buy prices, approves credit, signs export docs and releases farmer payments — preventing the proprietor-bottleneck and costly documentation/compliance misses.

risk_model.risk: Adverse commodity price movement on open/unhedged inventory wiping out trading spread
risk_model.control: Buy back-to-back against confirmed orders; enforce open-position and stop-loss limits; hedge via NCDEX where liquid; mark-to-market positions daily.

risk_model.risk: Export consignment rejection for pesticide residue/aflatoxin or failed phytosanitary/quality spec
risk_model.control: Pre-shipment lab testing per buyer/destination spec, accredited fumigation, lot-level QC and APEDA-compliant documentation before dispatch.

risk_model.risk: Buyer default / receivable non-collection on credit sales
risk_model.control: Counterparty credit limits, advances/LC for export and new buyers, ECGC cover on export receivables, and Sec 43B(h) discipline on MSME payables.

risk_model.risk: GST/ITC leakage and e-way bill non-compliance from cash-heavy mandi purchases
risk_model.control: Digitise purchase capture, reconcile ITC in GST portal, raise compliant e-way bills on every movement, and minimise informal cash dealing.

risk_model.risk: Working-capital crunch / CC-limit breach at peak season choking buying
risk_model.control: Use WDRA e-NWR pledge finance against stored stock, sweat inventory turns, stagger procurement, and monitor drawing power vs RBI MSME credit norms.

risk_model.risk: Storage shrinkage, pest/moisture damage and pilferage in godown
risk_model.control: WDRA-accredited warehouse, moisture/temperature control, scheduled fumigation, stack-wise physical audits and lot-level inventory reconciliation.

risk_model.risk: Food-safety / FSSAI non-compliance on packed/branded domestic sales
risk_model.control: Maintain FSSAI licence, labelling and hygiene standards for any packed/branded product; segregate food-grade handling from bulk.

kpi_structure.definition: COGS divided by average inventory value over the period; how many times stock cycles into cash.
kpi_structure.healthy: >8x per year (12-15x for fast-moving spot trading)

kpi_structure.definition: Inventory days + receivable days - payable days; net days cash is tied up per trade.

kpi_structure.kpi: Gross trading spread per quintal / per trade
kpi_structure.definition: Net realisation minus full landed cost (mandi price + charges + freight + shrinkage + finance) per unit.
Value of consignments rejected or claimed against, as % of dispatched value.
Quantity/value lost in storage and handling vs procured, as % of throughput.
Value of inventory not backed by a confirmed sale or hedge vs the approved risk limit.

kpi_structure.kpi: CC/OD limit utilisation & interest as % of gross profit
kpi_structure.definition: Drawing-power usage and finance cost as a share of gross spread earned.

profitability_analysis.typical_net_margin: 1-3% net for pure trading; 3-6% with value-add/export after finance & shrinkage
unit_economics: Basmati rice export: landed cost ~₹6,800-7,500/quintal at mill; realisation ~₹8,000-9,000/quintal; gross spread ~₹800-1,200/quintal (~10-13%) before freight/finance
Turmeric/spice domestic lot: mandi buy ~₹14,000-16,000/quintal; resale spread ~₹500-900/quintal (~3-5%); shrinkage of 2% (~₹300) and finance cost can halve net
Pulses (tur/chana) wholesale: buy ~₹7,000-8,000/quintal, spread ~₹150-350/quintal (~2-4%) — a high-turns, thin-margin game where 10-12 turns/year makes the ROCE
profitability_analysis.working_capital_notes: Working capital is the business. Cash cycle of 45-90 days is common; peak-season procurement spikes CC utilisation. Pay farmers/FPOs fast (often advance/immediate) while buyers/exporters pay in 30-90 days (or against LC), so the firm self-funds the gap via CC/OD (10-14%) and WDRA e-NWR pledge loans. ROCE is driven by turns x thin spread minus finance cost — a 3% spread at 10 turns beats a 6% spread at 3 turns. Sec 43B(h) makes timely payment to MSME suppliers a tax issue too.
levers: Increase inventory turns — sweat the same capital more times rather than chasing fatter per-unit spreads
Shift mix toward value-add (graded/sortex/packed) and export to lift gross margin from ~3% to 8-15%
Cut finance cost via WDRA e-NWR pledge finance and tighter cash-conversion cycle
Reduce shrinkage and rejections with better moisture control, QC and lot traceability
Source direct from FPOs/farm-gate to remove arhatiya commission and improve traceability

pm_workflows.cadence: Pre-season planning + daily trading desk review
milestones: Set per-commodity buy targets, price bands and open-position/stop-loss limits
Line up FPO/mandi sourcing and confirmed buyer/export orders
Daily mark-to-market and position review against limits
Post-season trade-wise P&L and lessons review
Map cash-conversion cycle and CC/pledge utilisation
Tighten buyer credit terms and collections
Secure/renew APEDA RCMC, IEC, FSSAI as needed
Onboard CHA & freight forwarder; LC/ECGC terms agreed
Track e-BRC realisation and document turnaround time

pm_workflows.initiative: Digitisation of purchase, QC & inventory capture
milestones: Digitise mandi/FPO purchase slips with grade/moisture/weight
Lot-numbering and grade-wise inventory in system

key_activities: Assess crop arrivals, quality and seasonal price view
Decide buy against confirmed order or within risk limit
Lift stock, weighbridge intake, capture grade/moisture/foreign-matter
Assign lot numbers and release farmer/FPO payment
Match lot to domestic buyer or export contract
Pack/label, raise GST invoice + e-way bill or export docs
Collect payment / realise LC / track e-BRC
Reconcile position and book trade-wise net spread
Feed learnings into next price view

stages.focus: Discipline, books and risk control on the existing trading book
plays: Digitise purchases, GST/e-way and trade-wise P&L
Enforce open-position and stop-loss limits; buy more back-to-back
Tighten cash-conversion cycle and activate e-NWR pledge finance
Reduce rejections via inbound QC and moisture control

stages.focus: Move up the margin curve and secure supply
plays: Invest in cleaning/sortex/drying to sell graded, value-added stock
Source direct from FPOs/farm-gate to cut commission and improve traceability
Add 2-3 adjacent commodities to balance seasonality
Build private-label/packed lines for processors and brands

stages.focus: Higher-margin export channels and capital efficiency
plays: Secure APEDA RCMC + IEC, build buyer relationships in GCC/SE-Asia/Africa
Set up pre-shipment compliance + lab/fumigation tie-ups
Use ECGC/LC to de-risk export receivables and expand limits
Leverage FIEO networks and government export incentives; scale turns with data-driven price intelligence

digital_maturity_model.name: Manual / paper-and-cash
signals: Purchases recorded on mandi slips and a register
Prices via phone calls to arhatiyas
Cash-heavy dealing, year-end accounting only
No lot tracking or position view
digital_maturity_model.next_step: Digitise purchase capture and switch to GST-compliant invoicing with e-way bills.

signals: Purchases/sales in Tally/Excel
GST invoices and e-way bills generated
Basic inventory quantity tracking
Bank/CC managed manually
digital_maturity_model.next_step: Add lot-level grade/moisture tagging and a trade-wise P&L view so true spread per deal is visible.

digital_maturity_model.name: Integrated operations
signals: Lot-level inventory with grade/moisture and aging
Trade-wise profitability and CC utilisation visible
QC/lab results linked to lots
Export documentation managed on a checklist
digital_maturity_model.next_step: Connect external price feeds (eNAM/mandi/NCDEX) and start tracking open-position risk against limits.

digital_maturity_model.name: Data-driven trading
signals: Live multi-mandi/eNAM price dashboard
Open-position and cash-conversion KPIs monitored daily
Working-capital and shrinkage analytics

Automated procurement-to-order matching and document generation
