playbooks.name: Export / Import Businesses
playbooks.one_liner: An India-based export/import or merchant-trading MSME that sources goods (domestically or abroad), clears them through customs against an IEC, and resells across borders — monetising sourcing arbitrage, logistics orchestration and trade-finance, not manufacturing.

operating_model.summary: A capital-and-relationship business: the firm buys on one side (foreign supplier or domestic factory/mandi aggregator), moves goods through ports/CHA/freight, clears customs against an IEC, and sells on the other side — earning a spread plus, on exports, government incentives (RoDTEP/Duty Drawback). Cash is locked in inventory-in-transit and receivables for 60-150 days, so working-capital management and FX risk define survival more than the gross spread itself.
revenue_streams: Merchant trading spread (buy-sell margin) on exported/imported goods
Export incentives: RoDTEP scrip, Duty Drawback, RoSCTL, EPCG/Advance-Authorisation duty savings
Commission / indenting income (agent for foreign principal, no inventory risk)
Value-added services: consolidation, repacking/labelling, QC, last-mile distribution for imported brands
Trade-finance arbitrage (early-payment discounts vs LC tenor) and FX gains on favourable hedging
cost_structure: Cost of goods (60-80% of revenue) — the dominant line
Freight, ocean/air, container detention & demurrage
Customs duty/IGST on imports, CHA/clearing & forwarding fees, port/CFS charges
Bank charges: LC issuance, bill negotiation, forward-cover, FX spread, interest on packing credit/buyer's credit
Compliance & certification (FSSAI/APEDA/BIS/phytosanitary/COO), inspection & lab testing
Warehousing, insurance (marine + credit), and quality-claim/rejection provisions
value_drivers: Reliable supplier base + buyer relationships (repeat order book)
Working-capital access and cost of credit (packing credit at concessional ~7-9%)
Customs/HS-code & FTA expertise that legally minimises duty and maximises incentives
FX hedging discipline that protects the thin spread
On-time-in-full delivery and quality consistency that prevents costly rejections/claims

value_chain: Market & product selection (HS code, demand, FTA duty advantage)
Documentation (commercial invoice, packing list, COO, BL/AWB, e-BRC)
Customs clearance (shipping bill / bill of entry via ICEGATE) & CHA coordination
Payment realisation (LC negotiation / collection) & incentive claim (RoDTEP/Drawback)
Last-mile delivery / domestic distribution & after-sales / claims

core_processes.description: Build the full landed cost — FOB + freight + insurance + customs duty + IGST + clearing + finance cost — net of expected RoDTEP/drawback, to price every deal above a minimum spread and avoid loss-making orders.

Generate and reconcile commercial invoice, packing list, COO, BL/AWB, shipping bill/bill of entry on ICEGATE, e-BRC closure and incentive claim — the documentary chain that releases goods, payment and incentives.
Sequence packing credit, LC, buyer's/supplier's credit and forward FX cover against the order pipeline so cash gaps in the 90-150 day cycle are pre-funded and FX exposure is hedged.
Maintain a qualified vendor panel and a repeat-buyer order book with QC scorecards, payment-discipline tracking and claim history.

department_structure.mandate: Own the physical and documentary flow end-to-end: bookings, CHA/freight coordination, customs filing, container/demurrage control, on-time delivery.
Identify products, qualify suppliers/factories, run sampling and costing, negotiate buy-side terms and maintain the vendor panel.
Build and retain the export buyer / import-customer book, attend trade fairs, negotiate Incoterms and payment terms, manage claims.
Run the working-capital loop (packing credit/LC/forwards), FX hedging, GST/customs/DGFT compliance, e-BRC and incentive claims, and credit-risk control.

operational_bottlenecks.bottleneck: Cash locked in long trade cycle
operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Profitable on paper but always short of cash; can't take new orders without fresh limits
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Working capital cycle of 90-150 days; growth capped at bank limit; forced to refuse orders
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Advance to supplier + transit + buyer credit period all funded before realisation, with limited/expensive packing-credit and LC limits for an MSME

operational_bottlenecks.bottleneck: FX volatility eroding a thin spread
operational_bottlenecks.symptom: A deal quoted at a 6% spread turns to 2% or a loss when USD/INR moves between order and realisation
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Margin wipe-out on un-hedged exposure; unpredictable profitability
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: No hedging discipline; treating forward cover as cost rather than insurance; mismatch between invoice currency and cost currency

operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Containers stuck at port; surprise demurrage/detention bills; HS-code disputes and assessment queries
operational_bottlenecks.impact: ₹10,000-50,000+/container in avoidable charges; missed delivery windows; buyer penalties
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Incomplete/incorrect documents, wrong HS classification, over-reliance on a single CHA, and reactive (not pre-cleared) filing

operational_bottlenecks.symptom: RoDTEP/Drawback/IGST-refund claims delayed, short-paid or never filed; e-BRCs not closed
operational_bottlenecks.impact: 1-3% of export turnover (the firm's actual profit) stuck or lost in scrolls/refunds
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Manual, fragmented documentation; no reconciliation between shipping bills, BRCs and claims; weak DGFT/ICEGATE follow-up

operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Shipment rejected at destination, quality/short-shipment claims, returned/destroyed goods
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Loss of full COGS + freight both ways + reputation; insurance rarely covers quality disputes
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Weak pre-shipment QC, no third-party inspection, and over-dependence on unverified suppliers

operational_bottlenecks.symptom: One or two parties drive most volume; a buyer delays/defaults on payment with goods already shipped
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Single default can equal a year's profit; no recourse across borders
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: No ECGC credit insurance, over-reliance on open-account/DA terms, and thin vendor/buyer panel

ai_automation_opportunities.opportunity: Auto-generate and cross-validate trade document sets (invoice, packing list, COO, shipping bill data) and flag mismatches before filing on ICEGATE to prevent customs queries and demurrage
Landed-cost & quote engine that computes duty (by HS/FTA), freight, finance cost and net incentives to price every deal above a minimum spread
RoDTEP/Drawback/IGST-refund and e-BRC reconciliation tracker that matches shipping bills to BRCs to claims and chases leakage
Working-capital & FX exposure dashboard tying the order pipeline to packing-credit/LC utilisation and recommending forward-cover triggers
Buyer/supplier counterparty risk scoring (payment history, ECGC cover eligibility, country risk) to set credit terms
Market & product opportunity scanner across HS codes, FTA duty advantages and destination demand to spot new export/import lines
Container/shipment milestone and demurrage-alert tracker integrating CHA/freight status to pre-empt detention charges

consulting_frameworks.use: Map advance-to-supplier + inventory-in-transit + receivable days minus payable days to size the funding gap and target the single biggest lever in this business — DSO and inventory turns.
Pinpoint where this trader actually adds value (sourcing, compliance, finance, logistics orchestration) vs where it merely passes goods through, to defend margin against disintermediation.
Treat each deal/container as a unit: landed cost, spread, finance cost, incentives, and demurrage risk, to set minimum-margin and minimum-order-value rules.
Identify the binding constraint — usually the bank credit limit or customs throughput — and route improvement effort there rather than to non-bottleneck activities.
Quantify FX, counterparty, regulatory and freight risks by severity x likelihood and net long/short currency positions before deciding hedge ratio and ECGC cover.
Assign clear ownership across sourcing, ops, CHA and finance for each document and customs step so nothing falls between desks and triggers a customs query.

risk_model.risk: FX rate movement between order and realisation wipes out the spread
risk_model.control: Mandatory forward-cover above an exposure threshold; match invoice currency to cost currency; weekly net-exposure review

risk_model.risk: Buyer default / non-payment on open-account or DA terms across borders
risk_model.control: ECGC credit insurance, LC or advance for new/high-value buyers, counterparty credit scoring and limits

risk_model.risk: Customs misclassification, valuation dispute, demurrage & detention
risk_model.control: Pre-validate HS code & valuation, AEO accreditation, multi-CHA panel, document checklist before filing on ICEGATE

risk_model.risk: IEC/DGFT non-compliance, scheme misuse (EPCG/Advance-Authorisation export-obligation default)
risk_model.control: Track export-obligation timelines, maintain IEC validity & AD-code registration, periodic DGFT compliance audit

risk_model.risk: Sector certification failure for agro/food exports (rejection at destination)
risk_model.control: APEDA registration, FSSAI compliance, accredited lab testing & phytosanitary certificates before shipment

risk_model.risk: GST/IGST refund and e-BRC mismatch blocking incentive realisation and ITC
risk_model.control: Reconcile shipping bills, BRCs and GSTR filings monthly; LUT for zero-rated exports; automated refund tracking

risk_model.risk: Quality rejection / claim with goods already in transit or abroad
risk_model.control: Third-party pre-shipment inspection, supplier QC scorecards, marine + claims insurance, retention on supplier payment

kpi_structure.definition: (Sell price - full landed cost) / sell price, per deal/container
Supplier-advance + inventory-in-transit + receivable days - payable days
Share of open foreign-currency receivables/payables covered by forwards
RoDTEP/Drawback/IGST refunds actually received vs eligible
Avoidable port/container charges as share of freight spend
Shipments delivered complete and on schedule vs buyer commitment
Revenue (or purchases) from the single largest counterparty

unit_economics: Per 20ft container of mid-value goods: revenue ~₹25-40 lakh, landed cost ~₹22-35 lakh, gross spread ~₹2-4 lakh (8-12%); finance + demurrage + claims erode ₹0.8-1.5 lakh, leaving net ~₹1-2.5 lakh
Export incentives (RoDTEP ~0.5-2% + Drawback) typically add ₹15,000-60,000 per ₹25 lakh shipment — often the difference between net profit and break-even
Packing-credit interest at ~8% over a 100-day cycle costs ~2.2% of order value — a direct charge against the spread
profitability_analysis.working_capital_notes: This is a working-capital-intensive business: ₹90-150 of cash is tied up per ₹100 of monthly revenue. Growth is gated by sanctioned bank limits (packing credit, LC, buyer's credit), not by demand. Every extra day of DSO or transit directly consumes the limit and the margin. Sec 43B(h) 45-day payment rule to MSME suppliers further tightens payable timing. ECGC cover can unlock higher bank limits against insured receivables.
levers: Maximise incentive capture (RoDTEP/Drawback/IGST refund) — 1-3% of turnover that is pure margin
Shorten cash conversion cycle via shorter buyer terms, LC at sight, and faster customs clearance (AEO)
Disciplined FX hedging to protect the quoted spread
Reduce demurrage/detention through pre-cleared documentation and CHA diversification
Move up the value chain (repacking, branding, distribution) to escape pure-spread commoditisation

pm_workflows.cadence: Per order, with daily ops standup

milestones: Order pipeline mapped to funding need
Shipping bill vs BRC vs claim matched

key_activities: Product/market selection by HS code & FTA advantage

stages.focus: Get the rails right: IEC, AD-code, GST/LUT, first reliable supplier-buyer pair, basic packing-credit limit
plays: Register IEC, RCMC (FIEO/EPC) and Udyam; open AD-code with bank
Win 2-3 repeat buyers via referrals and a focused trade fair
Lock LC/advance payment terms to avoid early default risk
Build a simple landed-cost calculator and minimum-spread rule

stages.focus: Expand limits, diversify counterparties, professionalise compliance and incentive capture
plays: Negotiate higher packing-credit/LC limits backed by ECGC cover
Diversify to 5-8 buyers and a vendor panel to cut concentration
Institutionalise FX hedging and incentive reconciliation
Add 1-2 adjacent product lines using existing buyer relationships
Pursue AEO accreditation for faster customs clearance

stages.focus: Move up the value chain — value-add, own brand/distribution, or backward integration
plays: Add warehousing, repacking/labelling and last-mile distribution for imports
Consider EPCG/Advance-Authorisation for duty-saving on capital/inputs
Build a treasury function and structured trade-finance (buyer's/supplier's credit)
Develop own brand or exclusive distributorship to escape pure-spread commoditisation
Geographic and currency diversification to de-risk single-market exposure

digital_maturity_model.name: Manual / paper
signals: Documents in Word/Excel re-typed per shipment
Costing on ad-hoc spreadsheets, errors common
No central record of shipments, BRCs or claims
Compliance dates tracked in memory or diary
digital_maturity_model.next_step: Adopt a shared shipment tracker and standard document templates to stop re-keying and lost claims

digital_maturity_model.name: Digitised records
signals: Centralised shipment & document register in cloud sheets
Standard landed-cost template reused
ICEGATE/DGFT portals used for filing
Basic bank-portal use for LC/packing credit
digital_maturity_model.next_step: Connect documents to a system so invoice, packing list and customs data auto-populate from one order record

digital_maturity_model.name: Integrated systems
signals: EXIM/ERP module links order to documents to finance
Incentive & BRC reconciliation tracked systematically
FX exposure and limit utilisation visible in a dashboard
QC and CHA milestones logged against each shipment
digital_maturity_model.next_step: Layer analytics — margin-by-deal, DSO, demurrage and incentive-leakage reporting to drive decisions

digital_maturity_model.name: Data-driven
signals: Real-time dashboards on cash cycle, spread, hedge ratio, OTIF
Counterparty credit scoring informs payment terms
Automated alerts for demurrage, EO deadlines, refund delays
Demand/price signals inform sourcing decisions
digital_maturity_model.next_step: Introduce AI agents to auto-validate documents, recommend hedges and pricing, and chase incentive leakage

digital_maturity_model.name: AI-native
signals: AI auto-generates and cross-checks trade documents pre-filing
Quote engine prices deals with live duty/FX/incentive data
Predictive working-capital & FX hedging recommendations
Autonomous incentive/refund reconciliation and counterparty-risk monitoring
digital_maturity_model.next_step: Continuously expand agent autonomy and feed outcomes back to improve pricing, risk and sourcing models

playbooks.name: Logistics & Warehousing
playbooks.one_liner: An Indian MSME logistics & warehousing operator moves and stores goods — running owned/attached truck fleets, full-truckload (FTL) and part-load (PTL) freight, last-mile delivery, and shared/cold-storage warehouses — typically as a 3PL or transport contractor serving manufacturers, distributors, e-commerce and FMCG clients across Tier-1/2/3 India.

operating_model.summary: Asset-light-to-medium 3PL/transporter model: revenue from per-km/per-trip freight, per-pallet/sq-ft warehouse rent and value-added handling, while the cost base is dominated by diesel, driver wages, toll, vehicle EMI/lease and warehouse rent. Margins are thin and volume-driven; profitability is won on truck utilisation, return-load (backhaul) fill, fuel/toll efficiency and tight receivables. Most operators run a mix of owned trucks and attached/market vehicles to flex capacity against seasonal demand (festive, harvest, e-com sale events).
revenue_streams: FTL freight (per trip / per km, lane-based rate cards) for manufacturers and traders
PTL & parcel/last-mile delivery (per kg / per shipment / per drop) for e-commerce, FMCG and D2C
Warehouse storage rent (per sq-ft or per pallet per month) + handling/in-out, VAS like kitting, labelling, repacking
Cold-chain / reefer movement and frozen-storage premium (pharma, dairy, frozen foods, fresh produce)
Ancillary: detention/demurrage charges, fuel surcharge pass-through, insurance markup, FASTag/toll recovery
cost_structure: Diesel/fuel (35-50% of trip cost) and toll/FASTag
Driver + cleaner wages, batta (trip allowance), and statutory labour cost
Vehicle EMI/lease, depreciation, tyres, maintenance & breakdown
Warehouse rent, racking, MHE (forklift/reach truck), power (esp. cold-store refrigeration)
Attached-vehicle / market-load hire payouts, broker commissions, GST + e-way/e-invoice compliance overhead, insurance and claims
value_drivers: Truck utilisation % and return-load (backhaul) fill rate — empty kms kill margin
Lane density / network effect — repeatable high-volume lanes lower per-trip cost
On-time delivery (OTIF) and low damage/shrinkage — wins contract renewals & premium rates
Receivables discipline (DSO) — freight is sold on 30-90 day credit, working capital is the real constraint
Warehouse throughput per sq-ft and dock-to-stock cycle time

value_chain: Demand capture / load booking (client indent, lane, rate negotiation)
Capacity planning & vehicle allocation (owned vs attached, route/lane matching)
Order/trip documentation (LR/consignment note, e-way bill, e-invoice, GST)
Dispatch & in-transit tracking (GPS, FASTag, driver/POD coordination)
Warehouse inbound: gate-in, unloading, QC, put-away (FEFO/FIFO)
Storage & inventory management (bin/pallet locations, stock accuracy)
Outbound: pick-pack, staging, loading, last-mile dispatch

core_processes.description: From indent to closure: rate confirmation, vehicle allocation, LR + e-way bill generation, GPS-tracked transit, POD capture, and trip-cost reconciliation (diesel, toll, batta, attached-vehicle payout) to compute true per-trip margin.
Inbound gate-in/QC/put-away, location-based storage with FEFO/FIFO, pick-pack-dispatch, cycle counting and stock-accuracy reconciliation; tracks throughput, dwell time and shrinkage per SKU/client.
Consolidate trips/PODs into client invoices, apply fuel/detention surcharges, raise GST e-invoices, and drive collections against 30-90 day terms with ageing follow-up to protect working capital.

Maintain owned-vehicle health (service schedule, tyres, fitness/permit/insurance renewals, driver roster) and broker the attached/market-vehicle pool to flex against demand peaks at controlled hire rates.

department_structure.mandate: Plan capacity, allocate vehicles, match return loads, track transit and ensure OTIF; the profit engine of the business.
Run inbound, storage, outbound and VAS to SLA with high stock accuracy and low shrinkage; manage MHE and cold-chain integrity.
Win lanes and warehouse contracts, negotiate rate cards, retain key accounts and grow share-of-wallet.
Trip costing, freight invoicing, GST/e-way/e-invoice compliance, collections/DSO, payroll and statutory filings.
Vehicle uptime, service/tyre/diesel procurement, spares, and attached-vehicle vendor management.
Recruit/retain scarce drivers, manage attendance, batta/wages, safety, training and statutory labour compliance.

operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Trucks return empty or wait days for a return load; per-trip margin collapses on one-way lanes.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: 20-40% of running kms unbilled; effective revenue per truck drops sharply, especially on non-industrial corridors.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Fragmented load market and lack of a return-load network/visibility; over-reliance on brokers and manual phone-based load matching.

operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Freight billed on 60-90 day credit while diesel, toll, driver batta and EMIs are paid in cash daily/weekly.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Chronic cash-flow stress; operators borrow at high rates or delay vendor/driver payments; growth is self-throttled.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Weak credit terms vs large shippers, slow POD-to-invoice cycle, and no disciplined ageing/collections process; MSME bargaining weakness.

operational_bottlenecks.bottleneck: Driver shortage, turnover and trust gaps
operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Trucks idle for want of drivers; frequent absenteeism, diesel/route pilferage and accident exposure.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Asset utilisation falls, insurance/claim costs rise, customer SLAs missed during peak.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Hard working conditions, low formalisation, cash-based batta culture, and absence of telematics-based monitoring.

operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Manual LRs, late/incorrect e-way bills, detention at checkpoints, mismatched invoices and ITC blockage.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Delays, penalties, vehicle detention, and lost input-tax credit eroding thin margins.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Paper/Excel-based processes, no TMS integration with the GST/e-way portal, and low digital literacy on the ground.

operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Temperature excursions, reefer breakdowns, and product spoilage/shrinkage in fresh/pharma loads.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Rejected consignments, claims, FSSAI/pharma compliance exposure and lost premium clients.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Ageing reefer assets, no continuous temperature telemetry/alerting, power outages at warehouses, and weak SOP discipline.

operational_bottlenecks.bottleneck: Fragmented systems & no single source of truth
operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Dispatch in WhatsApp/Excel, billing in Tally, tracking on separate GPS apps; reconciliation done manually month-end.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Trip-level profitability is invisible until too late; leakage in diesel, detention and attached-vehicle payouts goes uncaught.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: No integrated TMS/WMS; tools bought piecemeal; data never joined to compute true unit economics.

ai_automation_opportunities.opportunity: AI load-matching & return-load (backhaul) optimiser that scans booked one-way trips and suggests return loads/lanes to slash empty kms and lift per-truck revenue.
Automated e-way bill + e-invoice generation from the trip/LR record, with validity and lane checks to eliminate detention penalties and ITC mismatches.
Receivables/DSO copilot that auto-ages freight invoices, links POD-to-invoice, and triggers tiered collection nudges to compress the cash cycle.
Trip-cost & lane-profitability analytics that reconciles diesel, toll/FASTag, batta and attached-vehicle payouts per trip to expose loss-making lanes and leakage.
WMS automation: barcode/QR put-away with FEFO/FIFO logic, cycle-count scheduling and shrinkage alerts for warehouse and cold-store stock accuracy.
Cold-chain telemetry agent that ingests reefer/warehouse temperature feeds, predicts excursions and auto-escalates before spoilage, with FSSAI/pharma audit logs.
SOP generation for warehouse and transit safety, driver onboarding and incident handling to standardise operations across branches.
Sales/tendering copilot that builds lane rate cards, RFQ responses and key-account QBR decks to win and renew 3PL contracts.

consulting_frameworks.use: Identify the binding constraint — usually truck/driver availability or dock throughput — and subordinate scheduling to it; exploit the constraint (e.g. maximise return-load fill) before adding capacity.
Map diesel-and-batta cash-out vs 60-90 day freight cash-in; target POD-to-invoice and DSO reduction as the primary lever for survival and self-funded growth.
Compute contribution per trip and per sq-ft after diesel, toll, driver and payout costs to price lanes correctly and kill loss-making business.
Decompose booking-to-collection to find margin leakage points (empty running, detention not billed, ITC lost) and where VAS can add billable value.
Clarify ownership across dispatch, warehouse, billing and compliance so e-way bills, PODs and collections never fall through cracks during peaks.
Track on-time-in-full per client and lane as the contract-renewal and premium-pricing driver; tie ops incentives to it.
Rank digitisation initiatives (TMS, WMS, telematics, e-way automation) by Reach, Impact, Confidence, Effort to sequence the transformation roadmap.

risk_model.risk: E-way bill / e-invoice non-compliance causing detention, penalty and ITC loss
risk_model.control: TMS-integrated auto e-way/e-invoice generation with validity tracking; reconcile GSTR-2B for ITC monthly.

risk_model.risk: Chronic receivables stretch / customer default eroding working capital
risk_model.control: Credit limits per client, POD-linked invoicing within 48h, ageing-based collections, invoice discounting/TReDS; invoke MSMED 45-day payment protection.

risk_model.risk: Goods damage, theft or in-transit loss claims
risk_model.control: Adequate goods-in-transit & marine cum warehouse insurance, GPS tracking, sealed/locked vehicles, POD discipline and clear liability clauses in contracts.

risk_model.risk: Cold-chain temperature excursion / spoilage and food-safety breach
risk_model.control: Continuous temperature telemetry with alerts, reefer preventive maintenance, backup power, FSSAI-compliant SOPs and audit logs.

risk_model.risk: Driver/labour disputes and statutory non-compliance (wages, PF/ESI, safety)
risk_model.control: Formal employment/contracts, EPF/ESI enrolment, batta-on-record, driver safety training and labour-code adherence.

risk_model.risk: Fuel price volatility & toll cost squeezing thin margins
risk_model.control: Fuel-surcharge pass-through clauses in rate cards, FASTag/route optimisation, and quarterly rate-card resets indexed to diesel.

risk_model.risk: Vehicle permit/fitness/insurance lapse and overloading penalties
risk_model.control: Renewal calendar for permits/fitness/PUC/insurance, axle-load compliance checks, and Udyam-registered formalisation for credit access.

kpi_structure.definition: Share of running kilometres that are revenue-generating vs empty/positioning.
% of trips that secured a paying return load.
Deliveries completed on time and in full per client/lane.
Average days to collect freight invoices.
System vs physical stock match at cycle count.
Freight revenue minus diesel, toll, batta and payout per trip.
% of reefer trips/storage hours with temperature breach.

unit_economics: FTL 32-ft multi-axle, ~₹55-75/km billed; diesel+toll+driver ≈ ₹40-55/km, leaving ₹8-15/km contribution if return load secured (near-zero if empty).
Warehouse: ₹18-35/sq-ft/month rent realised vs ₹8-15/sq-ft cost (rent+power+labour); cold storage commands ₹2-4/kg/month premium with higher power cost.
Last-mile parcel: ₹25-60 per drop in Tier-1; viable only above ~25-30 drops/route/day.
A single owned 32-ft truck: ~₹2.5-3.5 lakh/month revenue at good utilisation; EMI+fixed ≈ ₹0.9-1.3 lakh/month.
profitability_analysis.working_capital_notes: Working capital is THE constraint: diesel, toll, batta and EMIs are cash-out within days while freight collects in 60-90 days, creating a 30-75 day funding gap. Festive/harvest peaks spike attached-vehicle hire (paid faster than clients pay). Levers: POD-to-invoice <48h, TReDS/invoice discounting, fuel-surcharge pass-through, and advance/milestone billing for warehouse contracts. MSMED Act 45-day clause is a legal lever against delayed-paying buyers.
levers: Lift return-load fill and lane density to cut empty kms (biggest margin lever)
Compress DSO via POD-linked invoicing and TReDS/invoice discounting
Pass through diesel/toll via surcharge clauses and quarterly rate resets
Shift idle owned fleet toward asset-light attached model in low-density lanes
Add high-margin VAS (kitting, labelling, cold storage, reverse logistics) to warehouse contracts
Telematics to cut diesel pilferage, idling and maintenance cost

milestones: Select/configure TMS with GST e-way/e-invoice integration

pm_workflows.cadence: Weekly collections war-room for first quarter

milestones: Analyse one-way vs round-trip lane data
Identify anchor return lanes & partner transporters/load boards
Pilot return-load matching on top 5 lanes

pm_workflows.cadence: Phased per site, monthly stock-accuracy audit

key_activities: Design network (lanes, warehouse footprint, fleet mix)
Build rate card & contract with fuel/detention clauses
Set up master data, EDI/portal integration, KYC
Secure owned vs attached vehicle mix
Hire/train drivers & warehouse staff, deploy SOPs

stages.focus: Survive on cash flow; master core lanes and a few anchor clients.
plays: Get Udyam + GST registered to access formal credit & contracts
Lock 2-3 anchor clients on repeat lanes for utilisation
Move dispatch/billing off paper to a basic TMS + Tally
Enforce POD-to-invoice discipline to protect cash

stages.focus: Build lane density, add warehousing/VAS, formalise systems.
plays: Add shared-warehouse + VAS to deepen client wallet share
Build return-load network to lift utilisation
Adopt integrated TMS+WMS and telematics
Onboard TReDS/invoice discounting to fund growth
Hire key-account managers for contract renewals

stages.focus: Network effects, specialisation premium, and capital efficiency.
plays: Specialise (cold-chain/pharma/e-com) for premium margins
Asset-light scaling via vetted attached-fleet & franchise hubs
Data-driven pricing & lane optimisation at scale
Pursue large enterprise/anchor 3PL contracts & RFPs
Consider PE/NBFC growth capital and investor-readiness

digital_maturity_model.name: Manual / paper
signals: Hand-written LRs and registers
Dispatch coordinated by phone/WhatsApp
Billing in Excel; PODs in physical files
Trip profitability unknown until month-end (if at all)
digital_maturity_model.next_step: Adopt Tally + a basic spreadsheet trip-and-collections tracker; standardise the LR and POD process.

digital_maturity_model.name: Basic digital records
signals: Accounting in Tally; GST filed via CA
Some GPS tracking on owned trucks
E-way bills generated manually on the portal
Customer-wise ledgers maintained
digital_maturity_model.next_step: Implement a TMS for trip lifecycle and integrate e-way/e-invoice generation to remove manual portal work.

digital_maturity_model.name: Integrated TMS/WMS
signals: TMS covers booking-to-billing; WMS runs the warehouse with bin locations
Auto e-way/e-invoice from trip records
Fleet-wide GPS/telematics dashboards
DSO and OTIF tracked on dashboards
digital_maturity_model.next_step: Join TMS+WMS+telematics+finance data into one source of truth and start trip/lane profitability analytics.

digital_maturity_model.name: Data-driven operations
signals: Single integrated data layer across ops, fleet, warehouse & finance
Lane-level profitability and utilisation analytics live
Cold-chain telemetry with alerts
ePOD and automated collections workflows
digital_maturity_model.next_step: Layer AI/ML on the data for predictive load-matching, dynamic pricing and proactive cold-chain/maintenance alerts.

digital_maturity_model.name: AI-native logistics
signals: AI backhaul/load-matching minimising empty kms
Dynamic lane pricing and demand forecasting
Predictive maintenance & route optimisation
Autonomous compliance (e-way/e-invoice/ITC) and AI collections copilot
digital_maturity_model.next_step: Continuously retrain models on network data and extend AI to multi-party network/partner optimisation and self-serve client portals.

playbooks.name: D2C Brands
playbooks.one_liner: A direct-to-consumer brand that designs and sells its own physical products to Indian consumers across its own Shopify/website, marketplaces (Amazon, Flipkart, Nykaa) and quick-commerce (Blinkit, Zepto, Instamart), owning the customer, data and margin instead of routing through traditional distribution.

operating_model.summary: An asset-light brand company: product is designed in-house and made by third-party contract manufacturers (private-label), sold across own-website + marketplaces + quick-commerce + emerging retail, fulfilled via 3PL/dark stores, with demand manufactured by paid performance media (Meta/Google), influencers and content. Profit is decided by the spread between blended contribution margin and blended CAC, constrained by working capital locked in inventory and marketplace receivables.
revenue_streams: Own website / Shopify D2C sales — highest margin, full first-party data and customer ownership
Marketplace sales — Amazon, Flipkart, Myntra, Nykaa — high volume but lower margin after commission and fees
Quick-commerce — Blinkit, Zepto, Swiggy Instamart — impulse and repeat velocity, high margin share to platform
Offline general/modern trade once the brand scales — distributor-led, lower margin
Subscriptions / replenishment and bundles for consumables (nutrition, coffee, personal care)
B2B and corporate gifting plus exports — incremental, higher AOV
cost_structure: COGS — landed product cost from contract manufacturer incl. packaging, typically 30-45% of net selling price
Performance marketing / ad spend (Meta, Google, marketplace ads) — largest variable cost, 20-40% of revenue at early scale
Marketplace commissions, fulfilment and closing fees (Amazon/Flipkart 12-30%; quick-commerce margin share 25-45%)
Logistics and fulfilment — 3PL pick-pack, forward shipping and RTO/return shipping (₹60-120 per shipment)
Payment gateway + COD handling charges (2-3%)
Team — performance marketing, brand/content, ops, support; plus influencer/creator payouts
Inventory carrying cost and write-offs/expiry (esp. F&B and cosmetics with FSSAI shelf-life)
value_drivers: Repeat rate and LTV — repeat revenue carries near-zero CAC and is what makes the model profitable
Blended contribution margin after all variable costs (CM2/CM3) — the true unit-economics number
First-party data and retention engine (email/WhatsApp/CRM) to cut dependence on paid acquisition
Brand equity and differentiation that holds price and lowers CAC over time
Channel-mix discipline — shifting volume toward own-site and repeat vs expensive marketplace acquisition
Working-capital velocity — inventory turns and marketplace payout cycle

value_chain: Consumer insight & product development (formulation/design, CM sourcing, sampling)
Sourcing & contract manufacturing (private-label PO, QC, packaging, FSSAI/BIS compliance)
Inventory planning & inbound to 3PL / dark stores / marketplace FCs (FBA, Flipkart FA)
Demand generation (performance ads, influencer, content, SEO, marketplace ads)
Listing & merchandising across own-site + marketplaces + quick-commerce
Post-purchase: support, reviews, retention/CRM, repeat & subscription

core_processes.description: Daily budget pacing, ROAS/MER monitoring, creative testing, campaign scaling/cutting across Meta, Google and marketplace ads; the CAC engine of the business.
Forecast SKU-level demand, place CM purchase orders against lead times, allocate stock across own-3PL, FBA and quick-commerce dark stores to avoid stockouts and overstock.
Order routing to nearest 3PL, pick-pack-ship, courier allocation, COD reconciliation and marketplace payout reconciliation.
RTO prediction and prevention (address/pincode scoring, COD-to-prepaid nudges), reverse logistics, QC of returns, restocking vs write-off.
Email/WhatsApp/SMS flows, win-back, subscription, reviews and referral to lift repeat rate and LTV.
Keeping titles, images, A+ content, pricing, ratings and buy-box healthy across every channel with consistent MRP and offer hygiene.

department_structure.mandate: Acquire customers profitably — own blended CAC, ROAS/MER, marketplace ads and the acquisition P&L.
Build brand equity and a creative engine that lowers CAC — UGC, influencer, design, social and content.
Source, plan and fulfil — CM management, inventory planning, 3PL, logistics, returns/RTO.
Own the storefront, listings, conversion-rate optimisation and channel merchandising across all platforms.
Drive repeat, LTV and CSAT — CRM lifecycle, subscriptions, reviews and support/WhatsApp.
Unit economics, cash-flow/working capital, GST/marketplace reconciliation, FSSAI/BIS compliance and investor reporting.

operational_bottlenecks.symptom: ROAS falling each quarter, MER below 3, growth stalls the moment ad spend is cut, CAC payback stretching past 12 months.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Contribution margin erodes to zero or negative; the brand grows revenue but burns cash and cannot reach profitability.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Over-reliance on Meta/Google for first-purchase acquisition, weak repeat/retention engine, undifferentiated product, and creative fatigue as ad auctions get more competitive in India.

operational_bottlenecks.symptom: 20-40% of COD orders returned-to-origin, reverse-logistics costs, damaged/unsellable returned stock, cash blocked.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Each RTO destroys unit economics — forward + reverse shipping + handling with zero revenue; can wipe out the margin of 2-3 good orders.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: High COD share in Tier-2/3 India, no address/pincode risk scoring, no prepaid incentives, poor delivery-promise accuracy and impulse cancellations.

operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Bestsellers stock out (lost sales, lost buy-box/ranking) while slow SKUs and near-expiry stock pile up across 3PL, FBA and dark stores.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Stockouts kill ranking and momentum; overstock locks working capital and forces markdowns/write-offs (acute for FSSAI shelf-life products).
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Long CM lead times, multi-channel stock fragmentation, no SKU-level forecasting, and demand spikes from campaigns/quick-commerce that planning can't absorb.

operational_bottlenecks.bottleneck: Working-capital squeeze from marketplace payout cycles
operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Cash tied up in inventory plus 7-30 day marketplace/quick-commerce payment cycles; struggle to fund the next inventory + ad cycle.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Growth is throttled by cash, not demand; founders take expensive revenue-based or NBFC financing, compressing margins further.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Inventory paid upfront to CM, receivables stuck with marketplaces/QC platforms, and ad spend that must be funded before revenue lands.

operational_bottlenecks.symptom: GST mismatches, unreconciled marketplace settlements, hidden fees/short-payments, undetected ad waste — true per-channel profit is unknown.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Brand thinks it is profitable but is leaking margin via fees, RTO and ad waste it cannot see; decisions made on revenue not contribution.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Fragmented data across Shopify, Amazon, Flipkart, QC, 3PL and payment gateways with manual spreadsheet reconciliation and no unified CM dashboard.

operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Marketplace sellers undercut own-site, broken offer hygiene, lost buy-box, eroded brand-direct margin.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Cannibalises the highest-margin channel (own website) and trains customers to wait for marketplace discounts.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Unauthorised/grey sellers, inconsistent MRP and promo governance across channels, and no MAP (minimum advertised price) enforcement.

ai_automation_opportunities.opportunity: Automated daily creative + campaign performance analysis across Meta/Google/marketplace ads with recommendations to scale, cut or refresh creatives — turning the growth team's morning audit into an AI brief.

AI-driven RTO/COD risk scoring at checkout — predict high-risk orders by pincode/address/behaviour and auto-trigger prepaid nudges, address confirmation on WhatsApp, or COD-to-prepaid conversion before shipping.
SKU-level demand forecasting and reorder-point automation across own-3PL, FBA and quick-commerce dark stores to cut stockouts and overstock/expiry.
Automated multi-channel settlement and GST reconciliation — matching Shopify/Amazon/Flipkart/QC payouts, fees and TCS to surface short-payments and per-channel true contribution margin.
AI customer support over WhatsApp/email/chat for order status, returns, WISMO and product Q&A, deflecting the bulk of repetitive tickets and triaging the rest.
Retention/CRM lifecycle automation — AI-segmented win-back, replenishment and cross-sell flows on email/WhatsApp to lift repeat rate and LTV with no incremental CAC.
Competitor and category price/listing intelligence — track competitor pricing, offers, ratings and ad presence on marketplaces and quick-commerce to guide pricing and positioning.
Automated GST + e-invoice/e-way bill and FSSAI/BIS compliance tracking for a multi-state marketplace seller (TCS, multiple GSTINs/FC states, label compliance).

consulting_frameworks.framework: Unit economics / contribution-margin waterfall (CM1 → CM2 → CM3)
consulting_frameworks.use: Decompose price → COGS → CM1, then subtract shipping/RTO/fees → CM2, then ad spend → CM3 to find the real per-order profit and where margin leaks by channel.
Govern acquisition spend — keep blended LTV:CAC ≥ 3:1 and CAC payback < 12 months; decide how aggressively to scale paid vs invest in retention.
Track repeat rate and revenue by acquisition cohort/channel to value customers properly and prove the retention engine is improving over time.

consulting_frameworks.framework: Channel-mix / portfolio (own-site vs marketplace vs quick-commerce vs offline)
consulting_frameworks.use: Optimise the blend for contribution margin and data ownership, not just topline — shift volume toward the channels that actually make money.
Map inventory days + marketplace receivable days − supplier payable days to size the cash gap and plan inventory + ad cycles without running dry.
Identify the current binding constraint — cash, CAC, RTO, or fulfilment capacity — and focus the whole org on it rather than optimising everywhere.
AARRR to instrument acquisition→activation→retention→revenue→referral; RICE to prioritise growth experiments (creatives, offers, channels) by reach/impact/confidence/effort.
Anchor product development and positioning on the real consumer job, driving differentiation that lowers CAC and lifts repeat.

risk_model.risk: CAC inflation outpaces contribution margin — paid-acquisition treadmill leads to negative unit economics and cash burn.
risk_model.control: Govern by blended LTV:CAC ≥ 3:1 and CAC payback < 12 months; cap discretionary ad spend to a MER floor; build retention/repeat to lower blended CAC.

risk_model.risk: Working-capital crunch — cash locked in inventory + marketplace receivables stalls growth and forces expensive financing.
risk_model.control: Manage cash-conversion cycle, hold inventory turns > 4-6x, negotiate CM credit terms, and use early-settlement/RBI-regulated MSME credit prudently.

risk_model.risk: High RTO/returns (COD) destroy per-order economics, especially in Tier-2/3 markets.
risk_model.control: RTO risk-scoring, prepaid incentives, address verification on WhatsApp, courier performance tracking and a returns QC/restock workflow.

risk_model.risk: GST / marketplace TCS and multi-state compliance errors (multiple GSTINs for FC states, e-invoice, e-way bill, ITC mismatches).
risk_model.control: Automated marketplace settlement-to-GST reconciliation, register GSTIN in every FC/dark-store state, e-invoice + e-way bill discipline and monthly ITC matching.

risk_model.risk: FSSAI / BIS / labelling non-compliance for F&B, nutrition, cosmetics and electronics — listings delisted, penalties, recalls.
risk_model.control: Hold valid FSSAI licence and BIS marks where applicable; legal-metrology compliant labels (MRP, net qty, mfg/expiry, importer); pre-launch label review.

risk_model.risk: Platform/channel concentration — over-dependence on one marketplace or one ad platform (algorithm/policy change, account suspension, ad-cost spike).
risk_model.control: Diversify across own-site + marketplaces + quick-commerce + retention; grow first-party/own-site share; keep account-health and policy compliance strong.

risk_model.risk: Inventory obsolescence / expiry write-offs from over-forecasting or trend-driven SKUs.
risk_model.control: SKU-level forecasting, FEFO for dated stock, ABC analysis, markdown/clearance plans and conservative reorder on long-tail SKUs.

risk_model.risk: Brand/IP and counterfeit/grey-market risk — trademark not secured, copycats and unauthorised sellers undercutting price.
risk_model.control: Register trademark, enrol in marketplace brand registry, enforce MAP and seller authorisation, monitor listings and issue takedowns.

kpi_structure.definition: Lifetime gross-margin per customer ÷ blended customer acquisition cost across all channels.
Months of contribution margin needed to recover the cost of acquiring a customer.
Net revenue minus COGS, shipping, RTO, fees and ad spend, as a % of revenue.
Total revenue ÷ total marketing spend (marketing efficiency ratio).
% of customers who purchase again within the window — proxy for retention strength.
% of orders returned-to-origin plus customer returns (weighted heavily by COD).
Annual COGS ÷ average inventory — how fast stock converts to sales.
% of orders paid online (prepaid) vs COD — drives RTO and cash velocity.

profitability_analysis.typical_gross_margin: 55-70% (on own-site net of COGS+packaging; lower on marketplace/QC after fees)
profitability_analysis.typical_net_margin: -15% to +8% (most early/mid-scale Indian D2C run negative-to-thin until retention kicks in)
unit_economics: Example AOV ₹800: COGS ₹280 (35%) → CM1 ₹520; minus shipping+RTO+payment+fees ₹160 → CM2 ₹360 (45%); minus CAC ₹300 → CM3 ₹60 (≈7.5%) on a first order — profit only emerges on repeat orders that carry no CAC.
Blended CAC ₹250-500 per customer at early scale; first-order contribution often barely covers it, so LTV across 2-4 repeat orders is what makes the customer profitable.
Marketplace order of same ₹800 AOV: after ~20-30% commission+fulfilment+TCS, CM2 can fall to ₹200-250 (25-30%), making own-site the structurally more profitable channel.
profitability_analysis.working_capital_notes: Cash is the binding constraint. Inventory is paid upfront to the contract manufacturer (often 30-60 day lead time), marketplace/quick-commerce pay out in 7-30 days, and ad spend is funded before revenue lands — creating a cash gap that funds growth. Target inventory turns > 4-6x, push prepaid share up, negotiate CM credit terms, and keep DSO from marketplaces tight. RBI-regulated MSME/NBFC and revenue-based financing can bridge the gap but compress margin if overused.
levers: Lift repeat rate / LTV via retention CRM (email/WhatsApp/subscription) — cheapest margin gain available
Shift channel mix toward own-site and high-margin SKUs; reduce reliance on discount-heavy marketplace volume
Cut RTO via prepaid incentives and risk-scoring — directly recovers destroyed margin
Improve creative + targeting efficiency to lower blended CAC and raise MER
Negotiate COGS down with CM at scale (volume) and reduce packaging cost; raise AOV via bundles/upsell
Tighten working-capital cycle — inventory turns, CM credit, faster payouts, higher prepaid share

pm_workflows.initiative: Weekly growth experiment sprint (creatives, offers, channels, landing pages)
milestones: Read results, kill or scale, document learning
PO placement against CM lead times

pm_workflows.initiative: Quarterly channel expansion (new marketplace / quick-commerce / offline)

key_activities: Create listings + A+ content + creative across channels

stages.focus: Prove a repeatable, ranged product and positive first-order or near-term unit economics on one or two channels.
plays: Nail one hero product and JTBD-led positioning
Validate on own-site + one marketplace
Build review/social proof and an early creative library
Instrument unit economics (CM waterfall) from day one

stages.focus: Make acquisition profitable and repeatable while standing up retention so blended CAC falls.
plays: Systematic creative-testing engine on Meta/Google
Stand up retention CRM (email/WhatsApp/subscription)
Tighten RTO and prepaid share
S&OP discipline to stop stockouts/overstock
Reconcile per-channel contribution margin

stages.focus: Diversify channels and de-risk, push toward profitability and prepare for capital/offline.
plays: Expand into quick-commerce and modern/general trade
Geographic + range expansion (and exports where relevant)
Build brand to structurally lower CAC
Fund growth with working-capital discipline and selective capital
Investor-grade reporting and cohort/LTV reporting

digital_maturity_model.name: Manual / spreadsheet
signals: Orders and inventory tracked in Excel/WhatsApp
No unified view of CAC or margin
Manual marketplace and GST reconciliation
Selling on one channel only
digital_maturity_model.next_step: Adopt Shopify + a marketplace and start tracking CAC, AOV and contribution margin in one sheet.

digital_maturity_model.name: Tooled & multi-channel
signals: Shopify + Amazon/Flipkart live
Basic analytics (GA, ad-platform dashboards)
3PL for fulfilment
Email/WhatsApp used ad hoc
digital_maturity_model.next_step: Centralise data — connect channels into one dashboard and instrument the full CM waterfall and cohort retention.

digital_maturity_model.name: Integrated & measured
signals: Unified order/inventory management (OMS) across channels
Blended CAC, LTV:CAC and MER tracked
Automated marketplace + GST reconciliation
Retention flows running on CRM
digital_maturity_model.next_step: Move from reporting to prediction — add demand forecasting and RTO/COD risk scoring.

digital_maturity_model.name: Predictive & automated
signals: SKU-level demand forecasting and auto-reorder
RTO/COD risk scoring at checkout
Automated lifecycle CRM segmentation
Real-time per-channel profitability
digital_maturity_model.next_step: Layer AI agents on top — autonomous creative/budget recommendations and self-serve support deflection.

digital_maturity_model.name: AI-native brand
signals: AI-driven creative generation + budget allocation
Autonomous inventory and pricing optimisation
AI customer support handling majority of tickets
Closed-loop data: acquisition→retention→product decisions
digital_maturity_model.next_step: Continuously optimise the full operating system with human oversight on strategy and brand.

playbooks.name: Construction & Infra Suppliers
playbooks.one_liner: An Indian MSME construction & infra supplier — civil contractors, building-material traders (cement/steel/aggregate/RMC), and small real-estate/EPC sub-contractors — that wins tendered or RERA-linked work and supplies/builds against milestone payments while carrying heavy working capital and labour risk.

operating_model.summary: A project-and-order business: revenue is booked against BOQ line-items, RA (running-account) bills, or material dispatch, but cash lags badly behind work-done. The operator juggles three engines simultaneously — (a) tender/quotation to win work, (b) site execution or material supply against a fixed BOQ, and (c) collection of certified bills with 5-10% retention held for the defect-liability period. Margin is made or lost in procurement of steel/cement/aggregate (50-65% of contract value) and in labour productivity, while EBITDA is silently eaten by interest on stretched receivables and idle equipment.
revenue_streams: Civil/EPC contract execution billed on RA bills against measured BOQ quantities (govt PWD/CPWD, private builders, infra)
Building-material trading & supply — cement, TMT steel, RMC, aggregates, tiles, sanitaryware, electricals — at distributor/dealer margin
Sub-contract & specialised works (waterproofing, plumbing, MEP, interiors, road/drainage) on rate contracts
Equipment & shuttering hire and ready-mix concrete (RMC) sale on per-cum / per-day rates
Annual maintenance / O&M and small repair-renovation jobs (higher-margin, faster cash)
cost_structure: Direct materials 50-65% of project value (cement, TMT steel, aggregate, RMC, fittings) — highly price-volatile
Labour & sub-contractor / piece-rate (thekedar) cost 15-25%, largely informal/cash
Plant, equipment hire, fuel/diesel, shuttering & site overheads 8-12%
Finance cost on working-capital loans, OD/CC and BG/LC charges 3-6% (interest on 90-150 day receivables)
Statutory & site overheads — GST, labour cess (1% under BOCW), insurance, site establishment, EMD/security deposits locked up 4-8%
value_drivers: Working-capital velocity — speed of RA-bill certification and collection, and release of retention/BG
Procurement edge — bulk rate contracts with cement/steel mills and timing of buys against price swings
Tender win-rate and bid quality (accurate BOQ rate analysis avoiding loss-making lines)
Labour productivity and on-time milestone delivery (LD/penalty avoidance)
Credit standing — bank limits, BG/LC capacity and contractor registration class determine ticket size of jobs winnable

value_chain: Lead & tender intake (e-procurement portals, builder enquiries, RERA project pipeline)
Bid submission with EMD + technical qualification
Work order / contract award & mobilisation advance
Site execution / material supply against schedule
Defect-liability / O&M & BG release & project closeout

core_processes.description: Build item-wise rates from material+labour+plant+overhead+profit; the single most decisive process — under-rating a line locks in a loss for the whole project term.
Joint measurement at site, entry into Measurement Book, RA-bill submission, client/PMC certification, deduction of advance/retention/TDS/cess, then payment — typically a 30-90 day loop per bill.
Convert BOQ into purchase plan, issue POs against rate contracts, GRN at site, and 3-way match (PO-GRN-invoice) to control theft/over-billing and protect ITC.
Mobilise gangs/thekedars, track attendance & productivity, maintain BOCW/labour-cess and wage-code compliance, and reconcile piece-rate measurements.
Plan CC/OD draw-downs, manage EMD/security-deposit lock-ups and bank guarantees, and chase retention release at DLP-end to free trapped cash.

department_structure.mandate: Source tenders/enquiries, qualify technically & financially, prepare accurate BOQ rate analysis, and submit competitive yet profitable bids with EMD.
Deliver work-orders on schedule and quality, manage labour/sub-contractors, equipment and site safety, and avoid LD/penalties.
Lock rate contracts for cement/steel/aggregate/RMC, run POs, GRN and 3-way match, and minimise material wastage and theft.
Raise & certify RA bills, file GST e-invoices/returns, manage CC/OD/BG limits, drive collections and retention release, and report project P&L.
Maintain RERA/contractor registrations, BOCW labour-cess, EPF/ESI, wage-code and safety compliance, and statutory filings.

operational_bottlenecks.bottleneck: Severe receivable stretch — money trapped in RA bills and retention
operational_bottlenecks.symptom: DSO of 90-150 days; retention (5-10%) and security deposits locked for 12-24 months; OD/CC limit perpetually at peak.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Interest cost silently erodes 3-6% of margin; growth is capped by cash, not order book.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Milestone billing + slow PMC/govt certification + DLP retention; no escrow protection (unlike RERA buyers); MSMED 45-day rule rarely enforced against large clients/PSUs.

operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Steel/cement prices move 10-20% within a project; site material 'shrinkage', over-billing by vendors, and wastage above norms.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Fixed-price BOQ contracts turn loss-making; gross margin swings unpredictably.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Fixed-rate tenders with no/weak price-escalation clause; weak 3-way match and stores discipline; cash purchases from local mandi without GST trail (ITC loss).

operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Won tenders that lose money on specific BOQ lines; frequent variation/extra-item disputes.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Negative project margins discovered only at RA-bill stage; cash burn on 'won' work.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Manual rate analysis in Excel, outdated rates, pressure to bid low (L1) in crowded govt tenders, no historical cost feedback loop.

operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Migrant-labour shortages (post-monsoon, harvest), thekedar dependence, cash wages, attendance disputes.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Schedule slippage triggers LD/penalties; BOCW cess/EPF/ESI non-compliance risk; quality rework.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Informal piece-rate ecosystem, no biometric attendance, low mechanisation, fragmented sub-contractor accountability.

operational_bottlenecks.bottleneck: BG/EMD and bank-limit constraints throttle scale
operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Cannot bid larger tenders — EMD, security deposit, mobilisation BG and performance BG exhaust bank limits.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Forced to decline higher-class work; multiple BGs locked across slow-closing projects.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Limited fund-based + non-fund-based banking limits for MSMEs; collateral-light balance sheet; delayed BG release after project completion.

operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Extra/variation work done without written approval; disputes over measured quantities; arbitration backlog.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Unbilled WIP, write-offs, legal cost; cash stuck in arbitration for years.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Weak contract/MB discipline at site, verbal client instructions, no formal change-order process, under-stamped agreements.

ai_automation_opportunities.opportunity: Auto-generate BOQ rate analysis from current material/labour rates + historical project costs, flagging loss-making line items before bid submission.
Receivables/DSO copilot that tracks every RA bill, certification stage, retention and BG, predicts cash gaps, and auto-drafts MSMED 45-day + interest follow-ups.
Procurement agent for cement/steel/aggregate rate-contract negotiation, price-trend buy-timing alerts, and PO-GRN-invoice 3-way match to plug ITC and shrinkage leakage.
RERA + contractor-registration + BOCW labour-cess compliance calendar with auto-reminders and document vault for renewals/filings.
GST e-invoice + e-way-bill automation on every material dispatch and RA bill, with GSTR-2B ITC reconciliation against site GRNs.
Tender-discovery + bid-qualification bot scanning GeM/CPP/state e-procurement portals, matching eligibility (class, turnover, similar-work) and computing win-probability.
Site-execution & milestone tracker (S-curve vs plan) that forecasts LD/penalty exposure and labour-productivity shortfalls.
Contract/variation-order intelligence — flag missing price-escalation, weak retention/LD/arbitration clauses and unstamped agreements before signing.

consulting_frameworks.use: Quantify days cash is trapped in RA bills, retention, WIP and stock vs supplier credit; the core lever for a sector where margin is good but cash is starved.
Identify the binding constraint per project — usually bill certification/collection or BG/bank-limit capacity, not site labour — and subordinate everything to relieving it.
Map tender-to-collection chain to locate margin leakage points (estimation rates, procurement, measurement, retention) and where to add controls.
Compute contribution per project after material+labour+finance cost; reject L1-bidding into negative-contribution tenders.
Fix accountability across estimation, site PM, QS measurement, billing engineer and finance so RA bills and change-orders don't fall between desks.
Track physical progress vs billing vs cost to catch schedule slippage (LD risk) and cost overrun early on each project.
Rank which tenders to chase and which process/automation fixes (billing speed, procurement, compliance) to build first by reach-impact-confidence-effort.

risk_model.risk: Receivable default / prolonged retention & BG lock-up from large/govt clients causing a working-capital crunch
risk_model.control: Stage-gate exposure per client, invoke MSMED 45-day + interest, factor/bill-discount certified RA bills, and track retention/BG release diligently.

risk_model.risk: RERA / contractor-registration non-compliance on real-estate-linked work (project not registered, escrow/timeline breach)
risk_model.control: Verify developer's RERA registration & escrow before mobilising; maintain own agent/contractor registration and renewals.

risk_model.risk: GST ITC denial / e-way-bill penalty due to cash purchases, mismatched GSTR-2B or missing dispatch documents
risk_model.control: Buy only GST-invoiced materials, enforce e-invoice + e-way bill on dispatch, and reconcile ITC to GRN monthly.

risk_model.risk: Labour-law & BOCW cess / EPF-ESI non-compliance and site-safety incidents with informal/migrant labour
risk_model.control: Biometric attendance, register sub-contractors, deduct/deposit 1% BOCW cess + EPF/ESI, and run documented HSE protocols.

risk_model.risk: Contract disputes / variation-order write-offs from weak documentation and under-stamped agreements
risk_model.control: Written change-orders before extra work, disciplined Measurement Book, and properly stamped contracts with clear LD/escalation/arbitration clauses.

risk_model.risk: Material price escalation on fixed-rate contracts wiping out project margin
risk_model.control: Negotiate price-escalation/star-rate clauses, lock rate contracts/forward buys for steel-cement, and hedge timing of bulk purchases.

kpi_structure.definition: Average days from RA-bill submission to cash receipt, including retention release.
Revenue minus direct material, labour and site cost per project.
Awarded contracts / technically-qualified bids submitted.
Earned value vs planned value; share of milestones hit without LD.

kpi_structure.kpi: Material cost variance vs BOQ estimate
kpi_structure.definition: Actual material cost minus estimated, as % of BOQ material value.
Outstanding BGs+EMD / sanctioned non-fund limit.

unit_economics: A ₹1 crore civil contract: materials ₹55-65 L, labour/sub-contract ₹18-25 L, plant+site overhead ₹8-12 L, finance+statutory ₹4-7 L -> net ₹4-8 L (4-8%); but ₹5-10 L sits in retention for 12-24 months
RMC sale ~₹4,500-5,500/cum with ₹400-700/cum contribution; TMT steel trading at ₹1,500-3,000/MT margin on a ₹55,000-65,000/MT price — thin, volume-and-velocity driven
EMD (1-2%) + security deposit (2-5%) + performance BG (5-10%) on a ₹1 cr job locks ₹8-17 L of non-fund/cash capacity per project
profitability_analysis.working_capital_notes: This is the make-or-break dimension. Cash is trapped 90-150 days in RA bills plus 12-24 months in retention/SD, while suppliers give only 15-30 days credit and labour is paid weekly in cash — a deeply negative cash cycle funded by CC/OD at 11-15%. Every ₹1 cr of revenue typically needs ₹25-40 L of working capital. Survival depends on bill-discounting/TReDS, disciplined retention chasing, MSMED 45-day enforcement, and refusing tenders that over-stretch the bank limits.
levers: Compress DSO: faster joint-measurement & RA-bill certification, TReDS/bill-discounting on certified bills, and aggressive retention/BG release at DLP-end
Protect material margin: annual rate contracts + price-escalation clauses + disciplined 3-way match to cut shrinkage and capture full ITC
Bid discipline: walk away from negative-contribution L1 tenders; price variation/extra items correctly
Labour productivity & mechanisation: biometric attendance, formwork systems and RMC to cut labour cost and rework
Overhead & finance-cost control: cap per-client exposure, right-size bank limits, and avoid idle equipment carrying cost

pm_workflows.cadence: Daily site DPR + weekly S-curve review; monthly RA bill

milestones: Ageing of all RA bills & retention mapped
BG/SD release applications filed at project close
Buy-timing alerts on price swings actioned

key_activities: Project P&L & lessons-learned feedback to estimation

stages.stage: Micro contractor / local material trader (<₹2 cr)
stages.focus: Survive cash cycle, get registered, win sub-contract & local supply work
plays: Complete Udyam + GST + contractor/labour registration to qualify for tenders
Stick to fast-cash jobs (renovation, supply, sub-contract) to fund the cash cycle
Build 2-3 rate contracts with local cement/steel dealers
Maintain clean books to unlock CC/OD bank limit

stages.focus: Professionalise estimation, billing & banking; raise contractor class
plays: Systematise BOQ rate analysis with historical cost feedback to stop loss-making bids
Set up disciplined RA-billing + retention-tracking and adopt TReDS/bill-discounting
Expand non-fund (BG/LC) limits to bid larger govt/private tenders
Add a specialised higher-margin line (waterproofing/MEP/RMC) and HSE/quality systems

stages.stage: Established contractor / EPC sub & multi-branch supplier (₹25 cr+)
stages.focus: Scale order book without breaking working capital; diversify clients & geographies
plays: Run a project-portfolio cash war-room; cap exposure per slow-paying client
Diversify into PSU+private+real-estate mix to de-risk receivables
Mechanise (formwork systems, RMC, equipment fleet) to cut labour dependence
Pursue JV/consortium bidding and investor/working-capital funding for scale; consider equipment leasing

digital_maturity_model.name: Manual / paper site
signals: BOQ & rate analysis in paper/loose Excel
Measurement Book and RA bills handwritten
Labour attendance & cash wages in registers
No visibility of receivables ageing
digital_maturity_model.next_step: Move estimation and billing onto structured spreadsheets/Tally; digitise the receivables ageing list.
