signals: Tally/Busy for accounting + GST returns
Standardised Excel BOQ templates
POs and material registers maintained
Collections tracked in a shared sheet
digital_maturity_model.next_step: Adopt e-invoice + e-way bill workflow and a simple project-cost tracker linking BOQ to actuals.

digital_maturity_model.name: Integrated project + finance system
signals: Construction ERP / project module (cost vs BOQ, RA bills)
3-way match (PO-GRN-invoice) in place
Compliance calendar (RERA/BOCW/GST) maintained
Biometric/site attendance digitised
digital_maturity_model.next_step: Connect dashboards across projects and put working-capital/DSO on a live cash-flow view.

digital_maturity_model.name: Data-driven & dashboarded
signals: Portfolio S-curve/SPI-CPI dashboards
Live DSO/retention & BG-utilisation dashboards
Historical cost feedback into estimation
Vendor price-trend tracking
digital_maturity_model.next_step: Layer predictive/AI agents for bid pricing, cash-gap forecasting and procurement buy-timing.

digital_maturity_model.name: AI-native operations
signals: AI rate-analysis flags loss-making bids pre-submission
Cash-flow & DSO forecasting with auto-drafted MSMED collection notices
Tender-discovery + win-probability scoring
Auto ITC reconciliation and predictive material buying
digital_maturity_model.next_step: Continuously retrain models on project outcomes; expand to autonomous procurement and portfolio risk steering.

playbooks.name: Restaurants & Cloud Kitchens

ai_automation_opportunities.opportunity: Dynamic menu/pricing engine that re-prices aggregator listings, toggles items, and adjusts portion/combo offers by daypart, weather, and live food-cost — reducing the 18-28% aggregator commission drag via direct-channel nudges.
Recipe-level food-cost and theoretical-vs-actual variance tracker: ties POS sales to BOM/recipe yields and live mandi/supplier rates to auto-flag pilferage, over-portioning, and wastage daily.
Auto-reconcile Swiggy/Zomato/ONDC settlement reports against POS sales, GST, TCS and commission deductions; surface short-payments and disputed orders for claim filing.
Demand-forecast + prep-list and indent generator per kitchen by daypart so chefs prep to forecast and procurement raises POs against par-levels, cutting spoilage of perishables.
FSSAI/labelling/hygiene compliance copilot: maintains licence renewals, FoSTaC food-handler training calendar, temperature/cleaning logs, and audit-ready records per outlet.
AI review/CSAT triage that auto-categorises Zomato/Google/Swiggy reviews and chat complaints, drafts responses, and routes recurring quality/delivery issues to the right outlet/SOP owner.
New-cloud-kitchen site & cuisine selector: scores delivery-zone demand, cuisine whitespace, rent/CAM, and rider serviceability before committing a lease or virtual brand.
Labour rostering optimiser matching shift staffing to forecast covers across dayparts to control the 18-25% labour-cost line without breaching service.

consulting_frameworks.use: Build the bottom-up economics of one outlet/virtual brand: AOV, COGS (food cost %), labour %, rent %, aggregator commission %, packaging, and contribution margin per order — the single source of truth for whether to open, close, or re-engineer a kitchen.

consulting_frameworks.framework: Prime cost control (Food cost % + Labour cost %)
consulting_frameworks.use: Industry's core operating discipline: keep prime cost (COGS + labour) under ~55-62% of net sales. Used to set portion standards, recipe BOMs, and rostering against forecast covers.

Identify the bottleneck station (e.g. tandoor, fryer, expo/packing) that caps orders-per-hour during peak dayparts; sequence the menu and KOT flow to lift the constraint rather than the whole kitchen.

Manage payable days to suppliers vs aggregator/ card settlement cycles (T+7 to T+15) and perishable inventory turns; restaurants are often cash-positive on dine-in but cash-tight on aggregator-heavy delivery models.

Classify every dish by popularity and contribution margin to re-design the menu — promote high-margin Stars, re-price or re-cost Plowhorses, reposition Puzzles, and cull Dogs that tie up prep and inventory.

consulting_frameworks.framework: Channel-mix / contribution analysis (dine-in vs delivery vs takeaway vs catering)
consulting_frameworks.use: Allocate true contribution by channel after commissions, discounts, packaging and rider/marketing cost to decide where to push capacity — direct ordering (ONDC/own app) almost always carries higher contribution than aggregators.
Define ownership across outlets for opening/closing, food safety logs, cash/settlement, and stock counts so a multi-outlet/cloud-kitchen network runs consistently without the founder in every shift.

department_structure.mandate: Consistent food quality, recipe/portion adherence, food-cost control, and meeting order throughput at peak dayparts within FSSAI hygiene norms.

department_structure.dept: Front of House / Service & Delivery Ops
department_structure.mandate: Guest experience for dine-in and on-time, accurate dispatch for delivery; manage aggregator order flow, packaging quality, and rider hand-off.
Daily indenting, vendor management (mandi, dairy, meat, packaging), par-level stock, FIFO/FEFO storage, and goods-receipt/3-way match.
Aggregator listing optimisation and ad spend, own-channel ordering (app/WhatsApp/ONDC), reviews & reputation, loyalty, and new virtual-brand launches.
Daily sales reconciliation across POS/aggregators, GST & TCS, payroll/PF/ESI/PT, FSSAI & shop licence renewals, and cash/banking controls.

digital_maturity_model.name: Manual / Paper-run kitchen
signals: KOTs and bills on paper or a basic billing machine
Stock counted by eye; indents on WhatsApp/phone
No recipe costing; food cost unknown month-to-month
Aggregator settlements never reconciled to POS
digital_maturity_model.next_step: Adopt a cloud POS that captures every dine-in/aggregator order and prints KOTs, so sales data exists to act on.

digital_maturity_model.name: Digitised billing & aggregator-connected
signals: Cloud POS in place; Swiggy/Zomato linked to POS
GST invoicing automated; daily sales report exists
Menu live on at least one aggregator + Google
Inventory still manual; food cost reviewed monthly
digital_maturity_model.next_step: Introduce recipe-level BOM and a basic inventory/indent module so food cost % and wastage become measurable per item.

digital_maturity_model.name: Integrated ops & inventory
signals: POS + inventory + recipe costing integrated
Par-levels and auto-indents to vendors
Settlement reconciliation done weekly; dashboards by outlet/channel
FSSAI logs, rosters and SOPs maintained digitally
digital_maturity_model.next_step: Layer analytics: menu engineering, channel contribution, and daypart staffing — and stand up an own-ordering channel (app/ONDC/WhatsApp).

digital_maturity_model.name: Data-driven, omnichannel network
signals: Direct-ordering channel live (own app/ONDC) reducing aggregator dependence
Menu re-engineered on contribution data; dynamic pricing/combos
Multi-outlet/cloud-kitchen scorecards with prime-cost targets
CRM/loyalty driving repeat orders; review triage in place
digital_maturity_model.next_step: Deploy predictive demand forecasting and automated prep/indent + variance alerts to pre-empt spoilage and stockouts.

digital_maturity_model.name: AI-native restaurant operating system
signals: Demand forecasting drives prep lists, rosters and procurement automatically
Theoretical-vs-actual food cost variance flagged daily with pilferage alerts
AI re-prices/toggles menu by daypart, weather and live food cost
Auto-reconciliation, compliance copilot and review-response largely autonomous
digital_maturity_model.next_step: Use the network's data to expand virtual brands and new sites with model-driven site/cuisine selection and franchise-ready playbooks.

stages.stage: Stage 1 — Validate a single profitable unit
stages.focus: Prove one outlet or cloud kitchen hits target prime cost and contribution before replicating; nail the core menu and SOPs.
plays: Cap menu to a tight, high-margin core (avoid SKU sprawl that kills prep speed)
Hit food cost <32-35% and prime cost <60% before any expansion
Get FSSAI, shop/Udyam, GST and aggregator listings clean from day one
Build the per-order P&L and reconcile aggregator settlements weekly

stages.focus: Sweat the same kitchen and team harder via virtual brands and own channels before adding rent.
plays: Launch 2-4 virtual brands from one kitchen to fill idle dayparts
Build a direct-ordering channel (own app/WhatsApp/ONDC) to cut aggregator commission
Add catering/bulk/corporate orders for high-AOV, low-CAC revenue
Standardise SOPs and recipe BOMs so a manager — not the founder — can run the kitchen

stages.focus: Replicate a proven, systemised unit across delivery zones/cities with a commissary and consistent quality.
plays: Set up a central commissary/cloud kitchen for prep and procurement scale
Expand by delivery-zone density (cluster outlets) rather than scattered sites
Roll out multi-outlet dashboards with prime-cost and CSAT targets per unit
Explore FOCO/franchise or partner-kitchen models once SOPs and brand are repeatable

kpi_structure.definition: COGS of food/beverage as a % of net sales
Food cost plus total labour cost as a % of net sales
Total commission, ads and funded discounts on delivery sales as a % of delivery GMV
Net sales divided by number of orders/covers (channel-wise)
Value of discarded/spoiled inventory as a % of food purchases
Share of orders from repeat customers or own (non-aggregator) channels
Orders dispatched complete and within target prep/SLA time
Net sales less food, packaging, commission and variable labour per order

playbooks.one_liner: A food-service MSME — dine-in restaurant, café, delivery-only cloud kitchen or caterer — selling prepared meals across dine-in, delivery-aggregator, takeaway and catering channels in India, where margins live or die on food cost, labour, rent and aggregator commissions, all under FSSAI licensing.

operating_model.summary: Restaurants and cloud kitchens convert raw ingredients and labour into prepared meals sold across multiple channels. Dine-in formats carry rent, ambience and service cost but earn higher AOV and direct customer relationships; cloud kitchens trade ambience for low rent and aggregator-led demand but live under 18-28% commission and discount pressure. Profit is a thin spread defended through prime-cost discipline, menu engineering, channel mix, and high asset utilisation (multiple virtual brands and dayparts from one kitchen).
revenue_streams: Dine-in covers (food + beverage, higher AOV, alcohol where licensed)
Delivery via aggregators (Swiggy/Zomato) — high volume, commission-heavy
Direct/own-channel orders (own app, WhatsApp, ONDC, phone) — higher contribution
Takeaway / counter sales
Catering, bulk, corporate and event orders (high AOV, planned)
Virtual/cloud brands run off the same kitchen
cost_structure: Food & beverage COGS (28-35% of sales) — perishable, mandi/supplier-driven
Labour (kitchen + service + delivery support, 18-25%)
Rent + CAM (dine-in 8-15%; cloud kitchen 3-8%)
Aggregator commission, ads & funded discounts (18-28% of delivery sales)
Packaging & consumables (delivery-heavy models 4-8%)
Utilities (power, gas/LPG, water), licences (FSSAI), marketing, and wastage
value_drivers: Prime cost control (food + labour) and low wastage
Asset utilisation — orders/covers per kitchen per daypart and virtual-brand stacking
Channel mix tilted toward higher-contribution direct orders vs aggregators
Brand strength, ratings/reviews, and repeat-customer rate
Menu engineering toward high-margin Star dishes

operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Strong order volumes but persistently thin or negative net margin on delivery; founder feels they 'work for Swiggy/Zomato'.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: 18-28% of delivery GMV lost to commission/ads/discounts; full dependence leaves pricing and customer data with the platform.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: No direct-ordering channel or loyalty; brand has no demand of its own, so it must keep buying visibility and funding discounts on aggregators.

operational_bottlenecks.bottleneck: Food cost leakage, over-portioning and pilferage
operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Food cost % drifts up month to month with no menu/price change; theoretical and actual cost diverge.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Each 2-3 point rise in food cost can wipe out the entire net margin given how thin restaurant economics are.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: No recipe-level BOM, standard portions or daily stock variance tracking; manual stores with weak goods-receipt and FIFO/FEFO discipline.

operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Dump of unsold prep at close on some days; stockouts and '86'd items (item unavailable) on others.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Wastage above 5-6% of purchases plus lost sales and bad reviews from unavailable popular dishes.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Prep and indenting driven by gut feel, not daypart-level demand forecasting; no par-levels tied to sales history.

operational_bottlenecks.bottleneck: Labour scheduling, attrition and skill dependence
operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Overstaffed slow shifts and understaffed peaks; quality dips when the head chef is absent; high churn of cooks/stewards.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Labour cost above 25% and/or service breakdowns at peak that hurt ratings and throughput.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Rosters not matched to forecast covers; tacit recipes in the chef's head rather than documented SOPs/BOMs; sector-wide high attrition.

operational_bottlenecks.bottleneck: Inconsistent quality & food-safety control across outlets/orders
operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Same dish tastes/looks different by outlet or shift; recurring 'cold/wrong/spilled' delivery complaints; ratings volatility.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Falling aggregator ratings throttle visibility and orders; FSSAI hygiene lapses risk fines or licence action.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Weak standardisation — no enforced SOPs, temperature/cleaning logs, packaging specs or food-handler (FoSTaC) training discipline.

operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Bank receipts from aggregators don't match expected sales; short-payments and disputed/cancelled orders go unclaimed.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Silent revenue leakage of a few percent and a GST/TCS mismatch that surfaces at filing or audit.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: No automated reconciliation of POS sales against aggregator settlement reports, commission deductions and TCS; manual, delayed accounting.

pm_workflows.cadence: 8-12 week project, then weekly review for first 90 days
milestones: Kitchen/site secured; FSSAI, GST, shop/Udyam registrations filed
Menu, recipe BOMs and packaging finalised; food-cost modelled
Aggregator + own-channel listings live with launch offers
Classify dishes into Stars/Plowhorses/Puzzles/Dogs on margin x popularity
Re-cost recipes against current supplier/mandi rates
Re-price, re-portion or cull; design high-margin combos
Update POS, aggregator and own-channel menus; track post-change contribution
Stand up own ordering (app/WhatsApp/ONDC) and offer wallet/loyalty
Migrate repeat customers off aggregators with direct-order incentives
Set monthly target for direct-channel order share
Measure CAC vs aggregator commission saved per order

pm_workflows.cadence: Initial 6-8 weeks, then monthly audit cadence
milestones: Document recipes/BOMs, opening-closing, hygiene and packaging SOPs
Assign RACI ownership per outlet; train staff (FoSTaC)
Roll out temperature/cleaning logs and stock-count discipline
Run monthly cross-outlet quality + compliance audit scorecard

key_activities: Define format (dine-in/cloud/cafe/catering), cuisine and target daypart/zone
Develop and standardise recipes with portion specs and BOMs
Cost each dish and set price for target food cost %
Source and qualify suppliers (mandi, dairy, meat, packaging)
Secure site/kitchen and obtain FSSAI, GST, shop/Udyam, fire/health NoCs
Install POS, integrate aggregators, set up own-channel ordering
Hire and train kitchen/service staff (FoSTaC food-handler training)
Launch listings, photography, intro offers and soft-launch trials
Daily indent, goods receipt (3-way match), FIFO/FEFO storage and prep
Run dayparts: KOT flow, cooking to standard, dispatch/service within SLA
Maintain hygiene, temperature and cleaning logs
Reconcile daily sales across POS and aggregator channels
Track prime cost, food cost %, wastage, AOV and channel contribution
Run menu engineering and re-pricing; act on review/CSAT triage
Tune rosters to forecast covers; manage par-levels and vendor terms
Add virtual brands/dayparts on existing kitchens
Open new outlets by delivery-zone density; set up commissary
Standardise playbooks for repeatable, manager-run units

profitability_analysis.typical_gross_margin: 60-70% (food gross margin; i.e. food cost 30-40% of sales)
profitability_analysis.typical_net_margin: 5-12% for a healthy unit; cloud kitchens often 3-8% after aggregator drag; many marginal units run 0-5%
unit_economics: Delivery order: AOV ₹350; food cost ₹120 (34%); packaging ₹20; aggregator commission+ads ~₹80 (23%); variable labour/utilities ₹35 → contribution ~₹95/order before rent & fixed overhead
Dine-in cover: AOV ₹600; food cost ₹190 (32%); service+variable labour ₹110; no commission → contribution ~₹300/cover before rent & fixed overhead
Cloud kitchen monthly: ~₹12-18 lakh sales possible per kitchen with 2-4 virtual brands; rent ₹40k-1.2 lakh keeps rent % low vs dine-in
profitability_analysis.working_capital_notes: Mostly cash/UPI-positive on dine-in, but aggregator and card receipts settle on a T+7 to T+15 cycle while perishable stock and wages are paid up front, creating a short cash gap; supplier credit (7-15 days) and high inventory turns (perishables turn every 2-5 days) are the main levers. Watch Sec 43B(h) — payments to MSME-registered suppliers must clear within 15/45 days for the expense to be deductible.
levers: Cut aggregator dependence by growing higher-contribution direct/own-channel orders
Tighten food cost via recipe BOMs, standard portions and daily variance tracking
Stack virtual brands and dayparts to raise sales per kitchen against fixed rent/labour
Menu-engineer toward Star dishes and high-margin combos; re-price Plowhorses
Reduce wastage below 3% with par-levels and forecast-driven prep
Match labour roster to forecast covers to hold labour % under 25%

risk_model.risk: FSSAI/food-safety violation — unhygienic conditions, expired stock, missing licence or labelling, food-poisoning incident
risk_model.control: Hold valid FSSAI licence per turnover slab; enforce FIFO/FEFO, temperature & cleaning logs, FoSTaC-trained handlers, and periodic internal hygiene audits.

risk_model.risk: Aggregator concentration & margin squeeze — commission hikes, ranking/algorithm changes or de-listing collapse demand
risk_model.control: Build a direct-ordering channel (own app/WhatsApp/ONDC) and loyalty; cap aggregator drag and diversify channel mix and brands.

risk_model.risk: Food-cost inflation & inventory leakage eroding thin margins
risk_model.control: Recipe BOMs with standard portions, daily theoretical-vs-actual variance, par-level indenting and 3-way goods-receipt match.

risk_model.risk: GST / TCS / settlement non-compliance — mismatch between POS sales, aggregator TCS and filed returns
risk_model.control: Automated reconciliation of POS vs aggregator settlement, correct GST rate/composition treatment, timely returns, and TCS credit claims.

risk_model.risk: Labour-law & payroll non-compliance — PF/ESI, professional tax, shop & establishment, wage/hours under new labour codes
risk_model.control: Register under Shops & Establishment, EPFO/ESIC and professional tax; maintain attendance, wage registers and statutory remittances.

risk_model.risk: Delayed payment to MSME suppliers triggering Sec 43B(h) disallowance and supplier disputes
risk_model.control: Track MSME-registered vendors and clear dues within 15/45 days; formalise purchase terms in writing.

risk_model.risk: Quality/brand reputation collapse — review bombing, recurring complaints throttle aggregator visibility
risk_model.control: Standardised SOPs, packaging specs, order-accuracy checks and active review/CSAT triage with response SLAs.

value_chain: Prep & production (mise en place to daypart forecast)
Order capture (POS, aggregators, own channel) & KOT

core_processes.description: Forecast covers by daypart, count stock, raise indents/POs against par-levels, receive and store goods (3-way match, FIFO/FEFO), and prep mise en place to forecast to minimise spoilage and stockouts.
Capture orders from dine-in/aggregator/own channel into one POS, fire KOTs, cook to standard, pack to spec, and dispatch within prep/SLA time while keeping order accuracy high.
Reconcile POS sales daily against aggregator settlement reports, commissions, discounts and TCS; bank receipts; and post correct GST — flagging short-payments and disputed orders for claims.
Quarterly classify dishes by margin x popularity, re-cost against current supplier rates, and re-price/re-portion/cull to defend prime cost and lift contribution.
Maintain FSSAI licence, FoSTaC training, temperature/cleaning/hygiene logs and statutory registrations (GST, shop, PF/ESI/PT) on a renewal and audit calendar.

playbooks.name: Healthcare Clinics
playbooks.one_liner: An owner-doctor-led outpatient healthcare MSME — single/multi-specialty clinics, day-care, and attached diagnostic labs/telemedicine — delivering consultations, diagnostics, and minor procedures across India's Tier-1/2/3 cities largely on cash-and-walk-in volumes.

operating_model.summary: A clinic monetises a doctor's time, diagnostic throughput and pharmacy/procedure margins. Footfall is driven by the lead doctor's reputation, locality catchment (2-5 km), and increasingly Google/Practo/Justdial discovery. Most Indian clinics run lean: 1-3 doctors, 3-8 paramedical/front-desk staff, owned or leased ~600-1,500 sq ft. Revenue mixes high-frequency low-ticket consults with higher-ticket diagnostics, procedures and pharmacy. Cash and UPI dominate; insurance/TPA cashless is rising in metros but brings 45-90 day receivables.
revenue_streams: OPD consultation fees (₹300-₹800 Tier-2, ₹500-₹1,500 Tier-1 per visit)
In-house diagnostics / pathology / radiology (highest-margin line, 50-70% GM)
Minor procedures, day-care, dressings, vaccinations, IV/injection room
Pharmacy / dispensing counter (Schedule-H sales, 15-22% trade margin)
Telemedicine / follow-up teleconsults and chronic-care subscription packages
Health check-up packages, corporate tie-ups and camp revenue
cost_structure: Doctor compensation / revenue-share to visiting consultants (35-55% of consult revenue)
Rent (8-15% of revenue in Tier-1, 5-10% Tier-2/3) and utilities/power backup
Paramedical, nursing, front-desk and lab-tech salaries + EPF/ESI/PT
Diagnostic consumables, reagents, lab outsourcing, AMC on equipment
Medicines / vaccine inventory (cold-chain, expiry write-offs)
Software (clinic management/EHR), Practo/online listing fees, marketing, biomedical waste contract
value_drivers: Lead doctor reputation and repeat/retention rate of the local catchment
Diagnostics attach-rate per consult (in-house vs referred-out leakage)
Chair/room utilisation and average revenue per patient visit (ARPV)
Cashless/TPA empanelment and corporate health-package contracts
Accreditation (NABH/NABL) unlocking insurance panels and premium pricing

value_chain: Patient acquisition & discovery (referrals, Google/Practo, camps, corporate tie-ups)
Appointment booking & registration (front-desk, token/queue, EHR record)
Triage & vitals capture by nursing/paramedical staff
Diagnostics / pathology / radiology order & sample collection
Billing, payment collection (cash/UPI/TPA claim) & GST invoice

core_processes.description: Registration -> token -> vitals -> doctor queue with minimal patient wait; demographics + history captured once in EHR and reused, avoiding re-keying and duplicate records.
Doctor order -> sample collection/scheduling -> processing (in-house or outsourced lab) -> validated report -> result delivery (WhatsApp/portal) with TAT tracking and critical-value alerting.

Service capture -> coded bill -> cash/UPI or TPA cashless pre-auth -> claim submission -> reconciliation of denials/short-payments -> collection; the largest leakage point for clinics doing insurance.
Drug/reagent/vaccine procurement -> FEFO storage with temperature logging -> dispensing -> reorder at par level -> expiry and narcotics/Schedule-H register compliance.

department_structure.mandate: Deliver safe, evidence-based care; own clinical protocols, documentation quality and patient outcomes.
Run pathology/radiology and the dispensing counter with accurate TAT, calibration, FEFO and Schedule-H compliance.
Own appointments, registration, queue/wait management, billing and patient communication/recall.
Manage cash/UPI reconciliation, TPA/insurance claims, GST/TDS filings, payroll and vendor payments.
Maintain licences (Clinical Establishment, Drug, PCPNDT, BMW), NABH/NABL readiness, biomedical-waste, fire/safety and HR/statutory compliance.

operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Footfall and revenue collapse when the lead doctor is on leave; no continuity, patients defer.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: High revenue volatility, inability to scale beyond one chair, low enterprise value.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Brand equity sits with the individual doctor, not the clinic; no protocolised care or junior-doctor leverage.

operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Crowded waiting room, token disputes, walk-ins jumping appointments, negative Google reviews.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Poor experience drives churn to competitors; caps daily throughput and ARPV.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: No real appointment discipline; overbooking, manual tokens, no triage/queue system.

operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Doctors send patients to outside labs/imaging centres instead of capturing in-house.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Loss of the highest-margin revenue line (50-70% GM) and break in care continuity.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: No in-house diagnostics or weak attach-process; report TAT distrust; informal referral kickbacks elsewhere.

operational_bottlenecks.bottleneck: TPA/insurance claim denials and slow collections
operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Cashless claims rejected/short-paid; receivables ageing 45-90+ days; cashflow squeezed.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Working-capital strain, write-offs of 5-12% of claimed value, staff time lost on resubmission.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Incomplete documentation/pre-auth, coding errors, no denial-tracking; under-resourced RCM.

operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Paper files/registers, no recall lists, can't measure repeat-rate, ARPV or doctor productivity.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: No retention engine, lost chronic-care revenue, weak NABH evidence, owner flies blind.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: No EHR/clinic-management adoption; staff resistance and perceived data-entry burden.

operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Scramble at inspection for Clinical Establishment, Drug Licence, PCPNDT, BMW, fire NOC renewals.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Penalties, sealing risk, blocked NABH/empanelment, reputational damage.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Fragmented multi-authority licensing with different cycles; no compliance calendar/owner.

ai_automation_opportunities.opportunity: AI appointment + WhatsApp scheduling with smart slotting, reminders and no-show prediction to cut wait-times and fill idle chair hours.
Automated TPA/insurance claim assembly, denial-prediction and follow-up workflow to shrink DSO and recover short-payments.
Patient recall & chronic-care adherence engine (diabetes/hypertension/follow-up) driving repeat diagnostics and teleconsults.
FEFO drug/reagent/vaccine inventory with cold-chain temperature logging, expiry alerts and Schedule-H register automation.
AI clinical-documentation/ambient scribe to auto-draft Rx and notes, freeing doctor time and improving EHR completeness.
Compliance calendar automation for Clinical Establishment, Drug, PCPNDT, BMW, fire NOC + NABH evidence pack.
Local-SEO / Practo / Google Business reputation and review-response automation to drive catchment discovery.
GST e-invoicing and TDS/payroll automation across consult, diagnostics and pharmacy lines.

consulting_frameworks.use: Model contribution per patient visit = consult fee + diagnostics attach + pharmacy margin minus doctor share and consumables; find the breakeven visits/day per chair.
Identify the binding constraint (usually doctor-hours or front-desk throughput) and schedule/triage around it; offload non-clinical work to staff and automation.
Map discovery -> booking -> consult -> diagnostics -> pharmacy -> follow-up to plug margin leakage (esp. referred-out diagnostics) and capture more of the patient journey in-house.
Manage the cash-vs-TPA split: cash/UPI is near-instant, TPA is 45-90 day DSO; quantify the receivables drag and the inventory days of drugs/reagents.
Frame why a patient picks this clinic (proximity, trust, speed, one-stop diagnostics) to design packages, telemedicine and recall offers around the real job.
Clarify ownership across owner-doctor, practice manager, RCM and quality coordinator for claims, compliance renewals and clinical protocols — kills the single-point dependency.
Rank improvement bets (EHR rollout, in-house lab, NABH, teleconsult) by Reach x Impact x Confidence / Effort before investing scarce owner bandwidth and capex.

risk_model.risk: Clinical negligence / medical malpractice claim or adverse patient outcome
risk_model.control: Maintain indemnity insurance, informed-consent documentation, clinical protocols, credentialing of consultants, and NABH-aligned incident reporting.

risk_model.risk: Drug Licence / Schedule-H & narcotics non-compliance at the dispensing counter
risk_model.control: Registered pharmacist on duty, prescription-validated dispensing, maintained sale/purchase registers, FEFO and expiry control.

risk_model.risk: PCPNDT / Clinical Establishment Act licensing lapse leading to sealing or penalty
risk_model.control: Compliance calendar with owner-assigned renewals, PCPNDT Form-F records for any ultrasound, NABH-grade document control.

risk_model.risk: TPA/insurance claim denials, short-payment and receivables ageing
risk_model.control: Pre-authorisation discipline, accurate coding, denial-tracking dashboard, dedicated RCM resource and reconciliation cadence.

risk_model.risk: GST mis-classification (exempt healthcare vs taxable diagnostics/pharmacy/cosmetic) and ITC errors
risk_model.control: Correct service-vs-goods tax mapping, e-invoicing where applicable, periodic GST review of mixed-supply lines.

risk_model.risk: Biomedical-waste, fire-safety and statutory labour (EPF/ESI/PT) non-compliance
risk_model.control: Authorised BMW vendor + manifests, fire NOC, EPF/ESI enrolment and PT/payroll automation with a compliance owner.

risk_model.risk: Patient health-data privacy breach (EHR / WhatsApp reports)
risk_model.control: Access-controlled EHR, consented data sharing, encrypted report delivery, DPDP-aligned retention and breach process.

kpi_structure.definition: Booked-and-seen consult hours as a % of available doctor hours per day.
Total revenue (consult + diagnostics + pharmacy) divided by patient visits.
% of consults that convert to an in-house diagnostic/lab order.
% of patients returning within 12 months (excl. one-off acute).
Average days to collect cashless/insurance receivables.
Registration-to-doctor time for appointed patients.
% of booked appointments not honoured.

unit_economics: Per consult: fee ₹300-₹800 (Tier-2) less doctor share 35-55% (₹120-₹400) = clinic contribution ₹150-₹400 before overheads
In-house diagnostic test: realised ₹400-₹2,500 at 50-70% GM; one CBC/lipid panel can equal 2-3 consults in contribution
Single-doctor clinic at 25-35 visits/day, ~26 days: ~₹6-12 lakh/month revenue; fixed overhead (rent+staff+software) ~₹2.5-4 lakh/month
Pharmacy counter: 15-22% trade margin, but ties up ₹2-5 lakh inventory with expiry write-off risk of 2-5%
profitability_analysis.working_capital_notes: Cash/UPI clinics are near working-capital-positive (collect at point of care, pay vendors on terms). Insurance/TPA-heavy practices carry 45-90 day receivables that must be financed; drug/reagent inventory adds 20-45 inventory days. Watch Sec 43B(h) timely payment to MSME diagnostic/equipment vendors. Equipment is the main capex (lab analyser/USG ₹5-40 lakh), often lease/AMC-financed.
levers: Lift diagnostics attach-rate and bring referred-out tests in-house (highest-margin swing)
Improve chair utilisation via appointment discipline and no-show reduction
Add high-margin packages (health check-ups, chronic-care subscriptions, vaccination, day-care procedures)
Negotiate consultant revenue-share and tighten drug/reagent procurement & expiry
Cut TPA DSO and denials via disciplined RCM to release trapped cash

pm_workflows.cadence: 12-week implementation, then weekly adoption review for 8 weeks
milestones: Front-desk + billing go-live with parallel run
Dashboard (ARPV, utilisation, DSO) live for owner
Gap assessment vs NABH entry-level standards
Map cash vs TPA flows and current DSO/denial baseline

key_activities: Premises, equipment, licences (Clinical Establishment, Drug, PCPNDT, BMW, fire)
Set up EHR, billing, GST registration
Local SEO/Google Business, Practo/Justdial listing, referral network
Add chairs/specialties, second location or hub-spoke
Data-driven optimisation of ARPV, utilisation, DSO

stages.focus: De-risk doctor dependency and capture the patient journey in-house
plays: Adopt EHR + appointment discipline to lift utilisation and cut wait-times
Add in-house basic pathology + pharmacy to raise diagnostics attach and ARPV
Build local-SEO/Practo presence and a recall list for repeat visits
Establish a compliance calendar for all licences

stages.focus: Institutionalise the brand beyond one doctor and professionalise operations
plays: Hire visiting consultants on revenue-share to add specialties and continuity
Stand up RCM and TPA empanelment for cashless volumes
Pursue NABH entry-level + NABL for diagnostics to unlock premium pricing
Launch chronic-care subscriptions, corporate packages and teleconsults

stages.focus: Standardise, centralise and scale with data and capital
plays: Centralise diagnostics in a hub lab feeding spoke clinics; standard SOPs/protocols
Build a management layer (practice managers, central RCM, quality function)
Data-driven expansion: pick catchments on demand modelling and unit economics
Prepare for institutional capital / strategic partnership with audit-ready books

digital_maturity_model.name: Manual / paper
signals: Paper case files and physical appointment register
Cash receipts, hand-written bills, no GST-clean invoicing
No patient database or recall capability
digital_maturity_model.next_step: Adopt a basic clinic-management/billing software and digitise registration and invoicing.

digital_maturity_model.name: Digitised records
signals: Billing/registration software in use; some EHR fields captured
Excel for collections; GST invoices generated digitally
Appointments still phone/walk-in heavy, no analytics
digital_maturity_model.next_step: Move to full EHR with e-prescription and online appointment booking, and start measuring utilisation/ARPV.

digital_maturity_model.name: Integrated clinic system
signals: EHR + diagnostics + pharmacy + billing on one connected system
Online booking, WhatsApp reminders, basic dashboards (ARPV, DSO)
TPA claims tracked digitally
digital_maturity_model.next_step: Add automation: reminders/recall workflows, denial-tracking RCM, FEFO inventory and reputation management.

digital_maturity_model.name: Automated & data-driven
signals: Automated recall, no-show prediction and claim follow-up
Real-time owner dashboards driving decisions
Local-SEO and review automation; FEFO/cold-chain alerts
digital_maturity_model.next_step: Layer AI: ambient clinical scribe, denial-prediction, demand forecasting and personalised chronic-care nudges.

digital_maturity_model.name: AI-native
signals: AI clinical documentation and decision support assist doctors
Predictive scheduling, claim-denial and inventory models
AI-driven patient engagement and outcome/quality analytics feeding NABH
digital_maturity_model.next_step: Federate data across locations for population-health insights and continuous AI-optimised operations.

playbooks.name: Real Estate Businesses
playbooks.one_liner: A tier-2-priority Indian MSME real estate business spanning small-to-mid developers, brokerage/channel-partner firms, and rental/property-management outfits that source, build/transact, and manage residential and commercial property under RERA, monetising through development margins, brokerage commissions and recurring management fees.

operating_model.summary: Indian MSME real estate firms operate in one of three overlapping models: (a) small/mid developers who acquire land, obtain approvals, build and sell units (₹5-50 cr project sizes in Tier-2/3); (b) brokerage/channel-partner firms that match buyers/tenants to inventory for a 1-2% commission; (c) property/rental management firms charging 5-10% of rent plus AMC fees. Cash is highly lumpy, governed by RERA escrow, approval timelines, and the festive/Akshaya-Tritiya/Diwali demand cycle.
revenue_streams: Developer: unit sale margin (sale price minus land + construction + approval cost), plus PLC/floor-rise/parking/club charges
Brokerage: 1-2% of deal value on resale/primary sales; 1-2 months' rent on rental closures; channel-partner override from developers (2-5% of primary inventory)
Property management: 5-10% of monthly rent as management fee, fixed AMC per unit, tenant-onboarding and maintenance markup
Recurring: facility management contracts, society maintenance billing, NRI portfolio management retainers
Ancillary: home-loan referral fees from banks/HFCs, interior/fit-out commissions, registration/documentation service charges
cost_structure: Land/inventory acquisition (developer's largest cost, 30-50% of project) and approval/sanction fees (RERA, plan sanction, NOCs)
Construction: materials (cement/steel/sand), labour contractors, RMC; 8-12% GST input on under-construction works
Sales & marketing: digital leads (99acres/MagicBricks/Housing portal subscriptions), broker commissions, site/sample-flat upkeep
Interest/finance cost on construction finance or LRD (lease-rental discounting) — often 11-16% for MSME builders
Manpower: sales executives (high attrition), site engineers, liaison/legal, accounts; plus RERA-mandated escrow-account audits
Statutory: GST, stamp duty/registration (passed to buyer), TDS u/s 194-IA on property buys, property tax
value_drivers: Land bank quality and clear title (single biggest value lever — title defects destroy projects)
Approval velocity and RERA-completion-track-record (timely delivery reputation drives premium and referrals)
Inventory turnover / sell-through rate before completion (reduces interest burden and unsold-stock risk)
Brand trust and verified listings (buyers pay premium and brokers retain clients on transparency)
Recurring management AUM (units under management) for annuity-like, low-capital income

value_chain: Design, construction & vendor management (developer) / inventory listing & verification (brokerage)
Post-sale: CRM, society formation, property/facility management & rentals

core_processes.description: 30-year title search, encumbrance certificate, mutation/khata, conversion/land-use, litigation check and legal opinion before any acquisition or marketing commitment.
Register project/agent with State RERA, deposit 70% of buyer receipts into a designated escrow account, file quarterly progress updates, and withdraw only against CA/engineer/architect certification.
Portal/digital lead capture to qualification, site visit, negotiation, token, booking form, allotment letter, agreement-to-sale, and registration — tracked in CRM with channel-partner attribution.
Demand letters tied to construction stages (slab-wise), reconciling collections vs. RERA escrow rules and tracking outstanding from buyers and home-loan disbursement timelines.
Snag-list closure, occupancy certificate, possession letter, handover kit, society/RWA formation and transition into facility/property management or AMC.

department_structure.mandate: Source land/inventory, conduct title due diligence, secure approvals/NOCs and RERA registration, and manage litigation and documentation.
Deliver projects on time, on cost and on quality; manage contractors, materials, site engineering and snag closure (developer model).
Generate and convert leads, manage channel partners/brokers, run digital campaigns and site experience, and hit booking/sell-through targets.
Manage escrow and project finance, construction-linked collections, GST/TDS/income-tax filings, lender reporting and audited RERA withdrawals.
Run post-sale CRM, society/RWA transition, rental management, tenant onboarding, maintenance and AMC contracts for annuity income.

operational_bottlenecks.bottleneck: Title and approval uncertainty stalling launches
operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Projects launched then halted; bookings cancelled; capital locked in land that cannot be developed or sold.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Months-to-years of delay, interest bleed, RERA penalties and buyer refunds; can be existential for a single-project MSME developer.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Fragmented land records, pending mutation/conversion, multi-agency NOC dependencies, and weak upfront due diligence under pressure to acquire fast.

operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Completed/near-complete units sitting unsold for 12-36 months; rising carrying and interest cost.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Margin erosion, distressed discounting, inability to service construction finance, and cash crunch for next project.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Overbuilding to local demand, generic positioning, weak digital lead engine, and over-reliance on a few brokers with no first-party CRM.

operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Money received but locked in RERA escrow (70%) while vendor/labour payments are due now.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Working-capital stress, delayed contractor payments, stalled construction, and reputational damage.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Poor milestone-collection planning, weak CA-certified withdrawal cadence, and inadequate construction-finance buffer.

operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Portal leads unanswered for hours/days, no attribution, brokers double-claiming the same buyer.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: High CAC, lost bookings, commission disputes, and inability to know true cost-per-booking.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: No integrated CRM, manual WhatsApp/Excel lead handling, and absence of channel-partner attribution rules.

operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Steel/cement price spikes, labour shortages and rework push budgets and possession dates past commitments.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Margin compression, RERA delay penalties, buyer compensation claims and damaged delivery reputation.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Fixed-price buyer commitments against variable input costs, weak BOQ/procurement discipline, and informal contractor management.

operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Maintenance complaints, rent-collection delays, tenant churn and disputed deposits in the management book.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Lost AMC renewals, owner/NRI dissatisfaction, and erosion of the recurring-revenue annuity.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Manual ledgers, no tenant/owner portal, and reactive (vs. SLA-driven) maintenance operations.

ai_automation_opportunities.opportunity: AI lead-response and qualification bot across portals/WhatsApp that instantly responds, qualifies budget/intent, books site visits and routes to the right executive with channel attribution.
Automated title/legal document checklist and red-flag extraction from EC, sale deeds, mutation and NOCs to accelerate and de-risk due diligence.
RERA compliance and escrow-withdrawal calendar copilot that tracks quarterly filings, CA-certified withdrawal eligibility and milestone collections.
Construction-linked collections and DSO automation: auto-generate demand letters by milestone, chase overdue buyers, and reconcile against escrow rules.
Local demand and price intelligence: scrape/analyse micro-market rates, competitor launches and absorption to inform pricing and launch timing.
Property/tenant management workflow with SLA-driven maintenance ticketing, automated rent reminders and owner/NRI reporting.

consulting_frameworks.use: Map land-to-handover-to-management stages to find where margin leaks (approvals delay, unsold stock, escrow lock) and where to digitise.
Model the lag between land outlay, construction spend and milestone collections vs. escrow release to size the construction-finance buffer and protect liquidity.
Compute per-unit contribution (sale price minus land+construction+approval+commission+interest) for developers, and per-deal/per-AUM economics for brokerage and management.
Identify the binding constraint per project — usually approvals/title, capital, or sales velocity — and concentrate management attention there rather than diffusing effort.
Rank land deals, new launches and tech investments by Reach (demand), Impact (margin), Confidence (title/approval certainty) and Effort (capital/time).
Clarify ownership across land/liaison, projects, sales/channel and finance for approvals, collections and RERA filings to stop dropped-handoff delays.
Frame buyer/tenant/owner jobs (safe title, on-time possession, hassle-free rental income) to sharpen positioning, trust signals and service design.

risk_model.risk: Defective/unclear land title or pending litigation derailing a project
risk_model.control: Mandatory 30-year title search, EC, independent legal opinion and title insurance before acquisition; no marketing before clearance.

risk_model.risk: RERA non-compliance — late filings, escrow misuse or possession delay penalties
risk_model.control: RERA compliance calendar, segregated 70% escrow with CA/engineer-certified withdrawals, and quarterly progress filings.

risk_model.risk: Liquidity crunch from unsold inventory and escrow-locked receipts
risk_model.control: Milestone-linked collection plan, pre-launch sell-through targets, construction-finance buffer and rolling 13-week cashflow.

risk_model.risk: GST/TDS errors on under-construction sales, RCM and 194-IA buyer deductions
risk_model.control: Correct GST treatment of under-construction vs. ready units, ITC tracking, and automated TDS/GST filing with reconciliation.

risk_model.risk: Stamp duty and registration disputes on agreements and conveyance
risk_model.control: State-specific stamp-duty computation, properly stamped and registered agreements, and standardised vetted templates.

risk_model.risk: Brokerage/channel commission disputes and contract ambiguity
risk_model.control: Written channel-partner and buyer agreements with clear attribution, payment triggers and indemnity clauses.

risk_model.risk: Delayed payments to MSME contractors triggering 43B(h) disallowance
risk_model.control: Track MSME-registered vendors, pay within 45 days, and reconcile against Sec 43B(h) before year-end.

kpi_structure.definition: Percentage of launched units booked over a defined period (e.g. per quarter or by completion).
Collections realised vs. demands raised on construction milestones; days to collect.
Total sales+marketing+commission spend divided by bookings closed.
Median time from portal/WhatsApp lead to first qualified contact.
Share of units handed over on or before RERA-committed date.
Rent collected vs. billed and occupied units vs. managed units.

profitability_analysis.typical_gross_margin: Developer 20-35% on project value; brokerage 70-85% gross on commission; property management 40-55% on fee income
profitability_analysis.typical_net_margin: Developer 8-18% after interest and overhead; brokerage 15-30%; property management 12-25%
unit_economics: Developer (Tier-2 mid-rise): sale ₹45-65 lakh/unit; land+construction+approval ₹32-48 lakh; interest+marketing+commission ₹4-7 lakh; net ₹5-12 lakh/unit
Brokerage: resale deal ₹60 lakh ticket at 1.5% = ₹90,000 commission; CAC (portal+executive) ₹15,000-30,000 per closure; net ₹50,000-70,000
Property management: ₹25,000/month rent at 8% = ₹2,000/unit/month + onboarding ₹3,000-5,000; servicing cost ₹800-1,200/unit/month; net ₹800-1,200/unit/month annuity
profitability_analysis.working_capital_notes: Highly negative and lumpy for developers: land and approvals are paid years before milestone collections, and 70% of receipts are locked in RERA escrow, so a construction-finance line (11-16%) bridges the gap. Brokerage is near cash-positive (commission on closure) but carries 30-90 day collection lag from developers. Management is cash-positive once at scale (rent collected monthly). DSO on developer demand letters often runs 30-75 days against home-loan disbursement timing.
levers: Increase pre-completion sell-through to cut interest carry and unsold-stock risk
Build a first-party CRM/lead engine to reduce broker dependency and CAC
Tighten milestone collection and escrow-withdrawal cadence to free working capital
Grow recurring property-management AUM for capital-light annuity income
Disciplined BOQ/procurement and fixed-rate vendor contracts to contain construction cost overruns

pm_workflows.cadence: Stage-gated over 6-18 months with weekly steering reviews
milestones: Title due diligence cleared & land acquired
Plan sanction + NOCs + RERA registration obtained
Escrow account opened & construction finance tied up

pm_workflows.cadence: Fortnightly site review + monthly collections & escrow reconciliation

milestones: CRM live with portal/WhatsApp lead capture
Booking target for the quarter achieved

key_activities: Title due diligence and legal opinion
Marketing, lead generation and site experience
Snag list closure and quality sign-off

stages.focus: Clean title, on-time delivery and trust-building in one micro-market
plays: Win on transparency: RERA-registered, verified listings, clear pricing
Build a first-party lead engine (portals + WhatsApp + referrals)
Deliver one project flawlessly to earn referral flywheel
Get Udyam-registered and set disciplined GST/escrow books

stages.focus: Repeatable launch playbook, channel network and working-capital discipline
plays: Standardise the land-to-RERA-to-handover stage-gate
Formalise channel-partner program with attribution and overrides
Tie up reliable construction finance and milestone collection discipline
Layer in recurring property management for annuity income

stages.focus: Brand, governance and capital-light recurring revenue at scale
plays: Build a regional brand around delivery track record
Adopt ERP + CRM + escrow automation for audit-ready governance
Grow management AUM and FM contracts as annuity base
Access structured capital (NBFC/PE/LRD) and investor-grade reporting

signals: Leads in WhatsApp and Excel
Physical files for title/agreements
Collections tracked in registers
No CRM or escrow tracking software
digital_maturity_model.next_step: Adopt a basic CRM and digitise lead capture and a collections tracker.

signals: CRM logging leads and bookings
Tally/accounting software for books
Documents scanned and stored on drive
Manual RERA filings and demand letters
digital_maturity_model.next_step: Integrate portal/WhatsApp leads into CRM and automate demand letters and reminders.

digital_maturity_model.name: Integrated & automated
signals: CRM auto-captures portal leads with attribution
Automated demand letters and rent reminders
Escrow/collections reconciled in software
Compliance calendar for RERA/GST/TDS

Micro-market pricing informed by data
