playbooks.name: Education Institutes
playbooks.one_liner: A founder-led Indian education institute spanning coaching/test-prep, vocational/skill training, and edtech-blended delivery that converts enrolled learners into outcomes (exam ranks, jobs, certifications) for fees, typically run as a single-location-to-multi-branch MSME in Tier-2/3 cities.

operating_model.summary: Revenue is enrollment-fee driven (batch coaching, test prep, vocational courses, online subscriptions) with high seasonal intake spikes (Apr-Jul admission season, Nov-Jan exam season). The business sells a future outcome, so brand/result-reputation drives demand and CAC. Cost is dominated by faculty salaries, rent of premises, and marketing. Cash is collected upfront or in installments, giving negative working capital when managed well, but refund/dropout liabilities and EMI-financed fees create reversal risk.
revenue_streams: Batch/classroom course fees (annual/multi-year coaching, test prep like JEE/NEET/UPSC/SSC/banking)
Vocational & skill-training course fees (IT, beauty, retail, healthcare, NSDC/PMKVY-aligned)
Online/hybrid subscriptions, recorded-content & app/LMS access fees
Study material, mock-test series, books and assessment-pack sales
Registration/admission fees, scholarship-test fees, certification & placement-assistance fees
Franchise/licensing fees and royalty from satellite centres; B2B corporate/college training contracts
cost_structure: Faculty & academic salaries + incentives (largest line, 30-45% of revenue)
Premises rent, electricity, furniture, AV/lab equipment (15-25%)
Marketing & lead generation (digital ads, local hoardings, seminars, referrals) 10-20%
Counsellor/admission sales team salaries & commissions
Content production, LMS/edtech software, exam/proctoring platform fees
Administration, compliance, scholarships/fee-waivers, bad-debt on installment fees
value_drivers: Demonstrable outcomes (selections, ranks, placement %, pass rates) that compound brand and referrals
Star faculty retention and standardised, scalable teaching content
Counselling-to-enrollment conversion efficiency and batch fill-rate (capacity utilisation)
Recurring/renewal revenue from multi-year programs and content subscriptions
Multi-branch / franchise replicability with consistent quality

value_chain: Curriculum & content design (syllabus, faculty hiring, material, mock tests)
Demand generation (digital ads, seminars, scholarship tests, school tie-ups, referrals)
Retention, renewal, upsell & referral / alumni advocacy

core_processes.description: Capture inquiries from ads/walk-ins/seminars into CRM, assign counsellors, run scholarship/aptitude test, follow-up cadence, close admission, collect fee and issue receipt/installment plan.
Time-table and batch scheduling, faculty allocation, syllabus pacing, periodic tests, doubt sessions, attendance and learning-outcome tracking against a defined teaching SOP.
Onboarding, parent/student communication, performance reviews, at-risk-dropout flagging, installment reminders, renewal/next-level upsell, alumni and placement tracking.
Forecast intake, size batches to break-even fill-rate, hire/contract faculty, manage utilisation, standardise content so delivery is not single-teacher dependent.

department_structure.mandate: Design curriculum, deliver teaching, maintain learning outcomes and result quality across batches and branches.
Generate, qualify and convert leads into paid enrollments and hit batch fill targets.
Build result-led brand, run digital + local campaigns, school/college tie-ups, manage seminars and referrals.
Run centre logistics, scheduling, attendance, exams, infrastructure, student/parent support and grievance redressal.
Fee accounting, installment/refund management, GST/TDS/payroll compliance, statutory filings and MIS.
Run LMS, app, online classes, proctoring, recorded content and data/analytics on learning.

operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Enrollments crash or students follow a teacher who quits or starts a rival institute nearby.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Revenue volatility, batch closures, brand erosion in a hyper-local market.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Teaching quality concentrated in individuals; weak content standardisation, no recorded/IP layer, no non-compete or retention incentives.

operational_bottlenecks.bottleneck: Low counselling-to-enrollment conversion and lead leakage
operational_bottlenecks.symptom: High ad spend and walk-ins but admissions don't convert; follow-ups dropped on paper registers/WhatsApp.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Inflated CAC, unfilled batches below break-even fill-rate, wasted marketing budget.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: No CRM or structured follow-up cadence; counsellor incentives misaligned; leads tracked manually.

operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Students stop attending after 1-2 installments; refund disputes; receivables on EMI-financed fees go bad.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Revenue reversal, locked capacity, bad debt, and negative word-of-mouth.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: No early at-risk detection (attendance/score drop), weak parent engagement, over-promising outcomes at sale, no structured renewal/retention play.

operational_bottlenecks.bottleneck: Severe demand seasonality with fixed cost base
operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Premises and core faculty sit idle Aug-Oct while peak intake overwhelms capacity Apr-Jul.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Poor asset/faculty utilisation, cash crunch in lean months, rushed hiring at peak.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Single-product/single-season offering, no off-season revenue (online, short courses, B2B), no rolling-batch model.

operational_bottlenecks.bottleneck: Inconsistent quality and results across branches/batches
operational_bottlenecks.symptom: One branch produces selections, another doesn't; parents compare and complain.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Hard to scale franchise/multi-branch; brand promise breaks; refund pressure.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: No standardised teaching SOP, content kit, faculty training or outcome-tracking discipline across locations.

operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Cannot prove selection/placement claims; ASCI/competition scrutiny on misleading ads.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Trust deficit, advertising-compliance risk, weaker premium pricing power.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: No clean student-outcome data trail; over-aggressive marketing claims not backed by verifiable records.

ai_automation_opportunities.opportunity: AI lead-scoring + automated multi-channel follow-up (WhatsApp/call/SMS) that ranks inquiries by conversion likelihood and never drops a follow-up, lifting counsellor productivity and cutting CAC.
At-risk dropout early-warning model using attendance, test-score trend and fee-installment behaviour to trigger mentor/parent intervention before churn and protect installment receivables.
AI-generated and standardised content/test-series + auto-graded assessments and doubt-solving chatbot, reducing star-faculty dependency and enabling scalable, consistent delivery across branches.
Automated fee, installment-reminder, refund and GST/TDS-compliant receipting workflow with reconciliation MIS, cutting collection leakage and compliance errors.
Hyper-local competitor and demand intelligence (fees, batch offers, faculty moves, search-trend by exam/skill) to time campaigns and price batches.
Standardised teaching, admission and exam-conduct SOPs auto-generated and version-controlled for consistent multi-branch/franchise rollout.

consulting_frameworks.framework: Unit economics (CAC vs LTV per student)
consulting_frameworks.use: Compute cost to acquire one admission (ad+counsellor cost / enrollments) against lifetime fee value including renewals/upsell; target LTV:CAC >= 3:1 and CAC payback within first installment cycle.
Identify the binding constraint each season — counselling conversion in peak intake, faculty capacity at scale, or classroom seats — and invest there rather than spreading effort.
Map the student journey from inquiry to enrollment to outcome to alumni referral, instrumenting drop-off at each stage to fix the weakest step.
Frame the real job a parent/learner hires the institute for (rank/selection, a job, a licence, confidence) to design course bundles, guarantees and messaging that beat generic competitors.
Exploit upfront and installment fee collection against deferred salary/rent payouts to run on negative working capital, while reserving for refunds and dropout reversals.
Clarify ownership across admissions, academics, operations and finance for handoffs like lead-to-counsellor, fee-to-receipt, result-to-marketing, avoiding dropped students.
Set the minimum students-per-batch where contribution covers faculty+room cost, and gate batch launch and discounting decisions on it.

risk_model.risk: Misleading-advertising / outcome-claim scrutiny (selection %, guaranteed jobs/ranks) inviting ASCI, consumer and CCPA action
risk_model.control: Back every result claim with verifiable student records, add disclaimers, pre-vet creatives; maintain an auditable outcome database.

risk_model.risk: Fee refund disputes and unfair-contract clauses (non-refundable fees, EMI-financed dropouts) leading to consumer complaints
risk_model.control: Clear, fair, written fee-and-refund policy in the enrollment contract; transparent installment terms; documented grievance redressal.

risk_model.risk: GST mis-classification of coaching/vocational services and incorrect ITC/exemption treatment
risk_model.control: Correctly apply 18% GST on commercial coaching, distinguish exempt approved-vocational/recognised-education services, maintain tax invoices and reconcile ITC.

risk_model.risk: Faculty attrition / poaching with students migrating to a competing institute
risk_model.control: Standardise content and record lectures (IP retention), retention bonuses, reasonable non-compete/non-solicit clauses, batch ownership by institute not individual.

risk_model.risk: Labour & payroll non-compliance for faculty/staff (EPF/ESI, contract vs employee mis-classification)
risk_model.control: Register and remit EPF/ESI where thresholds apply, issue proper contracts, run compliant payroll with TDS on salaries.

risk_model.risk: Student data privacy breach (minors' data, marks, payment info) under DPDP
risk_model.control: Consent-based data collection (verifiable parental consent for minors), access controls on LMS/CRM, breach-response plan, vendor data agreements.

risk_model.risk: Seasonal cash-flow shortfall and over-leverage on premises/expansion
risk_model.control: Build off-season revenue (online/short courses/B2B), maintain 3-4 month cash runway, avoid fixed-cost expansion ahead of validated demand.

risk_model.risk: Shops & Establishment / premises and safety non-registration for the centre
risk_model.control: Obtain Shops & Establishment registration, fire/safety NOC, and adhere to state coaching-regulation norms where applicable.

kpi_structure.definition: Paid admissions divided by qualified leads/walk-ins in a period.
Enrolled students divided by planned/break-even batch capacity.
Total marketing + admission-sales cost divided by number of enrollments.
Students completing the course vs total enrolled (inverse of dropout).
Fees actually collected vs fees committed/due (incl. installments).
Students achieving the promised outcome vs eligible students appearing.
kpi_structure.healthy: At or above local-market benchmark for the exam/skill

kpi_structure.definition: Total faculty compensation as a percentage of revenue.

unit_economics: Test-prep/coaching annual ticket: ₹25,000-₹1,50,000 per student (premium JEE/NEET/UPSC programs ₹1-2.5 lakh); contribution per student after direct faculty+material cost ₹12,000-₹70,000.
Vocational/skill course ticket: ₹8,000-₹60,000; CAC ₹1,500-₹6,000 per enrollment via digital + local; payback within first installment.
A single classroom batch of 30-60 students breaks even around 18-25 students once faculty+room cost is covered; marginal student is near-pure contribution.
Online/hybrid subscription: ₹500-₹3,000/month; gross margin 70-85% once content is produced, but CAC and churn determine profitability.
profitability_analysis.working_capital_notes: Structurally negative working capital is achievable: fees collected upfront or in monthly installments while faculty salaries and rent are paid in arrears — many institutes run on student cash. The discipline is to reserve for refunds/dropout reversals, avoid over-collecting EMI-financed fees that can go bad, and not lock peak-season cash into off-season fixed costs. DSO on B2B/college-training contracts can run 45-90 days; chase advances.
levers: Lift batch fill-rate and counselling conversion — the fastest margin lever since incremental students are near-pure contribution.
Standardise content and reduce star-faculty dependency to control the largest cost line and enable scale.
Add high-margin off-season and online/subscription + material revenue to amortise fixed premises/faculty cost across the year.
Cut CAC via referrals, alumni, school tie-ups and organic result-led brand instead of paid ads.
Tighten installment realisation and dropout retention to stop revenue reversal and bad debt.

pm_workflows.cadence: Quarterly run-up to each intake (esp. Jan-Mar for Apr-Jul intake), weekly stand-ups
milestones: Set enrollment & revenue targets and break-even fill per batch
Launch scholarship test + multi-channel campaign with tracked CRM funnel
Daily counsellor conversion review during peak
Close batches, post-mortem on CAC and conversion by channel

pm_workflows.cadence: One-time build then per-term refresh, monthly review
milestones: Map syllabus to standardised lesson kits and recorded lectures
Train all faculty/branches on the kit

pm_workflows.cadence: Continuous; weekly at-risk review, monthly parent reviews
milestones: Deploy attendance + score dashboard with at-risk flags
Define intervention SOP (mentor call, parent meeting)
Track completion and installment realisation weekly
Secure premises, licences (Shops & Estab, fire NOC), faculty
Replicate standardised SOP + content + brand kit
Hit batch break-even fill within first two intakes

key_activities: Identify exam/skill demand and target outcome
Design syllabus, schedule, fee structure and batch model
Develop content, study material and mock-test bank
Define faculty profile and teaching SOP
Run demand-gen campaigns, seminars, scholarship tests
Counsel and convert leads, collect fees / set installments
Form batches to break-even fill, allocate faculty and rooms
Run periodic tests, track attendance and learning outcomes
Engage parents/students, intervene on at-risk learners
Conduct final assessments / prep for board/competitive exams
Capture verifiable outcome data for credibility and marketing
Renew / upsell to next level or advanced program
Gather feedback, refine content and faculty for next cohort

stages.focus: Prove outcomes and unit economics in one location with a tight product
plays: Win on results in 1-2 flagship courses; convert into referral engine
Install CRM + structured counselling cadence to lift conversion
Standardise content so delivery isn't one-teacher-dependent
Reach break-even batch fill before adding courses

stages.focus: De-seasonalise and densify the existing catchment
plays: Add adjacent courses, foundation/junior batches and short/off-season programs
Launch online/hybrid + recorded content to amortise fixed cost and add margin
School/college tie-ups and corporate B2B training for steady demand
Build faculty bench and retention incentives to reduce poaching risk

stages.focus: Replicate a standardised, brand-led model across geographies
plays: Codify SOPs, content kit, brand and outcome-tracking for franchise/own-branch rollout
Centralise marketing, finance and quality MIS across branches
Layer a scalable edtech/app product for pan-India reach and recurring revenue
Pursue institutional capital/credit (RBI MSME credit, DPIIT incentives if tech-product arm) for expansion

digital_maturity_model.name: Manual / paper
signals: Admissions and fees tracked in registers/receipt books
Leads on WhatsApp and paper inquiry slips
Attendance and marks on paper; no MIS
digital_maturity_model.next_step: Move fee, admission and attendance records into a basic spreadsheet/Tally and a single CRM sheet.

digital_maturity_model.name: Digitised records
signals: Tally/Excel for fees and accounts; GST invoices generated
Basic LMS or WhatsApp groups for content sharing
Leads captured in a spreadsheet/CRM but follow-up still manual
digital_maturity_model.next_step: Adopt a proper CRM with follow-up cadence and an integrated fee/installment + LMS system.

digital_maturity_model.name: Integrated systems
signals: CRM-driven admissions funnel with stage tracking
Integrated LMS, online classes, fee/installment software and payroll
Dashboards for enrollment, collection and attendance
digital_maturity_model.next_step: Connect data sources into a single MIS and start tracking conversion, retention and CAC analytics.

digital_maturity_model.name: Data-driven
signals: Unified analytics on conversion, batch fill, CAC/LTV, retention and outcomes
Automated fee reminders, marketing attribution by channel
Cross-branch performance benchmarking from one dashboard
digital_maturity_model.next_step: Introduce predictive models (dropout risk, lead scoring) and automate routine counselling/support.

digital_maturity_model.name: AI-native
signals: AI lead-scoring + automated multi-channel follow-up
Predictive dropout intervention and personalised learning paths
AI content generation, auto-grading, doubt-bots and outcome forecasting feeding strategy
digital_maturity_model.next_step: Continuously retrain models on outcome data and expand AI personalisation into adaptive curriculum and pricing.

playbooks.name: Textile Businesses
playbooks.one_liner: A small-to-mid Indian textile MSME spanning yarn spinning, weaving/knitting, processing, and garment manufacturing that supplies fabric or finished apparel to domestic wholesalers, brands, and export buyers on largely order-driven, working-capital-heavy production.

operating_model.summary: Order-to-cash, conversion-margin business: a textile MSME buys cotton/yarn/grey fabric or raw cloth, converts it through labour- and power-intensive steps (spinning, weaving/knitting, dyeing/processing, cutting-stitching-finishing), and sells fabric by the metre or garments by the piece to wholesalers, brands, exporters or government tenders. Profit lives in the conversion spread, machine utilisation, and disciplined working-capital recycling on thin per-unit margins.
revenue_streams: Job-work / CMT (cut-make-trim) conversion charges where the buyer supplies fabric or yarn — pure conversion fee, low capital risk
Own-account fabric sales (by the metre / per kg) to wholesalers, traders and garment units in hubs like Surat, Erode, Bhiwandi, Ichalkaranti
Finished garment sales to domestic brands, large-format retail, and B2B wholesale (Tirupur, Ludhiana, Delhi)
Direct/indirect exports to buyers in US/EU/Middle East, often under buying-house or LC terms
Value-added services: dyeing/printing/embroidery/processing as a standalone service line; deadstock and fabric-waste (jhut/chindi) sales
cost_structure: Raw material — cotton, yarn, grey fabric, dyes & chemicals (typically 55-70% of cost; the single biggest and most volatile line)
Power & fuel — spinning/processing are highly energy-intensive (8-18% of cost; coal/gas/grid + DG backup)
Direct labour & contract/piece-rate workers — migrant-heavy, seasonal (10-18%)
Job-work paid out to external processors (dyeing, embroidery, washing) when not in-house
Machinery EMI/lease, maintenance & spares, factory rent, ETP/effluent compliance, freight & packing
value_drivers: Machine and capacity utilisation % (idle looms/spindles/stitching lines destroy margin)
Conversion cost per unit (per kg yarn, per metre fabric, per garment SMV) vs cluster benchmark
Working-capital velocity — inventory turns and receivable days, given the cash trapped in cotton-to-cash cycle
Right-first-time quality / low rejection & rework rate (shade matching, GSM consistency, stitching defects)
Buyer concentration and order-book visibility / repeat order ratio

value_chain: Fibre & raw material sourcing (cotton/PSF/yarn/grey fabric via mandi, ginners, yarn agents, importers)
Spinning (fibre to yarn) — for integrated units
Fabric formation — weaving / knitting (own looms or job-work powerlooms)
Wet processing — dyeing, printing, finishing (in-house or sent to processing houses + ETP)
Garmenting — design/sampling, cutting, stitching, embroidery/washing, finishing
Quality inspection (in-line + AQL final), packing & labelling
Dispatch & logistics (domestic transport / export consolidation at port/ICD)
Order-to-cash — invoicing, GST/e-invoice, collections, deadstock liquidation

core_processes.description: Convert a buyer enquiry/PO into a costed sheet — yarn/fabric BOM, consumption per piece, SMV-based labour cost, processing & overhead, target margin — and confirm delivery date against capacity. Weak costing here silently kills profitability.

Sequence orders across spindles/looms/stitching lines to maximise utilisation, balance style changeovers, and hit delivery dates; coordinate yarn/fabric availability and in/out job-work so machines never starve.
Lock raw material against confirmed orders, manage lot/shade/GSM consistency, inspect inwards (count, shade, defects), and reconcile 3-way against PO/GRN to control the 60%+ material cost.
Dyeing/printing recipe control, shade approval against buyer swatch, lab dips, and ETP/effluent compliance — the highest-rejection, highest-pollution-risk stage.
In-line checks plus AQL-based final audit on measurements, stitching, shade and packing to control rejection, claims, chargebacks and shipment rejects (critical for export buyers).
Pack, label, raise GST/e-invoice + e-way bill (and export docs/LUT for exports), dispatch, and chase receivables — the step that converts finished goods into cash and recycles working capital.

department_structure.mandate: Run spinning/weaving/processing/garmenting to plan at target efficiency, quality and cost; own machine utilisation, SMV/efficiency, rejection and on-time completion.
Win and own orders end-to-end — costing, buyer/agent relationships, sampling, order follow-up (T&A), and order-book/margin protection.
Enforce inward, in-line and final AQL standards; manage shade approvals, lab dips, rejections, rework and buyer claims/chargebacks.
Procure yarn/fabric/dyes/trims against orders at right cost/quality, manage lots/shades, and control raw material + WIP + finished-goods inventory and job-work in/out.
Manage working capital, costing/cost-sheets, GST/e-invoice/e-way, factory & labour compliance, ETP/pollution-board obligations, and lender relationships.
Recruit and retain migrant/contract labour, manage piece-rate wages, statutory labour compliance, canteen/hostel, and reduce absenteeism/attrition.

operational_bottlenecks.bottleneck: Cotton & yarn price volatility crushing locked-in margins
operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Orders quoted weeks earlier turn loss-making when cotton/yarn spikes; frequent re-negotiation or absorbing the hit
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Gross margin swings of 5-10 percentage points; episodic losses on confirmed order books
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Open exposure to commodity (MCX cotton, MSP, import duty on cotton/PSF) with no hedging or price-escalation clause, and costing not refreshed against live yarn rates

operational_bottlenecks.bottleneck: Low / erratic machine and line efficiency
operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Looms/stitching lines run at 45-60% of standard; high idle time on style changeovers and yarn/fabric stock-outs
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Fixed cost (power, rent, EMI, supervisor) spread over fewer good units; conversion cost per piece runs 15-30% above cluster benchmark
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: No SMV/IE discipline, poor line loading and feeding, frequent machine breakdowns from deferred maintenance, and unbalanced bottleneck operations

operational_bottlenecks.bottleneck: Working capital trapped in inventory and receivables
operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Cotton-to-cash cycle of 90-150 days; raw material and deadstock piling up; buyers/wholesalers paying at 60-120 days while suppliers want cash/short credit
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Chronic cash crunch, dependence on costly informal credit / over-utilised CC limits, inability to take large orders
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Speculative raw-material buying, slow-moving fabric/deadstock, weak collections discipline, and a structural credit-period mismatch between purchase and sale

operational_bottlenecks.bottleneck: Quality rejection, shade mismatch & buyer chargebacks
operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Repeat lots fail shade/GSM/measurement; export shipments get claims, discounts or rejection; rework eats capacity
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Rejection/rework of 5-12%, margin erosion, and loss of repeat buyers / order cancellations
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Inconsistent dye-recipe and process control, no robust AQL/lab-dip system, undertrained operators, and reliance on uncontrolled external processing houses

operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Lines under-manned post-festival/harvest; trained tailors and dyeing operators leave; 8-15% daily absenteeism
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Missed delivery dates, overtime cost, and quality dips from constant retraining of new hands
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Heavy dependence on migrant/contract labour, seasonal pull of agriculture and hometown festivals, piece-rate insecurity, and limited welfare/housing

operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Processing units face consent-to-operate scrutiny, ETP load violations, and shutdown notices; CETP issues in clusters
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Risk of plant closure, penalties, and disqualification from compliance-audited export buyers
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Wet processing generates effluent; under-investment in/inconsistent ETP operation and weak environmental documentation

ai_automation_opportunities.opportunity: AI-driven order costing engine that pulls live yarn/cotton rates and BOM/SMV consumption to flag loss-making quotes before acceptance and suggest a price-escalation clause
Automated working-capital and collections cockpit — DSO/DIO/deadstock ageing, CC-limit utilisation, and Sec 43B(h) 45-day MSME-supplier payment alerts with auto-reminders to slow-paying buyers
Production planning / line-loading optimiser that sequences orders across looms/stitching lines to lift utilisation, minimise changeovers and protect delivery dates
Computer-vision fabric & garment defect detection (holes, stains, shade variance, stitching defects) and AQL automation to cut rejection and buyer chargebacks
GST e-invoice + e-way bill auto-generation on dispatch and ITC reconciliation across yarn/dye/job-work vendors
Inventory & lot/shade tracking with reorder points for yarn/fabric/trims and deadstock liquidation suggestions to free trapped cash
Export compliance copilot for RoDTEP/duty-drawback claims, LUT/shipping-bill docs and AEPC/buyer-code compliance for apparel exporters
Demand & trend forecasting from buyer history and seasonality to plan raw-material buying and reduce speculative cotton purchases

consulting_frameworks.use: Identify the true bottleneck operation (often dyeing/finishing or a specific stitching operation) and subordinate scheduling to it — raising throughput without buying more machines.
Map fibre to finished-garment to decide where this MSME captures margin (CMT vs own-fabric vs integrated) and whether to insource or job-out processing/embroidery.
Quantify DIO + DSO − DPO across the cotton-to-cash cycle and attack the largest leg (usually inventory + deadstock) to release locked cash.

consulting_frameworks.framework: Unit economics (per kg / per metre / per garment)
consulting_frameworks.use: Build true conversion cost per unit including power, labour SMV, rejection and overhead — compare to cluster benchmark to price and prioritise profitable order types.
Cut changeover time between styles/shades and shop-floor waste (jhut, rework, motion) to raise line efficiency and on-time delivery.
Clarify ownership across merchandising, production, QA and stores for the order-to-dispatch handoffs where delays and quality slips usually occur.
Standard garment-export merchandising tool — back-schedule fabric, trims, sampling, production and inspection milestones from the ship date to prevent air-freight penalties.

risk_model.risk: Cotton/yarn commodity price shock erodes confirmed-order margins
risk_model.control: Refresh cost sheets against live yarn rates, insert price-escalation clauses, back-to-back raw-material booking on order confirmation, limited forward booking

risk_model.risk: Buyer default / concentration and stretched receivables
risk_model.control: Credit limits per buyer, advance/LC for exports and new buyers, diversify buyer base, enforce Sec 43B(h) discipline and trade-credit insurance

risk_model.risk: ETP / pollution-board non-compliance leading to plant closure
risk_model.control: Maintain consent-to-operate, run/monitor ETP within norms, periodic effluent testing, connect to CETP where available, environmental documentation

risk_model.risk: Labour & factory statutory non-compliance (PF/ESI/wages/contract labour)
risk_model.control: Registered contractor agreements, timely EPF/ESI remittance, wage registers, factory licence and labour-code adherence, time-office automation

risk_model.risk: Export shipment rejection / chargeback on quality or delay
risk_model.control: AQL inspection regime, lab dips and shade approvals, T&A calendar discipline, in-line QA, buyer compliance audits

risk_model.risk: GST/e-way bill and ITC mismatch on yarn/job-work invoices
risk_model.control: Auto e-invoice/e-way on dispatch, monthly ITC reconciliation with vendors, correct HSN/rate (inverted-duty awareness on fabric/garments)

risk_model.risk: Over-investment in machinery against an unstable order book
risk_model.control: Capex tied to confirmed order/utilisation thresholds, TUFS/cluster-scheme leverage, lease vs buy analysis, maintain utilisation KPI gate

kpi_structure.definition: Actual good output vs rated/standard capacity (spindle/loom/stitching-line basis or SMV efficiency)
Pieces or metres rejected or reworked as a share of total produced (in-line + final)
Days inventory outstanding + days sales outstanding − days payable outstanding across the cotton-to-cash cycle
Orders shipped complete by the committed/ship date
Sale price minus material and direct conversion cost per kg/metre/garment
Worker-days absent vs scheduled worker-days

kpi_structure.kpi: Deadstock / slow-moving inventory (% of inventory value)
kpi_structure.definition: Value of fabric/yarn/trims with no movement beyond a set ageing threshold

profitability_analysis.typical_gross_margin: 18-30% (CMT/job-work units at the lower end; integrated or value-added/printed-embroidered fabric at the higher end)
unit_economics: Job-work CMT garment: conversion charge ₹35-90/piece against SMV-based cost; net ₹5-15/piece after labour, power and overhead at 70%+ line efficiency

Own-account fabric: sells ₹60-180/metre with ₹12-30/metre contribution after yarn, processing and conversion; a 30-loom unit doing ~3-4 lakh metres/month nets a few lakh ₹ only if utilisation stays above ~70%
Spinning: yarn conversion spread of ₹15-40/kg over cotton cost, highly sensitive to power tariff and cotton-to-yarn realisation
profitability_analysis.working_capital_notes: Working-capital intensive: 25-40% of annual turnover is typically locked in inventory + receivables. Raw material is bought near-cash or 7-30 day credit while wholesale/brand buyers pay at 45-120 days, creating a structural gap funded by cash-credit limits (often 80-100% utilised). Deadstock and speculative cotton buying are the silent cash traps; festival/season cycles (Diwali, wedding, summer) swing inventory sharply.
levers: Lift machine/line utilisation above 70% to spread fixed costs (single biggest profit lever)
Cut rejection/rework and shade failures through QA and process control to recover lost margin and avoid chargebacks
Tighten the cash cycle — reduce deadstock, enforce collection terms, align supplier credit, and recycle CC limits faster
Shift mix toward value-added (printed, embroidered, finished, branded) and reduce pure low-margin CMT dependence
Reduce power cost via energy-efficient motors, solar, and TUFS-backed machinery upgrades; renegotiate yarn buying in larger consolidated lots

pm_workflows.initiative: New buyer / export order onboarding and execution
pm_workflows.cadence: Per order, with weekly T&A review

milestones: SMED changeover & line-balancing pilot on one line
CC-limit utilisation and CCC improvement confirmed
ETP load and effluent test results

key_activities: In-line quality checks and WIP control

stages.focus: Make the core profitable and reliable before scaling
plays: Fix costing so no order is taken below true conversion cost
Lift line/machine utilisation above 70% via planning and maintenance
Get GST, factory, ETP and labour compliance clean
Tighten collections and stop speculative raw-material buying

stages.focus: Move up the value chain and reduce buyer concentration
plays: Shift mix from pure CMT to own-fabric and value-added (print/embroidery/finishing)
Diversify buyers across domestic brands, wholesale and exports
Implement QA/AQL to win compliance-audited buyers
Avail TUFS/cluster/MSME schemes to modernise machinery and add solar/energy efficiency

stages.focus: Capacity, capability and capital for larger, stickier order books
plays: Build dedicated export merchandising and social/buyer-compliance certification
Add capacity tied to confirmed utilisation, not speculation
Integrate ERP across costing, production, inventory and finance
Tap export incentives (RoDTEP/drawback) and structured working-capital/term finance for growth

digital_maturity_model.name: Manual / paper-and-register
signals: Production, stock and wages tracked in registers and diaries
Costing on paper or memory; no per-order profitability
Billing via standalone software or by hand
digital_maturity_model.next_step: Move billing/GST and basic stock to Tally or a billing app; start recording per-order cost sheets digitally

digital_maturity_model.name: Digitised accounting & billing

Some Excel for stock and order tracking
e-invoice/e-way generated but disconnected from production
digital_maturity_model.next_step: Adopt a textile/garment ERP module for orders, BOM, inventory and job-work in/out so data is captured at source

digital_maturity_model.name: Integrated ERP / shop-floor data
signals: ERP links orders, BOM, inventory, production and finance
Line efficiency, rejection and WIP captured per shift/order
Job-work in/out and lot/shade tracked in system
digital_maturity_model.next_step: Add dashboards and exception alerts (utilisation, OTIF, DSO, deadstock) and start data-driven planning

digital_maturity_model.name: Data-driven & dashboarded
signals: Live KPI dashboards for management (efficiency, CCC, OTIF, margin)
Planning and procurement informed by demand/seasonality data
Automated compliance and collection reminders
digital_maturity_model.next_step: Introduce AI for costing-against-live-rates, demand forecasting, planning optimisation and vision-based QC pilots

digital_maturity_model.name: AI-native operations
signals: AI optimises line loading, raw-material buying and pricing in near real time
Computer-vision defect detection in QA
Predictive maintenance and prescriptive working-capital management
digital_maturity_model.next_step: Continuously retrain models on order/quality/market data and extend AI across the full order-to-cash value chain

playbooks.name: Electronics Distribution

ai_automation_opportunities.opportunity: Auto-replenishment engine that reads secondary sales + stock-in-hand by SKU/colour/variant and fires PO suggestions to brands/national distributors, sized to credit-period and slab targets, cutting dead-stock and stockouts on fast-moving handsets.
AI receivables chaser that ages every retailer ledger, predicts default risk from payment history, and auto-sends WhatsApp/IVR reminders with UPI collection links before the credit period lapses.
GST + e-invoice + e-way bill automation: auto-generate IRN and e-way bills from the sales order, reconcile GSTR-2B vs purchase register so ITC on high-value imported stock is never lost.

Beat-plan optimiser and salesman tracking: cluster 200-800 retail outlets by potential and geography, sequence daily beats, flag no-order outlets and detect under-servicing, lifting numeric distribution.

Scheme/claim reconciliation bot that parses brand price-protection, slab incentive and breakage circulars, computes accrued claims per SKU and reconciles against credit notes received, recovering leaked margin.

Price-erosion radar: scrape Flipkart/Amazon/online grey-market prices per model daily, alert when street price falls below landed cost so the owner liquidates ageing stock before NLC (new lower cost) revisions hit.
Import landed-cost + duty calculator tied to bill-of-entry data, FX rate and BIS/WPC compliance check before a container is booked.
Retailer credit-scoring and dynamic credit-limit engine using ledger ageing, bounce history and order velocity to set exposure caps and prevent bad-debt concentration.

consulting_frameworks.use: Electronics distribution lives and dies on the gap between supplier credit (often 0-21 days or cash for imports) and retailer credit (21-45 days) plus inventory days; model DIO+DSO-DPO to expose the financing gap funding it through channel finance.

Identify whether the binding constraint is working capital, warehouse pick-pack throughput, salesman beat capacity, or brand allocation, and subordinate everything to relieving that one constraint instead of chasing topline.

Compute true per-unit contribution after scheme accruals, breakage, financing cost of credit days and freight; reveals that high-turnover handsets at 2-4% can be loss-making once receivable-financing cost is loaded, while accessories at 18-30% carry the business.

Map brand/importer to super-stockist to distributor to retailer to consumer, locating where margin, claims and risk sit, and decide which links (e.g. own retail, online B2B) to integrate forward into.

Classify SKUs by value (A/B/C) and demand volatility (X/Y/Z) to set differentiated stock norms - tight on volatile high-value handsets, generous on stable accessories - controlling obsolescence in a sector with 6-9 month model cycles.

Clarify ownership across owner, sales head, warehouse, accounts and collections for scheme claims, credit approval and stock liability, which are the most commonly dropped responsibilities in family-run distributorships.

risk_model.risk: Price erosion / inventory obsolescence: brand cuts NLC or launches successor model, instantly devaluing on-hand stock bought at old cost.
risk_model.control: Cap days-of-inventory on high-value SKUs to under 21 days, negotiate written price-protection clauses, age-track stock weekly and liquidate slow movers before circulars hit.

risk_model.risk: Receivable concentration and bad debt: top 10 retailers carry oversized credit and a single default wipes a quarter's margin.
risk_model.control: Dynamic credit limits, PDC/UPI mandates, monthly ledger confirmation, and Section 43B(h) discipline on the payables side to protect own cash.

risk_model.risk: GST ITC mismatch / blocked input credit on high-value imported and locally bought stock due to supplier non-filing or e-way bill lapses.
risk_model.control: Monthly GSTR-2B reconciliation, hold payment of GST portion till supplier files, mandatory e-invoice + e-way bill on every dispatch.

risk_model.risk: Grey-market and parallel imports / counterfeit handsets undercutting authorised price and exposing the distributor to brand de-listing.
risk_model.control: Buy only against tax invoice with IMEI capture, verify BIS/WPC marking, avoid cash-channel sourcing, audit supplier provenance.

risk_model.risk: Import compliance failure: missing BIS registration, WPC/ETA, or wrong HSN/duty classification leading to seizure or penalty at customs.
risk_model.control: Pre-shipment BIS/CRS check, correct HSN classification, valid IEC, customs broker review of bill of entry before clearance.

risk_model.risk: Brand/distributorship termination or territory reallocation removing the core revenue line at short notice.
risk_model.control: Diversify across 2-3 brands and into accessories/IT, document performance to defend territory, formalise notice and stock-buyback terms in the agreement.

risk_model.risk: Cash-flow squeeze from mismatch between cash-on-import buying and credit selling, worsened by GST outflow timing.
risk_model.control: Channel financing / supplier bill discounting, weekly cash-flow forecast, align purchase pace to collection velocity.

playbooks.one_liner: A working-capital-intensive B2B trading MSME that buys mobile handsets, gadgets and accessories from brands/importers in bulk and redistributes them on credit to a beat of Tier-2/3 retailers, earning thin per-unit margins amplified by volume, schemes and turns.

operating_model.summary: Buy bulk inventory from OEM brands, national distributors or via import on cash/short credit; warehouse and break bulk; sell on 21-45 day credit to a network of multi-brand retailers and sub-dealers across a defined territory via a salesman beat, monetising volume rebates, brand schemes and accessory attach rather than headline margin.
revenue_streams: Primary trading margin on handsets/devices (thin, 2-5%)
High-margin accessories, chargers, cases, audio, screen-guards (18-35%)
Brand scheme income: slab incentives, quarterly QPS, display/visibility payouts, price protection
Value-added services: activation/insurance attach, EMI facilitation commission, repair/spares pass-through
Sub-distribution / C&F fees for secondary territories
cost_structure: Cost of goods (85-92% of revenue) - the dominant line
Working-capital finance cost on inventory + receivables (interest 11-18% p.a.)
Salesman salaries + incentives, delivery/logistics and fuel
Warehouse rent, insurance, shrinkage/breakage and obsolescence write-downs
GST cash-flow timing and compliance/accounting overhead
value_drivers: Inventory turns (the single biggest lever - 12-24x annually on handsets)
Numeric + weighted retail distribution (outlets billed per month)
Scheme/claim capture rate and on-time reconciliation
Receivable discipline (low DSO, near-zero bad debt)
Accessory and high-margin mix as % of revenue

value_chain: Import clearance / inbound goods receipt & QC (IMEI/serial capture)
After-sales / warranty & returns routing to brand

core_processes.description: Salesman books order on app during beat, credit check auto-runs, e-invoice + e-way bill generate, goods dispatch, retailer ledger debited, collection chased to closure - target cycle 21-35 days.
Demand-driven PO to brand, GRN with IMEI/serial scan, 3-way match (PO-GRN-invoice), payment within agreed credit honouring Section 43B(h) timelines.
Capture brand circulars, accrue incentives per SKU/slab at sale, file claims monthly, reconcile credit notes received vs accrued, escalate shortfalls - protects the real margin.
Weekly age-bucket review by model, liquidate >21-day high-value stock, ABC-XYZ stock norms, breakage/obsolescence provisioning.

department_structure.mandate: Maximise numeric/weighted distribution, secondary sales and scheme achievement across the territory beat.
Accurate goods receipt with serial capture, zero-shrinkage storage, fast pick-pack-dispatch and last-mile delivery.
Fund the working-capital cycle, control credit exposure, drive collections, manage GST and bank limits.
Negotiate allocation and credit with brands, manage imports/customs/BIS, accrue and reconcile all scheme claims.
Capital allocation, brand relationships, GST/Udyam/statutory compliance and overall P&L ownership.

operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Warehouse full of last-quarter models that must be sold below cost; cash always tight despite high turnover.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Margin evaporates into obsolescence write-downs; inability to fund new high-demand launches.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Over-buying against slab targets and brand push without demand-linked replenishment, in a category with 6-9 month model lifecycles and frequent NLC cuts.

operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Retailer ledgers run past agreed days, no PDC/UPI mandate, owner personally chases dues.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: DSO drifts to 45-70+ days, bad debts on weak retailers, and a permanent working-capital hole.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Credit extended on relationship/trust without limits or ageing discipline; collections not systematised or incentivised.

operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Brand incentives accrued mentally, claims filed late or partially, credit notes not reconciled.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: 2-4% of the real margin - often the difference between profit and loss - silently lost.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Schemes tracked on paper/WhatsApp, no SKU-level accrual at point of sale, no reconciliation discipline against brand portals.

operational_bottlenecks.bottleneck: GST / ITC and e-way bill friction
operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Blocked input credit from supplier non-filing, dispatches delayed for e-way bill, GSTR-2B mismatches.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Locked-up ITC on high-value stock, penalties, and cash-flow timing stress around GST due dates.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Manual billing not integrated with e-invoice/e-way bill, no monthly 2B reconciliation, payment released before supplier compliance verified.

operational_bottlenecks.symptom: 60-80% of revenue from one brand; allocation cuts during shortages, territory poaching by parallel distributors.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Existential revenue concentration and weak negotiating power on credit and schemes.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Single-brand comfort and lack of diversification into accessories, IT products or second brands.

kpi_structure.definition: COGS divided by average inventory at cost, for the period annualised.
Average receivables divided by daily credit sales.
(Net sales minus COGS, including scheme income) divided by net sales.
Value of stock aged over 45 days as a percentage of total inventory value.
Unique retail outlets billed in the month versus total mapped universe.
Claims realised as credit notes divided by claims accrued.

unit_economics: A ₹15,000 handset sells at ~3% gross = ₹450; financing 30 credit-days at 14% p.a. eats ~₹175, leaving ~₹275 before opex - razor thin
An accessory basket of ₹500 at 25% margin = ₹125 contribution on tiny capital - why attach rate drives the P&L
Monthly throughput of ₹2 cr at 6% blended margin = ₹12 lakh gross; ₹8-9 lakh opex+finance leaves ₹3-4 lakh net
profitability_analysis.working_capital_notes: Cycle is the core problem: imports/brand buys are cash or 0-21 day credit while retail sells at 21-45 days plus 15-25 inventory days, creating a 30-50 day funding gap. A ₹24 cr/yr distributor typically needs ₹2-3.5 cr of working capital, financed through channel finance, cash credit (CC) or bill discounting at 11-18% - that finance cost is the make-or-break line.
levers: Lift inventory turns (every extra turn frees lakhs of trapped cash)
Cut DSO via PDC/UPI mandates and tiered credit limits
Maximise scheme/claim capture and reconciliation
Grow high-margin accessory mix to lift blended margin
Negotiate longer brand credit / channel finance to shrink the funding gap

milestones: Liquidate aged stock + renegotiate brand credit
Re-measure cash conversion cycle and lock gains
Tie incentives to weighted distribution + range selling
Auto-accrue incentives per SKU at sale
Integrate billing with IRN + e-way bill

key_activities: Negotiate brand/distributor agreement, territory, credit & scheme terms
Set up imports (IEC, BIS, customs broker) if applicable
Receive goods with IMEI/serial capture & QC
Define stock norms and pricing per channel
Run beat plan and secondary sales
Execute brand schemes, visibility and range-selling
Liquidate slow movers before NLC cuts
Wind down end-of-life models, claim price protection

stages.focus: Secure brand allocation, build a tight beat, and instil credit + inventory discipline before scaling.
plays: Lock 1-2 strong brands with written credit/scheme terms
Digitise billing with e-invoice/e-way bill from day one
Set hard credit limits and weekly ageing review
Push accessory attach to lift blended margin

stages.focus: Densify territory and turns, professionalise finance, and reduce single-brand dependence.
plays: Add complementary brands and IT/accessory lines
Deploy salesman app + secondary-sales analytics
Arrange channel finance to widen credit headroom
Build a claims/scheme reconciliation function

stages.focus: Network expansion, forward integration and category diversification with institutional controls.
plays: Add sub-distributors / new territories or C&F
Forward-integrate into B2B e-commerce / own retail
Pursue super-stockist status for higher volumes
Diversify into adjacent categories (IT, IoT, appliances) and tighten ERP-driven controls

digital_maturity_model.name: Manual / paper
signals: Sales booked on order pads, ledgers in registers
Stock counted physically, no SKU master
Schemes tracked on WhatsApp/memory
digital_maturity_model.next_step: Adopt Tally/GST billing software and a basic SKU master with IMEI capture.

digital_maturity_model.name: Digitised records
signals: Tally/Busy for billing and GST
Inventory tracked in software but not real-time
Receivables visible but chased manually
digital_maturity_model.next_step: Integrate e-invoice/e-way bill and start monthly GSTR-2B reconciliation and ageing reports.

digital_maturity_model.name: Integrated operations
signals: Distribution ERP (e.g. Bizom/FieldAssist/Marg) live
Salesman ordering app feeding secondary sales
Automated e-invoice, e-way bill and ageing dashboards
digital_maturity_model.next_step: Layer analytics: ABC-XYZ stock norms, beat productivity and scheme accrual at SKU level.

digital_maturity_model.name: Analytics-driven
signals: Demand-linked replenishment suggestions
Credit scoring and dynamic limits
Scheme/claim reconciliation automated against brand portals
digital_maturity_model.next_step: Introduce AI agents for price-erosion alerts, predictive collections and auto-replenishment.

digital_maturity_model.name: AI-native
signals: Autonomous replenishment & price-erosion radar
Predictive credit and collections workflows
Real-time blended-margin and cash-conversion control tower
digital_maturity_model.next_step: Extend AI orchestration across multi-territory, sub-distributor and B2B e-commerce operations.

playbooks.name: Automotive Workshops
playbooks.one_liner: An Indian automotive workshop is an MSME garage that services and repairs two-wheelers, cars or commercial vehicles — combining labour-driven mechanical/electrical/body work with retail of spares, lubricants and consumables, typically run as a single-bay multi-brand independent in Tier-2/3 towns or a multi-bay authorised/MUV outfit in metros.

operating_model.summary: A workshop monetises two intertwined streams — billable labour hours on a fixed pool of service bays/lifts, and margin on spares, lubricants, tyres and consumables fitted during the job. Profit is gated by bay throughput (jobs/day), mechanic utilisation, parts margin capture vs. leakage to roadside vendors, and repeat/AMC retention. Independents run lean cash businesses; authorised service centres (ASCs) run higher-volume, OEM-warranty-linked, lower-margin operations.
revenue_streams: Labour charges — periodic/scheduled service, general repair, mechanical/electrical, AC, denting-painting (body shop), wheel alignment & balancing
Spares & consumables margin — genuine/OES/aftermarket parts, filters, brake pads, clutch plates, batteries, tyres, lubricants/oil change
Value-added & recurring — annual maintenance contracts (AMC), extended warranty, insurance-claim cashless body repairs, RSA tie-ups, detailing/ceramic coating, PUC, fastag/accessories fitment
cost_structure: Spares & lubricant COGS (largest variable cost, 55-70% of parts revenue)
Mechanic & technician wages + incentives (skilled labour is the core fixed-ish cost)
Rent / lease of workshop premises (high in metros, bay area is the constraint)
Equipment & tooling capex + AMC (lifts, scan tools, alignment machine, paint booth, compressor)
Utilities (power for compressors/booth), consumables, scrap/oil disposal, GST on inward parts, software/DMS subscription
value_drivers: Bay & lift utilisation (jobs completed per bay per day) and right-first-time fix rate
Parts attach rate and capture of parts margin in-house vs. customer sourcing outside
Customer retention / repeat-visit rate via AMC, reminders and trust (vehicle data ownership)
Skilled technician availability and productivity (flat-rate hours billed vs. clocked)

value_chain: Vehicle reception & job-card creation (complaint capture + estimate)
Diagnosis (scan/road test) & customer approval of estimate

core_processes.description: Standardised digital job card capturing odometer, customer complaints, pre-service vehicle photos/condition, labour ops and parts; customer approves a transparent estimate before work starts and signs off on additionals. Prevents disputes and revenue leakage.

Fast-moving SKU stocking (filters, pads, oils, bulbs), reorder against min-max levels, vendor/distributor sourcing with 3-way match, and same-day local procurement for slow movers to avoid bay idle time.

Appointment + walk-in load balanced across bays/lifts; jobs assigned to technicians by skill (engine vs. electrical vs. body), tracking promised delivery time and work-in-progress to maximise throughput.
Final inspection checklist, road test, wash, and explained handover with itemised bill; triggers feedback capture and the next service reminder for retention.

department_structure.mandate: Run bays at maximum productive utilisation with right-first-time quality and on-time delivery.
Ensure right part available at right time at right margin; control stock investment and pilferage.
Convert leads, manage appointments, drive AMC/retention and customer experience.
Cash control, GST billing & filing, payroll, vendor payments, profitability tracking.

operational_bottlenecks.bottleneck: Bay/lift idle time waiting for parts
operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Vehicle stuck on lift for hours/days; promised delivery slips; bay throughput low despite footfall
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Lost billable labour hours, angry customers, lower jobs/day; capital locked in WIP vehicles
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Poor min-max stocking of fast movers + no real-time stock visibility; reliance on same-day market runs to nearby spare-parts market for common items

operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Customers bring own parts or buy cheaper from roadside vendor; mechanics do 'cash' side-jobs after hours; untracked consumables
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Workshop captures only labour, loses 55-70% margin parts revenue; under-the-table cash erodes books and GST
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Owner-dependent, paper job cards with no enforced parts attach; weak trust/transparency so customers price-shop; no incentive alignment with technicians

operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Cannot staff a new bay; quality varies by who works the car; trained mechanic leaves and takes regulars/loyal customers
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Capped capacity, inconsistent quality, comebacks/rework, knowledge walks out the door
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Thin ITI/skilled talent pool, no structured training/SOPs, low documented process so expertise is tribal not institutional

operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Owner doesn't know true per-bay profitability; mixes personal and business cash; GST under-reported; no DMS
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Can't price jobs scientifically, can't access formal credit, audit/penalty risk, leakage invisible
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Manual ledgers/paper bills, fear of GST, no garage-management software, founder running everything from memory

operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Arguments at delivery over 'extra' charges; customer alleges unnecessary parts replaced; bad word-of-mouth/Google reviews
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Loss of repeat business, reputational damage in a referral-driven local market, refunds/discounts
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: No documented pre-approval of estimate, no before/after evidence, verbal commitments by service advisor

operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Cashless claim surveyor delays, partial approvals, long settlement DSO from insurers
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Body-shop vehicles occupy space for weeks, working capital stuck, disputes on supplements
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Manual claim paperwork, dependence on surveyor visits, weak documentation of damage and supplements

ai_automation_opportunities.opportunity: Digital job-card + AI estimate engine: capture complaint and photos, auto-suggest labour ops and parts with transparent pre-approval sent to customer on WhatsApp, killing estimate disputes and leakage
Inventory min-max + auto-reorder for fast-moving spares/lubricants with stock-out alerts, eliminating bay-idle waiting-for-parts and reducing dead stock
AI service-reminder & AMC retention engine: predict next-service due from odometer/last-visit, auto-WhatsApp campaigns, win-back lapsed customers

consulting_frameworks.use: The service bay/lift (and skilled technician) is the constraint; schedule, stock parts and pre-diagnose to keep the bay never idle — every constraint hour lost is permanently lost revenue.

Manage parts inventory days + insurance-claim receivable DSO vs. supplier credit days to free trapped cash, especially in body-shop operations.
Map booking-to-delivery to locate margin leakage (parts sourced outside, cash side-jobs) and where to add value (AMC, detailing, accessories).
Segment customers by recency-frequency-monetary to drive service reminders, AMC upsell and win-back — repeat service is far cheaper than new acquisition.
Clarify who owns job-card approval, estimate sign-off, quality check and delivery so disputes and rework don't fall through owner-dependent gaps.

playbooks.name: Printing & Packaging

ai_automation_opportunities.opportunity: AI quote/estimation engine: parse RFQ (size, GSM, colours, finish, qty) and auto-compute paper consumption, ink, plate, die, wastage and machine-hour cost into a costed quote in minutes instead of 1-3 days, with margin guardrails per substrate.

Job-cost reconciliation agent: compare quoted vs actual paper/ink/wastage per job-card after run, flag jobs bleeding margin (high makeready spoilage, reruns) and feed corrected standards back into estimation.

Substrate/board procurement optimiser: forecast paper-board demand from order book, track kraft/duplex/art-paper price index, time buys before mill price revisions and consolidate to hit slab pricing.

GST e-invoice + e-way bill automation: auto-generate IRN and e-way bills from the dispatch/job system for every carton/label consignment, reconcile ITC on board/ink purchases, cut manual portal entry.
Prepress artwork QA bot: AI proof-check for bleed, dieline fit, barcode/QR readability, Pantone vs CMYK mismatch and spelling before plate-making, cutting costly reprints from artwork errors.
Collections/AR agent: auto-chase overdue FMCG/pharma packaging buyers (DSO often 60-90d), send reminders, and surface customers breaching MSME 45-day payment limits under Sec 43B(h).

consulting_frameworks.use: The press (offset/flexo/digital) is almost always the bottleneck; schedule, makeready-reduce (SMED) and elevate around the press rather than buying more cutting/lamination capacity. Subordinate prepress and finishing to keep the press fed.

Map margin and lead-time across design/prepress -> plate/die -> printing -> lamination/coating -> die-cutting/folding-gluing -> dispatch to find where wastage and idle time destroy contribution per machine-hour.
Price and prioritise jobs by ₹ contribution per press-hour, not per order — a small high-margin label job can beat a large low-margin carton run that hogs the press.

Manage the gap between paying board mills (often advance/30d) and collecting from buyers (60-90d); model the cash conversion cycle to size the working-capital line and avoid the classic packaging cash crunch on growth.

consulting_frameworks.framework: SMED (Single-Minute Exchange of Die) / makeready reduction
consulting_frameworks.use: Cut plate/blanket/ink changeover and registration setup time between jobs — the single biggest lever on press OEE and short-run profitability.
Rank capex and automation bets (new die-cutter, MIS/ERP, prepress workflow, anti-counterfeit printing) by Reach x Impact x Confidence / Effort for the PM/transformation roadmap.

department_structure.mandate: Win and price jobs, manage key FMCG/pharma/D2C accounts, convert RFQs into costed quotes with protected margins and realistic delivery dates.
Convert customer artwork into press-ready files, manage colour separation, dielines, proofs, plate and die-making with right-first-time accuracy.
Run printing (offset/flexo/digital), lamination/coating, die-cutting, folding-gluing on schedule at target OEE and within wastage norms.
Inline and final QC (colour, registration, dimensions, GSM, pharma artwork compliance), manage paper-board/ink inventory and reorder.
Keep presses and finishing lines running via preventive maintenance, minimise breakdown downtime, manage spares and utilities (compressed air, power).
Costing, billing/e-invoicing, GST/e-way, AR collections, payroll, statutory and pollution/factory licence compliance.

operational_bottlenecks.bottleneck: High press makeready and changeover time
operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Press sits idle 30-90 min between jobs; short runs are unprofitable; OEE stuck at 45-60%.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Lost machine-hours and high setup wastage erode contribution per press-hour, especially as runs shrink with SKU proliferation.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Manual plate/ink/registration setup, no SMED discipline, poor job sequencing (not grouping similar substrates/colours), and skill-dependent operators.

operational_bottlenecks.bottleneck: Paper-board / substrate cost volatility and stockouts
operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Quoted margin evaporates when board prices rise mid-order; jobs stall waiting for the right GSM/board to arrive.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Margin erosion and missed delivery dates; emergency spot buys at premium prices.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Board is 45-60% of job cost and mill prices swing with pulp/import cycles; no demand-linked procurement, weak forecasting, and reliance on a few mills/traders.

operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Jobs rejected for wrong shade, barcode misread, dieline misfit, spelling/regulatory text errors — full reruns.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Direct wastage of board/ink/plates plus penalty/credit notes and lost customer trust; pharma reprints carry compliance risk.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Manual proofing, last-minute customer artwork changes, no version control, and weak prepress QA gate before plate-making.

operational_bottlenecks.symptom: DSO of 60-90+ days from large FMCG/pharma buyers while board suppliers want advance or 30 days; recurring cash crunch.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Cannot fund board purchases for new orders, forced to borrow at high cost or turn away growth; classic 'profitable but broke' trap.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Buyer power of large brands, weak collections discipline, no credit policy, and inventory of slow-moving board/finished stock locking cash.

operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Output and quality dip when a key press/die operator is absent or leaves; tribal knowledge not documented.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Quality inconsistency, longer makeready, and inability to add shifts or scale.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Shortage of trained press/finishing operators in Tier-2/3 clusters, no SOPs/cross-training, and informal hiring.

operational_bottlenecks.bottleneck: Wastage and spoilage not measured per job
operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Year-end paper consumption far exceeds standard; nobody knows which jobs bled material.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Silent margin leak of several percentage points across the order book.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: No job-cost reconciliation (actual vs standard), makeready/run waste not captured on job-cards, and no MIS to flag outliers.

playbooks.one_liner: An Indian MSME printing & packaging converter that turns paper-board, film and ink into printed cartons, labels, corrugated boxes and flexible packaging for FMCG, pharma, food and D2C brands, competing on price, quality, lead time and brand-vendor approvals.

operating_model.summary: A capex-heavy, order-driven conversion business: customers (brands, traders, pharma/FMCG/food makers) place jobs that flow design -> prepress -> printing -> finishing -> dispatch on owned presses and finishing lines. Profit comes from keeping expensive presses busy at high OEE with low wastage, while board (45-60% of cost) and long receivables dominate the cash cycle. Mix spans mono-cartons, labels/stickers, corrugated boxes and flexible/laminated packaging, often serving Tier-2/3 industrial clusters.
revenue_streams: Job-work printing & conversion (cartons, labels, corrugated, flexible) priced per 1000 pieces or per kg
Prepress, design and plate/die-making charges
Value-added finishing (lamination, UV, foiling, embossing, spot coating)
Anti-counterfeit / smart packaging (QR, holograms, variable data) and sustainable packaging premiums
Reorder / repeat-print runs at higher margin once dies and plates exist
cost_structure: Paper-board / film / substrate (45-60% of job cost)
Inks, plates, dies, chemicals and consumables (8-15%)
Direct labour (press/finishing operators) and shift wages
Power and utilities (significant for presses, compressors, lamination)
Machinery depreciation, EMI/lease and maintenance/spares
Freight/logistics, factory rent, and statutory/compliance overheads
value_drivers: Press OEE and makeready efficiency (machine-hours sold)
Material wastage control and accurate job costing
Brand-vendor approvals (FSSAI/pharma/BRC audits) that lock recurring high-margin business
Working-capital discipline (DSO vs board payment terms)
Differentiation via finishing, sustainable and anti-counterfeit packaging

key_activities: Receive RFQ (size, board/GSM, colours, finish, qty)
Quote with margin and lead time
Generate proof and get customer sign-off
Capture repeat/reorder using stored plates and dies

milestones: Costing standards and BOM templates finalised

milestones: Internal vs external setup tasks separated
Quick-change tooling and pre-staging in place

AR ageing and DSO dashboard live

unit_economics: Mono-carton: board+ink ~₹0.8-2.5/carton depending on size/GSM; sell at ₹1.5-5/carton; contribution ₹0.4-1.5/carton after wastage
Labels/stickers: priced ₹0.10-1.50/label; high margin on short reorders once plates exist
Corrugated box: priced ₹8-40/box depending on ply/size; thin margins, freight-sensitive (low value-to-volume)
A single offset press job: aim for ₹1,500-4,000 contribution per press-hour after board/ink/wastage
profitability_analysis.working_capital_notes: Cash cycle is the make-or-break: board mills want advance or 30-day terms while FMCG/pharma buyers pay in 60-90+ days, so a growing converter is chronically cash-short. Inventory of multiple GSM/board grades and finished stock further locks cash. Target cash conversion cycle reduction via demand-linked procurement, faster collections, and board-price pass-through clauses. Note Sec 43B(h): if the converter itself buys from MSME suppliers, dues must clear within 45 days or the expense is disallowed.
levers: Raise press OEE and cut makeready (more saleable machine-hours from the same capex)
Reduce paper-board wastage from 8-10% toward 3-6% via job-cost reconciliation
Shift mix to value-added finishing and short high-margin reorders
Pass board-price volatility to customers via index-linked pricing clauses
Cut DSO and slow-moving inventory to free working capital and reduce interest cost

risk_model.risk: Customer concentration: one or two large FMCG/pharma brands dominate the order book and dictate price and 90-day terms.
risk_model.control: Diversify to 5+ anchor accounts across segments; contract with price-revision and payment-term clauses.

risk_model.risk: Board/substrate price volatility wiping out quoted margins mid-order.
risk_model.control: Index-linked / pass-through pricing clauses, rate contracts with mills, and demand-linked procurement.

risk_model.risk: Receivables stretch and customers breaching the MSME 45-day payment limit, plus the converter's own MSME-supplier dues going unpaid >45 days.
risk_model.control: Credit policy, AR ageing dashboard, MSME-status flagging, and Sec 43B(h)-aware vendor payment discipline.

risk_model.risk: Pollution-control / factory and environmental non-compliance (inks, solvents, effluent, emissions) leading to closure notices.
risk_model.control: Maintain factory licence and state pollution-control board consents; manage solvent/VOC and effluent per norms.

risk_model.risk: Food-contact / pharma packaging quality and material-safety failure causing recalls and customer loss.
risk_model.control: FSSAI-aligned food-grade material controls, BIS standards, traceability SOPs and pre-printing artwork QA gate.

risk_model.risk: Press breakdown / unplanned downtime missing delivery commitments on capex-heavy assets.
risk_model.control: Preventive-maintenance schedule, critical-spares stock, and OEE monitoring with predictive maintenance.

risk_model.risk: GST e-invoice / e-way bill non-compliance on consignments causing detention and penalties.
risk_model.control: Auto-generate IRN and e-way bills from the MIS; reconcile ITC on board/ink monthly.

core_processes.description: Convert an RFQ into a costed quote by computing board/ink/plate/die/machine-hour and wastage, applying margin and a realistic delivery date.
Sequence and run jobs across press and finishing to maximise OEE and minimise makeready, issuing materials and capturing actual consumption/wastage against the job-card.
Validate artwork (bleed, dieline, barcode, colour, regulatory text), proof and obtain sign-off before plate-making to prevent reprints.
Forecast and buy board/ink/film against the order book, 3-way match GRN/PO/invoice, and pay MSME suppliers within 45 days.
Dispatch with e-invoice/e-way bill, raise invoice, and chase receivables within credit terms to control DSO.

Demand-forecast + auto-reorder for retail product and consumables (colour tubes, wax, serums) to cut dead stock and stop stockouts of hero SKUs
Membership/package churn prediction and personalised re-engagement campaigns (lapsed client win-back, birthday/festival offers) driving repeat-visit frequency

Stylist-level productivity and tip/commission analytics with utilisation dashboards to optimise rostering against footfall curves

consulting_frameworks.use: Model revenue, product cost, stylist commission and rent against each productive station to find the break-even occupancy and the true margin of each service vs retail line
Identify the binding constraint (usually skilled stylist hours or peak-hour chair capacity, not demand) and schedule, price and upsell around relieving it

Manage prepaid-membership float (negative working capital advantage) against consumable inventory and Sec 43B(h) MSME supplier dues to keep cash positive
