Routing and slotting auto-optimised across the beat
Predictive maintenance/AMC offers pushed from usage data
Technician copilot surfaces model-specific fixes in real time
digital_maturity_model.next_step: Expand AI into proactive predictive-maintenance contracts and franchise/multi-city replication on the same platform.

stages.focus: Build first-time-fix reliability, local trust and a steady inbound flow
plays: Get listed and rated on Google Business Profile and Justdial; chase reviews after every job
Secure 1-2 OEM authorisations or aggregator (Urban Company) onboarding for guaranteed lead flow
Start a basic AMC for high-repeat appliances (RO, AC) to create recurring revenue
Standardise transparent visit-charge + estimate-before-repair to win trust

stages.focus: Operational scale - SLA, utilisation and parts availability without quality drop
plays: Deploy a field-service system with technician app and SLA timers
Build van-stock standards and a parts reorder discipline to lift first-time-fix
Introduce technician incentives tied to FTF, CSAT and collection (not just job count)
Grow B2B/AMC book with offices, hospitals, builders for predictable volume

stages.focus: Replicable model, brand and platform leverage
plays: Codify SOPs and a training academy to onboard technicians fast at consistent quality
Standardise the tech platform so a new city launches on day one with dashboards
Negotiate OEM master service contracts and bulk spare-parts pricing
Use AI for triage, forecasting and routing to keep unit economics intact while scaling

kpi_structure.definition: Percent of jobs fully resolved on the first visit without a repeat trip
Percent of jobs attended and closed within the promised turnaround time
Average completed jobs per field technician per working day
Percent of jobs requiring a second visit for the same complaint
Percent of expiring AMC contracts renewed
Percent of billed value collected and reconciled (no technician cash leakage)

playbooks.one_liner: An Indian MSME repair and after-sales service business that diagnoses and fixes appliances, electronics and equipment - via field visits, bench/workshop, warranty work, and recurring AMC contracts - monetising labour, spare parts and maintenance subscriptions.

operating_model.summary: A people-and-parts business that converts a customer breakdown into a fast, reliable fix. Revenue comes from per-visit labour charges, spare-part margins, OEM warranty/contract work, and recurring AMCs. The economics live or die on technician utilisation, first-time-fix rate, and parts availability; cash flow is squeezed by spare-part purchases upfront versus delayed customer/OEM collection.
revenue_streams: Per-visit diagnostic/labour charges (₹250-700 visit charge + repair labour)
Spare-parts sale margin (typically 20-40% over cost)
Annual Maintenance Contracts (AMC) - comprehensive and non-comprehensive
OEM authorised warranty service reimbursement (per-call rate)
B2B/institutional service contracts (offices, hospitals, builders)
Out-of-warranty / extended-warranty plans
cost_structure: Technician salaries + incentives (largest cost, 30-45% of revenue)
Spare parts and consumables (gas, oils, PCBs, motors)
Travel/fuel and vehicle/two-wheeler running cost
Aggregator commission (Urban Company etc. 15-30%) or OEM-partner take-rate
Workshop/store rent, tools and diagnostic equipment
Software, call-centre and overheads
value_drivers: First-time-fix rate (kills costly repeat visits)
Technician skill, retention and utilisation
Spare-parts availability and van-stock discipline
Recurring AMC base and OEM authorisation for predictable lead flow
Local reputation / online ratings driving organic demand

operational_bottlenecks.bottleneck: Low first-time-fix due to missing spare part
operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Technician visits, diagnoses, but returns later with the part - two trips for one job
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Doubles cost per job, delays SLA, frustrates customers and erodes margin
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: No demand-based van-stock or parts forecasting; spares ordered reactively after diagnosis

operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Backlog of jobs, missed SLAs, over-reliance on a few senior technicians
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Capped capacity, lost revenue, quality variance, poached staff start competing shops
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Shortage of trained appliance/electronics technicians in India, weak training pipeline and incentive structure

operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Cash-collected jobs not deposited, spares 'used' but unaccounted, side-jobs done off-book
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Direct margin loss and untraceable inventory shrinkage
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Manual job cards, cash collection by technicians, no reconciliation between parts issued and billed

operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Technicians crisscross the city, idle gaps between jobs, can't fit same-day requests
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Low jobs-per-tech-per-day, high fuel cost, poor SLA on urgent calls
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Manual phone-based assignment with no geo-clustering or route optimisation

operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Warranty work done, parts consumed, but OEM payment arrives 60-90 days later or gets rejected on documentation
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Working-capital crunch; spares paid for upfront, money stuck with OEM
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Manual claim paperwork, mismatched serial/job documentation, no claim-tracking discipline

operational_bottlenecks.bottleneck: One-time jobs not converted to recurring revenue
operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Strong repair volume but flat, lumpy income with no predictable base
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Idle-capacity in lean seasons, high re-acquisition cost per customer
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: No service-history capture or AMC sales motion; customer contact lost after the job closes

key_activities: Identify appliance, brand, symptom, warranty status, location
Set SLA expectation and slot the visit
Assign and dispatch the right technician with likely parts
Digital job-card closure with parts and signature
Safety and e-waste disposal of replaced parts
Offer AMC / extended warranty / seasonal check

unit_economics: Avg repair ticket ₹600-1,800 (visit charge ₹250-700 + labour + parts); AMC ₹1,200-4,500/appliance/year
Per job: revenue ₹1,200 - parts ₹350 - technician cost ₹300 - travel ₹80 = contribution ~₹470 (≈39%)
Technician fully loaded ₹22,000-40,000/month; needs ~5-6 billable jobs/day to be profitable
Aggregator route: 15-30% commission eats most of the labour margin, so own-lead/AMC mix is key
profitability_analysis.working_capital_notes: Main strain is spare-parts inventory bought upfront against OEM warranty reimbursement that lands 60-90 days later, plus any B2B/institutional credit (DSO 45-75 days). Cash-collection jobs help liquidity but invite leakage. Watch Sec 43B(h) - pay MSME spare-part suppliers within 45 days or lose the deduction.
levers: Lift first-time-fix to cut the cost of repeat visits
Shift mix toward recurring AMC and own-generated leads (away from high-commission aggregators)
Improve parts margin via better OEM/aftermarket sourcing and van-stock discipline
Raise technician utilisation (jobs/day) through routing and slotting
Tighten OEM warranty-claim documentation to speed reimbursement

pm_workflows.initiative: Roll out field-service management software (booking to invoice)
milestones: Map current booking-to-collection flow and pain points
Configure job cards, SLA timers, technician app and parts module
Migrate customer/AMC history and train staff
Go-live with parallel run, then retire paper job cards
Baseline FTF and top repeat-visit fault codes
Define van-stock kit per appliance category
Publish model-specific repair SOPs to technician app
Track FTF weekly and tie technician incentive to it
Mine service history for AMC-eligible customers
Hit target AMC base and renewal rate

risk_model.risk: Spare-parts under-stocking causing low first-time-fix and SLA breaches
risk_model.control: Demand-forecast van-stock kits per appliance/region and enforce reorder levels

risk_model.risk: Cash and spare-parts pilferage by field technicians
risk_model.control: Digital job cards, parts-issued-vs-billed reconciliation, UPI-first collection and surprise audits

risk_model.risk: GST non-compliance on labour+parts billing (wrong rate/HSN-SAC, missing e-invoice)
risk_model.control: System-generated GST invoices with correct SAC/HSN split and e-invoice where turnover threshold applies

risk_model.risk: Labour-law and informal-staffing exposure (no EPF/ESI, unsafe field work)
risk_model.control: Register under Shops Act, enrol eligible staff in EPF/ESI, document safety/insurance for field technicians

risk_model.risk: Delayed/rejected OEM warranty-claim reimbursement straining working capital
risk_model.control: Standardise serial/job documentation, track claims to closure, age and escalate overdue claims

risk_model.risk: Improper e-waste / refrigerant (gas) disposal and consumer-grievance liability
risk_model.control: Use authorised e-waste recyclers, follow refrigerant-handling norms, give written estimates/warranty on repairs to limit Consumer Protection disputes

risk_model.risk: Late payment to MSME spare-part suppliers disallowing tax deduction
risk_model.control: Pay registered MSME suppliers within 45 days per Sec 43B(h); track supplier Udyam status

value_chain: Demand generation (OEM authorisation, aggregators, local SEO, referrals)

core_processes.description: Capture the complaint with appliance/brand/symptom/warranty/location, set SLA, and assign the right technician with the likely parts pre-picked
Field/bench diagnosis, transparent estimate-before-repair, customer approval, repair per SOP and functional QC to maximise first-time-fix
GST-compliant job-card-to-invoice, UPI/cash collection, parts-issued-vs-billed reconciliation, and OEM warranty-claim filing
Forecast fast-movers, maintain van-stock and store reorder levels, manage warranty-part returns and control shrinkage
Log service history, push AMC/extended-warranty offers, automate renewal reminders and reactivate dormant customers

playbooks.name: Event Businesses

ai_automation_opportunities.opportunity: AI quote/BOQ builder: from a client brief (guest count, venue, theme, date) auto-generate an itemised decor + production BOQ with vendor rates, GST, margin and a branded proposal PDF in minutes instead of 2-3 days.

Vendor/freelancer roster + availability matcher: AI maps required crew (decorators, light/sound, catering, mandap, photographers) against the event calendar, flags double-bookings and auto-issues purchase orders.
Cash-flow & advance-tracking copilot: predicts the 40-30-30 milestone collection schedule per event, chases overdue advances, and forecasts the wedding-season liquidity crunch.
GST + RCM autopilot: classifies each line (decor 18%, catering, venue) under correct SAC, computes reverse charge on unregistered labour/transport, and prepares GSTR-1/3B.
Event production SOP + checklist agent: auto-generates load-in/load-out, fire-safety, and rundown checklists per event type and assigns RACI to on-ground crew via mobile.
Lead intake + WhatsApp concierge: captures enquiries from Instagram/JustDial/WedMeGood, qualifies budget and date, and books a site-visit, reducing lead leakage.
Rental inventory tracker: barcode/QR check-in-check-out of props, furniture, lights and linen with damage/shortage reconciliation against each event.
Post-event profitability autopsy: reconciles quoted vs actual cost per event, surfaces margin leakage by category and crew overtime overruns.

consulting_frameworks.use: Decompose each event into brief to design to procurement to fabrication to load-in to execution to strike to settlement, exposing where margin leaks (overtime, rework, damaged rentals).
Model contribution per event (ticket size minus direct decor/production/crew/transport cost) and per square-foot decor cost to price reliably across wedding, corporate and exhibition jobs.
In peak wedding season the binding constraint is skilled crew + signature props, not demand; schedule and price around the bottleneck rather than chasing every enquiry.
Engineer the advance-milestone-balance schedule (40-30-30) so client advances fund vendor payments, minimising the founder's own bridge capital during the season.
Assign clear on-ground accountability (producer vs designer vs vendor manager vs client servicing) for each event so nothing falls between roles on show day.
Frame the client's real job (a stress-free, photogenic, on-budget celebration) to upsell coordination, hospitality and content packages beyond raw decor.
Rank service-line and capability investments (in-house fabrication, owned LED wall, second event team) by reach, impact, confidence and effort.

department_structure.mandate: Win and retain clients: enquiry handling, site visits, proposals, negotiation, and relationship management with families, corporates and planners.
Translate briefs into themes, mood boards, 2D/3D decor renders, floor plans and the production BOQ.
Procure, fabricate, schedule crew, manage logistics, run load-in/show/strike and on-ground execution.
Build and price the vendor network (catering, light/sound, mandap, florals, transport, manpower), raise POs and manage rentals/inventory.
Quotation costing, advance collection, vendor payouts, GST/RCM/TDS, payroll for crew, and per-event P&L.

digital_maturity_model.name: Manual / Paper & WhatsApp
signals: Quotes built in Excel or by hand
Client/vendor coordination entirely on WhatsApp and calls
No central calendar; bookings tracked in a diary
Cash advances, little documentation
digital_maturity_model.next_step: Adopt a single shared event calendar and a standard quotation template; record every enquiry in one sheet.

digital_maturity_model.name: Digitised Records
signals: Standardised quotation/BOQ templates
Shared Google Sheet/Drive for bookings and vendor rates
Tally/Zoho Books for accounting and GST
Photos of inventory catalogued
digital_maturity_model.next_step: Move enquiries into a CRM pipeline and tag every cost to an event ID to start measuring per-event margin.

digital_maturity_model.name: Integrated Systems
signals: CRM tracks lead to booking to delivery
Event/project management tool with crew scheduling
QR/barcode rental inventory check-in/out
Per-event P&L reconciled quoted vs actual
digital_maturity_model.next_step: Connect CRM, finance and inventory so a confirmed booking auto-creates POs, payment milestones and crew assignments.

digital_maturity_model.name: Data-Driven & Connected
signals: Dashboards on pipeline, occupancy, margin and overtime
Automated milestone invoicing and advance reminders
Vendor performance and damage rates tracked
Seasonal capacity and cash-flow forecasting
digital_maturity_model.next_step: Introduce AI for auto-BOQ generation, demand forecasting and crew/vendor matching on top of the connected data.

digital_maturity_model.name: AI-Native
signals: AI generates proposals/BOQs from a brief
Predictive crew and prop allocation across the calendar
Automated GST/RCM and profitability autopsy per event
AI concierge handles and qualifies inbound leads 24x7
digital_maturity_model.next_step: Continuously retrain pricing and forecasting models on closed-event data; expand AI to design ideation and content.

stages.focus: Build a reliable vendor network, a signature design style and a referral engine in one home city.
plays: Lock 8-12 reliable vendors with negotiated rates
Build an Instagram/portfolio of 15-20 shot weddings
Get listed on WedMeGood/JustDial and activate planner referrals
Standardise quotation template and advance-milestone terms

stages.focus: Add a second execution team, own high-rotation assets, and diversify into corporate/MICE for off-season cash flow.
plays: Bring signature fabrication and a few high-utilisation props (LED wall, structures) in-house
Add a dedicated corporate/exhibition sales line for weekday/off-season revenue
Implement CRM + per-event P&L; introduce a producer-led team-of-two model
Formalise crew payroll (EPF/ESI) and vendor contracts

stages.focus: Multi-city footprint, destination weddings and productised offerings with brand-led pricing.
plays: Open a second-city ops cell or asset-light partner network
Build a destination-wedding desk (logistics, travel, vendor sourcing across cities)
Productise packages (tiered wedding/decor bundles) for predictable margins
Pursue larger corporate/government event tenders and annual retainers

kpi_structure.definition: Confirmed bookings divided by qualified enquiries.
(Event revenue minus direct production, decor, crew, transport cost) divided by revenue.
Share of contract value received before show day.
Actual direct cost over quoted cost per event.
Average days to collect the post-event balance.
Damaged or lost rental items as a share of items deployed.

playbooks.one_liner: An Indian event business designs, produces and executes weddings, corporate functions and exhibitions, monetising creative design plus on-ground production, crew and rental logistics on a project-by-project basis.

operating_model.summary: A project-based services business: each event is a fixed-deadline, immovable-date project won by design and reputation, costed as a BOQ, executed through a flexible mix of in-house crew and external vendors, and settled on advance-milestone-balance terms. Revenue is highly seasonal (wedding/festive peaks) and capacity is bound by skilled crew and signature assets.
revenue_streams: Wedding decor, planning and execution (largest, seasonal)
Corporate events, conferences and MICE (weekday, off-season cash flow)
Exhibition/stall fabrication and brand activations
Prop, furniture, light and structure rentals
Add-on services: content/photography, hospitality, entertainment management commission
cost_structure: Direct production: fabrication material, florals, printing, structures (35-50% of event cost)
Crew and on-ground manpower including overtime (15-25%)
Vendor pass-throughs: catering, light/sound, transport (variable)
Owned-asset depreciation, warehousing and damage/replacement
Overheads: studio rent, design/creative salaries, sales and marketing
value_drivers: Distinctive design portfolio and brand reputation/referrals
Reliable vendor network and execution discipline on immovable dates
Disciplined BOQ costing and advance collection to protect margin and cash
Asset utilisation of owned high-rotation props

operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Multiple weddings on the same auspicious dates; scrambling for decorators, light/sound and transport at premium rates.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Margin erosion from last-minute premium hiring, quality dips, and turned-away revenue.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Highly concentrated demand on a handful of muhurat dates against a thin pool of skilled freelance crew and shared vendors.

operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Event executes over budget; client-approved changes and breakages not billed.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Gross margin slips 10-20 points below quote; some events run at a loss.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: BOQ built on rough estimates, no per-event cost reconciliation, scope creep accepted verbally without change orders.

operational_bottlenecks.bottleneck: Delayed balance collection and advance funding gap
operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Vendors demand payment before/at the event while the client balance arrives weeks later.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Founder funds the gap from personal capital; cash crunch through the season.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Weak contract enforcement of milestone terms, family clients negotiate post-event, no automated advance chasing.

operational_bottlenecks.symptom: A key caterer or light vendor cancels or under-delivers on show day.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Reputation damage, penalties, client refunds despite the fault being a vendor's.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Over-reliance on a few unwritten vendor relationships with no SLAs or backups.

operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Props, linen and lights return short or damaged after each event with no clear accountability.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Silent capital drain and unplanned replacement cost.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: No check-in/check-out tracking; deployment to multiple sites without per-event reconciliation.

operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Enquiries from Instagram, JustDial and referrals go uncaptured or unanswered for days.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Low conversion and wasted marketing spend in a referral-driven market.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: No CRM or single intake channel; founder personally handles every lead and drops some during execution-heavy weeks.

milestones: Design + BOQ approved and advance received
Vendor POs raised and crew rostered
Strike, inventory reconciliation and final billing
Forecast confirmed bookings vs crew/asset capacity
Lock vendor rates and crew retainers before peak
Model milestone cash inflow vs vendor payout timeline
Set per-date booking caps to avoid over-commitment
Review pipeline conversion and reactivate referral partners

key_activities: Capture and qualify enquiry (date, budget, guest count)
Contract signing with milestone terms and advance
Real-time issue resolution and client liaison

unit_economics: A mid-tier urban wedding decor+execution job: ticket ₹8-25 lakh, direct cost ₹5-16 lakh, contribution ₹3-9 lakh at ~35% before overheads
Corporate/MICE event: ticket ₹2-10 lakh, gross margin 30-45% (lower material, higher service)
Customer acquisition is largely referral/portfolio-driven; effective CAC ₹15-40k per won wedding via listings + content
Owned prop rental can return 30-50% gross once an asset crosses ~8-12 deployments
profitability_analysis.working_capital_notes: Cash flow is swingy and seasonal. Aim for 40% booking advance + 30% pre-event + 30% on/after event so client cash funds vendor payouts. DSO on the final balance should stay under 30 days; the danger zone is funding vendor advances out of pocket during peak muhurat weeks. Maintain a season buffer of 1.5-2 months of fixed overhead.
levers: Tighten BOQ accuracy and enforce paid change-orders to kill the 10-20 point quote-to-actual gap
Raise advance percentage and automate balance collection to compress DSO
In-source high-utilisation assets and negotiate annual vendor rate-cards to cut peak premiums
Diversify into off-season corporate/MICE to spread fixed overhead across the year

risk_model.risk: Immovable-date execution failure (vendor no-show, weather, logistics) damaging reputation
risk_model.control: Backup vendors, contracted SLAs, contingency budget, event insurance, and a pre-event technical rehearsal.

risk_model.risk: Client default on post-event balance / scope-creep disputes
risk_model.control: Written contract with milestone advances, signed change-orders, and clear payment + dispute clauses.

risk_model.risk: Food-safety incident at catered events
risk_model.control: Engage only FSSAI-licensed caterers, retain food handling records, and pass liability through vendor contracts.

risk_model.risk: Labour non-compliance on contract crew (no EPF/ESI, wage/safety issues)
risk_model.control: Register and remit EPF/ESI for eligible workers, use licensed manpower contractors, maintain attendance and wage records.

risk_model.risk: GST/RCM and TDS mis-handling on vendor and labour payments
risk_model.control: Correct SAC classification, reverse-charge on unregistered/transport vendors, timely GSTR filing and TDS deduction.

risk_model.risk: MSME Sec 43B(h) disallowance from delayed payments to micro/small vendors
risk_model.control: Pay registered micro/small vendors within 45 days; track vendor Udyam status and due dates.

risk_model.risk: Seasonal cash-flow crunch and over-commitment on peak dates
risk_model.control: Per-date booking caps, advance-funded vendor payments, and a pre-season liquidity buffer.

core_processes.description: Convert a creative brief into an itemised, margin-loaded bill of quantities covering decor, production, crew, vendors and contingency, used as the single source of truth for the event P&L.
Source, contract and schedule the right mix of in-house crew and external vendors against the event calendar, with SLAs, POs and backups to guarantee delivery on an immovable date.
Run load-in, technical rehearsal, show-day rundown and strike using checklists and RACI so execution is repeatable and safe.
Enforce advance-pre-event-balance milestones, automate reminders, and reconcile vendor payouts so client cash funds delivery.
Check owned props/rentals in and out per event, account for damage/shortage, and feed replacement and utilisation data back to costing.

playbooks.name: Travel Agencies
playbooks.one_liner: An Indian MSME travel agency aggregates and resells travel inventory — air/rail tickets, hotels, holiday packages, visas, forex and ground transport — earning commissions, markups and service fees while managing supplier credit, seasonal demand and thin per-booking economics.

operating_model.summary: A travel agency is a working-capital-intensive intermediary: it books inventory from airlines/GDS, hotels, DMCs (destination management companies) and bus/rail aggregators, marks it up or earns commission, and sells to leisure (FIT/group) and corporate (TMC) clients. Economics are razor-thin per air ticket (margins often near-zero after airline commission cuts) but rich on packaged holidays, hotels, visa and forex. Cash flow is dominated by advance collection from customers vs. credit/deposit cycles with suppliers (IATA BSP, hotel/DMC payments). The MSME survives on relationships, trust, repeat/referral business and the ability to assemble a bespoke itinerary faster and cheaper than OTAs.
revenue_streams: Air ticketing commission + service/convenience fee (₹150-₹500 domestic, ₹500-₹2,000 international per pax)
Holiday package markup (10-25% gross on domestic, 8-18% on international FIT/group)
Hotel booking commission/markup (10-20% on net rates from DMCs/B2B aggregators)
Visa, passport, travel insurance and forex commission (forex spread 1.5-3%)
MICE / corporate travel management fees and group-tour organising (school, religious, corporate offsites)
Ground services — cab/coach, guide, rail tatkal assistance, add-on excursions
cost_structure: Inventory / supplier cost (airfare, hotel net rates, DMC land cost) — 75-90% of revenue
BSP/IATA bank guarantee or deposit blocked + GDS/CRS segment fees
Staff salaries (ticketing/operations/sales counsellors) — 8-15% of revenue
Marketing & lead gen (Google/Meta ads, OTA listings, influencer/travel-fair spend)
Rent for high-street/footfall office, software (CRM/mid-office/accounting), payment-gateway MDR 1.5-2%
value_drivers: Supplier relationships & negotiated net rates / overrides that beat OTA public fares
Trust, advisory expertise and 24x7 on-trip support that justify a fee over self-service apps
Repeat & referral rate from delighted travellers (LTV multiplier on near-zero incremental CAC)
Niche specialisation (religious circuits, destination weddings, Schengen visas, adventure, NRI/inbound) commanding higher margin

value_chain: Lead generation & enquiry capture (walk-in, referral, Google/Meta, WhatsApp, OTA)
Itinerary design & quotation (sourcing net rates from DMCs/airlines/hotels)
Negotiation, customisation & conversion to confirmed booking + advance collection
Supplier confirmation & vouchering (PNR issuance, hotel/DMC confirmation, visa filing)
Pre-departure documentation, payment reconciliation & final balance collection
Post-trip feedback, settlement of supplier dues, refund/credit-note processing, repeat/referral nurture

core_processes.description: Counsellor captures enquiry, builds itinerary by pulling net rates from DMC/B2B portals/airline, applies markup rules, and sends a branded quote — speed and accuracy here drive conversion.

On advance receipt, issue PNR/tickets via GDS or airline portal, raise hotel/land bookings with DMC, file visa, collect docs — each step has a hard cut-off and non-refundable deadline that must be tracked.
Customer advance + balance reconciled against supplier payables (BSP fortnightly cycle, hotel/DMC credit terms), GST invoicing under TCS/Tour-operator rules, refund and credit-note handling.
24x7 desk handles flight delays, hotel no-shows, medical/visa emergencies; SLA on response protects reputation and repeat business.

department_structure.mandate: Capture leads, design itineraries, quote, negotiate and convert; own conversion rate and average ticket size.
Issue tickets/PNRs, confirm hotels/land with DMCs, file visas, prepare vouchers and travel docs, manage cut-offs.
Advance/balance collection, supplier (BSP/DMC) settlement, GST/TCS compliance, refunds, reconciliation, MIS.
Pre-departure handholding, on-trip emergency support, feedback capture, referral/repeat nurture.
Lead generation, brand/social, OTA/marketplace listings, and negotiating net rates/overrides with airlines, hotels and DMCs.

operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Customer asks for a package; counsellor takes hours/days collating net rates from multiple DMC portals, emails and PDFs — customer books with a faster competitor or OTA meanwhile.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Conversion drops to 10-20%; hot leads go cold; counsellor time is consumed in quoting rather than closing.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Fragmented inventory across many supplier portals with no unified rate aggregation; markup rules and itineraries rebuilt from scratch each time instead of templated.

operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Customer pays in instalments while airline BSP and DMCs demand deposits/advance/fortnightly settlement; agency funds the gap from its own pocket or blocked bank guarantee.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Cash crunch in peak season, inability to take more bookings, reliance on costly overdraft; one defaulting customer can wipe out a month's margin.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Thin margins + supplier credit terms tighter than customer payment behaviour; no disciplined advance-collection policy or credit insurance.

operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Hundreds of bookings, partial payments, airline credit-shells/refunds, DMC credit notes — accounts can't tell true booking-level profit or what supplier owes them.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Leakage of refunds never claimed, GST/TCS errors, disputes with suppliers, owner flying blind on margins.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Booking data in GDS/portals/WhatsApp/Excel never tied to a single mid-office ledger; refunds (esp. post-COVID credit shells) tracked manually.

operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Summer (May-Jun), Diwali, year-end and Char Dham/Hajj/festival windows overwhelm capacity; lean months idle staff and fixed costs.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Overtime, service quality dips and errors in peak; cash-flow drought and underutilisation off-peak.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Leisure demand is calendar-driven; no counter-seasonal product mix (corporate/MICE, inbound, off-season destinations) to flatten the curve.

operational_bottlenecks.bottleneck: Disintermediation by OTAs and direct airline/hotel booking
operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Customers compare on MakeMyTrip/Booking.com/airline apps and use the agency only for advice, then book elsewhere; airlines keep cutting commissions to near zero.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Margin compression on commodity air/hotel; agency reduced to unpaid advisor unless it adds bespoke value.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Commoditised, price-transparent inventory; agency value (curation, support, complex itineraries) not packaged or charged for explicitly.

ai_automation_opportunities.opportunity: AI itinerary & instant-quote builder that pulls net rates from supplier portals, applies markup rules and generates a branded, customisable quote/PDF in minutes — cutting Q2Q from hours to minutes and lifting conversion.
Automated mid-office reconciliation: match customer advances/balances to BSP and DMC settlements, flag unclaimed refunds/credit-shells, and surface true booking-level margin.
WhatsApp/chat lead-capture and AI follow-up bot that qualifies enquiries 24x7, sends quotes, nurtures undecided leads and reduces leakage of cold leads.
GST + TCS on tour-package compliance automation: correct invoicing under tour-operator margin scheme, 5%/18% rate logic, TCS on overseas tour packages, and timely return filing.
24x7 AI customer-support copilot for pre-departure FAQs, document checklists, flight-status and on-trip escalation triage, freeing staff for high-value advisory.
Demand-forecasting and dynamic-pricing assistant that predicts seasonal peaks by destination and recommends markup/inventory-block decisions to smooth the demand curve.

consulting_frameworks.use: Map advance-collection vs supplier-settlement timing to size the funding gap; tighten advance policy and negotiate DMC credit so the customer funds the trip, not the agency.
Compute true margin per air ticket vs package vs hotel vs forex after MDR, GDS fees and refunds — to shift mix toward high-margin packages and away from commoditised air.
Identify why travellers still use an agent vs OTA (complex multi-country itineraries, group/religious tours, visa hassle, on-trip safety) and design packaged, chargeable services around those jobs.
Segment customers by recency/frequency/monetary value to prioritise NRI, corporate and repeat-leisure clients whose referral-driven LTV dwarfs CAC.
In peak season the binding constraint is counsellor quoting/operations capacity — exploit via templated itineraries and AI quoting before adding headcount.
Decompose enquiry-to-settlement to find where margin leaks (unclaimed refunds, slow quotes, manual recon) and where defensible value is added (curation, support).

risk_model.risk: Supplier/DMC or airline default — agency has collected from customer but supplier fails to deliver or goes insolvent (e.g. airline grounding), leaving agency liable to refund.
risk_model.control: Deal with IATA/bonded suppliers, stagger supplier payments, take credit/trip insurance, and cap exposure per supplier; keep customer advances in a controlled account.

risk_model.risk: GST and TCS misapplication on tour packages (wrong rate, tour-operator margin scheme, TCS on overseas tour remittance) leading to notices, interest and penalties.
risk_model.control: Use compliant mid-office billing, correct HSN/SAC and TCS logic, reconcile ITC, and file returns on time; periodic GST health-check.

risk_model.risk: Customer payment default / chargeback after tickets issued or non-refundable bookings made, eroding thin margins.
risk_model.control: Strict advance-collection policy, non-refundable clauses in booking terms, milestone payments, and verified payment-gateway capture before issuance.

risk_model.risk: Reputation/legal liability from on-trip incidents — medical emergency, accident, visa rejection, stranded group — and consumer-court claims.
risk_model.control: Clear written terms & disclaimers, mandatory travel insurance, vetted ground partners, 24x7 support SOP, and documented duty of care.

risk_model.risk: Non-registration / lapsed statutory registrations (Udyam, GST, shops establishment, professional tax) attracting penalties and disqualifying from B2B/corporate tenders.
risk_model.control: Maintain Udyam, GST, Shops & Establishment and professional-tax registrations with a compliance calendar.

risk_model.risk: Cash-flow / payroll statutory lapse (EPF/ESI, TDS on salary) during lean off-season cash crunch.
risk_model.control: Maintain a peak-season cash buffer, ring-fence statutory dues, and automate EPF/ESI/TDS remittance.

kpi_structure.definition: Confirmed bookings ÷ total qualified enquiries in a period.
kpi_structure.critical: <15% — quoting too slow or pricing uncompetitive

kpi_structure.definition: (Sell price − supplier cost − transaction fees) ÷ sell price, by product type.
kpi_structure.critical: <6% blended — mix too air-heavy, margin leaking

kpi_structure.definition: Total sales value ÷ number of bookings.
kpi_structure.critical: Declining toward low-margin point-to-point air only

kpi_structure.definition: Customer advances received vs supplier payments due before departure.
kpi_structure.healthy: >90% of trip cost collected before supplier settlement
kpi_structure.critical: <70% — agency financing customers, cash crunch risk

kpi_structure.definition: Share of bookings from returning customers or their referrals.
Value and age of supplier/airline refunds and credits not yet recovered.

profitability_analysis.typical_gross_margin: 8-18% blended (packages 12-22%, hotels 10-18%, air near 2-5% after fee)
profitability_analysis.typical_net_margin: 2-6% of turnover (turnover is gross sales; on commission/margin basis net can be 15-30%)
unit_economics: Domestic holiday package: sell ₹50,000 → land/air cost ~₹42,000 → gross margin ₹8,000 (16%); after MDR + ops cost net ~₹3,000-₹4,000 per booking
International FIT: sell ₹1,50,000 → DMC/air cost ~₹1,28,000 → gross margin ~₹22,000 (14-15%); a single conversion can equal 8-10 domestic air tickets in profit
Air-only ticket: ₹6,000 fare → airline commission ~₹0 + service fee ₹300 − GDS/MDR ~₹120 → net ~₹150-₹200 (a loss-leader to capture the package sale)
profitability_analysis.working_capital_notes: The core constraint. Customers often pay in instalments while airlines (BSP fortnightly settlement against a blocked bank guarantee) and DMCs demand advances/deposits — so the agency can be net-funding trips. DSO is effectively negative when advance-collection discipline is strong (customer prepays), but turns sharply negative-cash if balances slip past supplier cut-offs. Peak season (May-Jun, Diwali, Dec) spikes the funding need; an overdraft or supplier-credit line bridges it. Unclaimed refunds/credit shells are trapped working capital.
levers: Shift product mix toward high-margin packages, hotels, visa and forex; treat air as a loss-leader funnel into packages
Charge an explicit, unbundled service/advisory fee so curation value is monetised even on commodity air/hotel
Tighten advance-collection (90%+ before supplier settlement) and enforce non-refundable milestones to flip working capital positive
Negotiate supplier overrides/net-rate deals and recover all refunds/credit shells to plug leakage
Build counter-seasonal revenue (corporate/MICE, inbound, off-season destinations) to use idle capacity and fixed cost

pm_workflows.cadence: Quarterly sprint, 6-8 weeks before each peak
milestones: Lock supplier net rates & inventory blocks for top destinations
Staff roster, temp hiring & 24x7 desk rota set
Cash/overdraft line confirmed for advance-settlement gap
All bookings tied to a single ledger with booking-level P&L
Supplier statements matched and disputes raised

key_activities: Negotiate net rates/overrides with airlines, hotels, DMCs
Build destination packages, fix-departure group tours and pricing rules
Define inclusions, T&Cs, cancellation and refund policy
Run seasonal campaigns and travel-fair/referral drives
Capture and qualify enquiries via WhatsApp/calls/walk-ins
Collect advance, issue tickets/PNR, confirm hotels/land
File visas, arrange insurance and documentation
Reconcile payments, settle suppliers, claim refunds
Nurture repeat/referral and upsell next trip

stages.focus: Survive thin margins, build supplier relationships and a repeat-customer base in a niche
plays: Pick a defensible niche (religious circuits, NRI, destination weddings, a specific outbound region)
Get Udyam + GST + IATA/consolidator tie-ups; secure a basic overdraft line
Enforce advance-collection discipline to stay cash-positive
Drive referrals from every delighted traveller

stages.focus: Systematise operations, add corporate/MICE for counter-seasonality, and digitise quoting & mid-office

Add a corporate travel (TMC) desk to flatten seasonality
Build a digital lead engine (Google/Meta/WhatsApp) and online quote/payment

stages.focus: Multi-branch / franchise, brand, inbound and own-DMC capability for margin capture

Build inbound and own ground-handling/DMC to capture land margin
Launch own-brand fix-departure series and white-label B2B sub-agent network

playbooks.name: Local Service MSMEs
playbooks.one_liner: A neighbourhood, owner-operated service business (salon, tailor, laundry/dry-clean, mobile/appliance repair, RO/AC service, electrician-plumber, photocopy/DTP, tuition centre, gym) serving a 2-5 km local catchment on cash-and-UPI walk-ins, where the proprietor's own time and a tiny team are the product.

operating_model.summary: A high-frequency, low-ticket, labour-intensive service shop where revenue is a direct function of footfall x conversion x ticket x repeat-rate within a tight geographic catchment. The proprietor is simultaneously owner, master-technician, cashier and marketer; capacity is capped by chair/bay/seat hours and skilled-hands availability. Most demand is walk-in and word-of-mouth, increasingly intermediated by JustDial/Google Maps/UrbanCompany-type aggregators. Cash-and-UPI heavy, thin records, rent + labour are the two dominant costs.
revenue_streams: Core walk-in service fees (haircut/stitching/wash/repair/class) on per-job pricing, ₹50-₹2,000 ticket
Repeat & subscription/package revenue (monthly laundry pack, gym membership, tuition fees, AMC for appliances)
Add-on product retail at point of service (hair products, detergents, spare parts, stationery) at 20-40% attach
Aggregator/platform-routed jobs (UrbanCompany, JustDial leads) and B2B contracts (society AMC, corporate housekeeping)
cost_structure: Skilled & semi-skilled labour wages + incentives (often 30-45% of revenue, frequently informal/cash)
Shop rent + electricity/water + maintenance in the local market (fixed, ₹15k-₹1.5L/month by city tier)
Consumables & spare parts (shampoo, detergent, thread, components) and product COGS
Equipment capex + repairs (chairs, machines, tools, washing/RO units) and aggregator commissions (15-30% on routed jobs)
value_drivers: Proprietor/master craftsman skill & trust — the brand IS the person, drives word-of-mouth
Location & catchment density (footfall, parking, visibility on the high street)
Repeat rate and customer lifetime value vs constant new-customer churn
Speed/turnaround and consistency of quality, which protects pricing power against the shop next door

value_chain: Demand capture (walk-in, signboard, word-of-mouth, Google/JustDial/UrbanCompany lead)
Intake & job ticketing (what service, customer details, expected price/time)

core_processes.description: Capturing customer, service requested, promised price and turnaround time — today mostly verbal/diary-based, the single biggest source of disputes and leakage.
Allocating chairs/bays/technicians/home-visit slots so skilled-hand hours are maximised and walk-ins are not lost to wait times.
Issuing a bill, collecting via UPI/cash/card, and tallying the day's takings against jobs done — where most under-recording and pilferage hides.
Following up, running loyalty/packages and rebooking reminders to convert one-time footfall into recurring revenue.
Reordering shampoo/detergent/thread/components and managing fast-vs-slow movers so jobs are never blocked for want of a ₹50 part.

department_structure.mandate: Deliver the core service at consistent quality and turnaround; this is where 70%+ of headcount and value creation sits.
Greet, book, queue-manage, bill, collect payment and capture customer contact for retention.
Pricing, hiring, vendor negotiation, marketing, compliance, cash management and overall P&L — usually one person wearing all hats.
Source consumables, spare parts and equipment; keep machines and the premises running.
key_roles: Owner or senior staff doubling as buyer

department_structure.mandate: Manage Google/JustDial/UrbanCompany listings, WhatsApp broadcasts, offers, hoardings and local tie-ups to drive footfall.
key_roles: Occasional freelance/agency for social media or pamphlets

operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Revenue drops sharply when the proprietor is sick, travelling or busy; cannot open a second outlet.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Hard cap on capacity and on owner's own income; business is unsellable and non-scalable.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Skill and customer trust concentrated in one person, no documented SOPs, no trained No.2.

operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Daily takings don't reconcile, jobs done off-book, staff pocket small cash jobs.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: 5-15% of true revenue lost; owner cannot see real margins; under-banked so cannot get formal credit.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: No per-job ticketing/billing discipline, heavy cash, no daily reconciliation, mixed personal-business money.

operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Trained stylist/technician leaves (often to start a rival shop nearby) taking customers along.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Sudden capacity loss, customer attrition, constant retraining cost.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Informal employment, no incentive/retention structure, low margins limiting wages, easy local competition.

operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Empty chairs/bays on weekday mornings, long waits and lost walk-ins on weekend evenings.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Low utilisation drags fixed-cost recovery; lost customers during peaks erode word-of-mouth.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: No appointment/queue system, no off-peak pricing, demand not smoothed via bookings or packages.

operational_bottlenecks.symptom: Constantly chasing new walk-ins; no idea who the regulars are or when they last visited.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: High effective CAC, fragile revenue, vulnerability to the next new shop on the street.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: No customer database, no follow-up/loyalty system, contact details never captured at billing.

operational_bottlenecks.symptom: UrbanCompany/JustDial take 15-30% and one bad rating tanks lead flow.
operational_bottlenecks.impact: Margin erosion on platform jobs and loss of pricing control and customer ownership.
operational_bottlenecks.root_cause: Over-reliance on aggregators for demand instead of building owned (Google/WhatsApp) repeat channels.

ai_automation_opportunities.opportunity: WhatsApp-based booking, queue tokens, automated reminders and rebooking nudges to cut idle capacity and lost walk-ins
Digital per-job ticketing + UPI/QR billing with automatic daily cash reconciliation to plug 5-15% revenue leakage
Customer database with last-visit, spend and visit-frequency to trigger loyalty offers and win-back of lapsing regulars
Auto-managed Google Business Profile + review solicitation and reply, and aggregator-listing optimisation to grow owned footfall
Lightweight P&L and GST/turnover tracking from UPI + billing data so the owner sees true margin and stays compliance-ready
Consumable/spare-parts reorder alerts based on consumption so jobs are never blocked and cash isn't tied in dead stock
Documented step-by-step service SOPs + apprentice training checklists to break owner-dependency and standardise quality

consulting_frameworks.use: Compute revenue, contribution and utilisation per chair/bay/technician-hour to find which services and seats actually make money and where to add or cut capacity.
Identify the binding constraint — usually skilled-hand hours or the owner's time — and schedule, price and delegate to relieve it rather than chasing more footfall the shop can't serve.

consulting_frameworks.framework: Customer LTV vs CAC & cohort retention
consulting_frameworks.use: Quantify how much a regular is worth over a year vs the cost of a walk-in or aggregator lead, justifying spend on loyalty and owned channels over commission-heavy platforms.
Understand the real job (convenience, trust, speed, 'looking good for the wedding') to design packages, add-ons and home-visit options that raise ticket size and repeat rate.
Assign who is Responsible/Accountable for intake, delivery, billing and follow-up so the owner can step away and a second outlet becomes possible.
Manage consumables/spares stock and any AMC/credit so cash isn't trapped, keeping the largely cash-positive model from being strangled by dead inventory.

risk_model.risk: Revenue/cash leakage and under-recording leading to untrue books and inability to raise formal credit
risk_model.control: Mandatory per-job digital ticketing + UPI/QR billing, daily reconciliation, separate business bank account

risk_model.risk: GST registration triggered once turnover crosses ₹20L (services) but owner stays informal and unregistered
risk_model.control: Track rolling turnover; register for GST and Udyam on time; issue compliant invoices and file returns

risk_model.risk: Unregistered/non-compliant shop establishment and labour exposure (wages, hours, PF/ESI for staff)
risk_model.control: Obtain Shops & Establishment registration, maintain wage/attendance records, enrol eligible staff in EPF/ESI

risk_model.risk: Key-person dependency — owner or star technician illness/exit collapses revenue or seeds a rival
risk_model.control: Document SOPs, train a No.2, retention incentives, non-solicit understanding, multi-skill the team

risk_model.risk: Statutory dues (PF/ESI/professional tax) and TDS lapses attracting penalties
risk_model.control: Calendarise EPFO/ESIC/professional-tax filings; use payroll tool once staff exceed thresholds

risk_model.risk: Local lease/eviction and pricing-war risk from a new competitor on the same street
risk_model.control: Lock multi-year registered lease, build owned customer database + loyalty to insulate from copycats

risk_model.risk: Aggregator dependence — sudden commission hikes, delisting or rating shocks
risk_model.control: Cap platform share of revenue, harvest customers to owned WhatsApp/Google channels, diversify lead sources

kpi_structure.definition: Billed service-hours divided by available service-hours across seats/technicians
Share of customers who return within 90 days
Total revenue divided by number of jobs/customers served
Total wages + incentives divided by revenue
Difference between expected billings and actual takings banked

kpi_structure.kpi: Cost per acquired customer (owned vs aggregator)
kpi_structure.definition: Marketing + platform commission spend divided by new customers acquired
kpi_structure.healthy: Owned CAC < aggregator CAC and < 1 month's contribution

unit_economics: Salon: avg ticket ₹250-₹600; ~60-65% gross margin after consumables; a chair doing 8-12 jobs/day at ~₹350 = ₹85k-₹1.3L revenue/chair/month
Appliance/AC/RO repair: per-job ₹300-₹1,200 + parts; technician does 6-10 jobs/day; AMC at ₹1,500-₹3,000/year smooths revenue
Laundry/dry-clean: per-piece ₹20-₹150, monthly pack ₹800-₹2,500; consumables+power ~25-30% of revenue
Tuition centre: ₹800-₹3,000/student/month; scalable past ~25 students as teacher cost is largely fixed
profitability_analysis.working_capital_notes: Largely cash/UPI-positive — customers pay at service, so receivables are minimal except B2B/society AMC contracts (DSO 30-60 days). Main working-capital trap is over-stocked consumables/spare parts and equipment EMIs; keep 2-4 weeks of fast-moving consumables only. Rent advance/deposit (3-10 months) is the big one-time cash lock.
levers: Raise utilisation via appointments, off-peak pricing and packages to spread fixed rent + wages
Lift average ticket through product attach, premium service tiers and AMC/subscription bundles
Shift demand from commission-heavy aggregators to owned WhatsApp/Google repeat channels to recover 15-30% margin
Control labour % via incentive-linked pay, multi-skilling and apprenticeship pipeline
Plug leakage with digital billing + daily reconciliation, directly adding 5-15% to recorded revenue

pm_workflows.initiative: Digitise billing, ticketing and daily reconciliation
milestones: Enforce per-job ticket + UPI QR at every transaction
Train staff and run parallel diary+app for 2 weeks
Daily close & reconciliation habit; weekly owner review of true revenue
Capture phone number at every bill (target 80%+ capture)
Segment regulars vs lapsing in a simple CRM/sheet
Launch WhatsApp reminders + a package/loyalty offer
Track 90-day repeat rate monthly and iterate offers

pm_workflows.initiative: Owner-independence via SOPs and a trained No.2
milestones: Document service SOPs and quality checklist
Identify and cross-train a deputy/senior technician
Define RACI for open/close, billing, intake
Trial owner-absent days; measure quality & revenue stability
Optimise Google Business Profile + solicit reviews
Set aggregator revenue cap and harvest customers to owned channel
Local tie-ups (societies, offices, gyms) for B2B/AMC
Track owned vs aggregator CAC and channel mix monthly

key_activities: Lease & fit-out shop in chosen catchment
Equipment purchase, Shops & Establishment + Udyam registration
Hire/skill core team, set service menu & pricing
Consistent delivery to SOP, turnaround control
Quality check, handover and on-the-spot upsell
Digital billing + UPI collection, daily reconciliation
Formalise books, GST/credit readiness, brand build

stages.focus: Stop leakage, see true numbers, secure compliance and basic stability
plays: Switch to digital per-job billing + UPI and daily cash reconciliation
Register Shops & Establishment, Udyam, separate business bank account
Capture customer phone at every bill to start the database
Set a clear service menu and pricing; stop ad-hoc discounting

stages.focus: Raise utilisation, retention and ticket size; reduce owner-dependency
plays: Introduce appointments/WhatsApp booking and off-peak pricing
Launch loyalty/packages/AMC and win-back of lapsing regulars
Document SOPs and train a deputy; incentive-link staff pay
Optimise Google profile and cap aggregator commission share

stages.focus: Replicate the proven unit and build a brand beyond the founder
plays: Open second outlet or home-visit vertical using standardised SOPs
Centralise procurement, books and marketing across outlets
Become GST/credit-ready for working-capital and expansion finance
Explore franchise/partner model and supervisor layer to free the owner

digital_maturity_model.next_step: Use AI insights to standardise, multiply outlets and run a near owner-independent network.
